title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄序
弘治乙卯當天下開科取士
之期巡撫陝西都察院右副
都御史張〔敷華〕巡按陝西監
察御史李〔鉉〕寔奉
命而來宣示
上意以風厲一方士氣丕振維時
===
鎮守陝西太監劉〔瑯〕都督同
知陳〔瑛〕皆愛禮文儒巡撫三
邊右副都御史孫〔仁〕熊〔繡〕左
僉都御史許〔進〕巡按監察御
史張〔泰〕張〔恕〕連〔盛〕郭〔珠〕皆崇
重文教左右布政使陳〔道〕鄭
銘左右參政髙〔弼〕韓〔重〕□〔□〕
banxin: 鄉試錄 前序 一
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄序

弘治乙卯，當天下開科取士之期，巡撫陝西都察院右副都御史張〔敷華〕、巡按陝西監察御史李〔鉉〕，寔奉命而來，宣示上意，以風厲一方，士氣丕振。維時，鎮守陝西太監劉〔瑯〕、都督同知陳〔瑛〕，皆愛禮文儒；巡撫三邊右副都御史孫〔仁〕、熊〔繡〕、左僉都御史許〔進〕、巡按監察御史張〔泰〕、張〔恕〕、連〔盛〕、郭〔珠〕，皆崇重文教。左右布政使陳〔道〕、鄭銘，左右參政髙〔弼〕、韓〔重〕、□〔□〕、
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the yimao year of the Hongzhi reign (1495), when examinations were being held throughout the empire to select men for service, Zhang Fuhua, Governor of Shaanxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, and Li Xuan, Regional Inspector of Shaanxi and Investigating Censor, came in obedience to imperial command. They proclaimed the emperor’s intentions to encourage and exhort the region, greatly invigorating the aspirations of its scholars.

At this time, Liu Lang, the Grand Eunuch stationed in Shaanxi, and Chen Ying, Vice Commissioner-in-Chief, both cherished and treated Confucian scholars with courtesy. Sun Ren and Xiong Xiu, governors of the Three Border Regions and Right Vice Censors-in-Chief; Xu Jin, Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief; and Zhang Tai, Zhang Shu, Lian Sheng, and Guo Zhu, Investigating Censors serving as Regional Inspectors, all held literary learning and moral instruction in high esteem. The Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioners, Chen Dao and Zheng Ming; the Left and Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners, Gao Bi, Han Zhong, and a person whose surname and given name are illegible [?]; …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
左右參議耿〔文〕〔春〕丘〔瑯〕翟〔通〕
李〔濯〕按察使仰〔昇〕副使李〔遜〕
朱〔漢〕李〔隆〕陶〔琰〕李〔旻〕馬〔龍〕韓
〔明〕僉事謝〔顯〕陳〔珍〕張〔貫〕馮〔允〕
〔中〕董〔寧〕潘〔威〕孟〔準〕宋〔禮〕葛〔瑩〕
雖各有司存而作興文事其
志一也至於甄別去取拔其
尤以進于場屋者則提學副
使楊〔一〕〔清〕有專職焉先是御
史瀚以進賢
===
朝廷第一事諜諸藩臬聘四方
儒紳典文柄百凡政務稽按
條格而慎行之又以校文之
室幽隘弗展乃飭所司拓而
banxin: 鄉試錄 前序 二
punctuated:
左右參議耿〔文〕〔春〕、丘〔瑯〕、翟〔通〕、李〔濯〕，按察使仰〔昇〕，副使李〔遜〕、朱〔漢〕、李〔隆〕、陶〔琰〕、李〔旻〕、馬〔龍〕、韓〔明〕，僉事謝〔顯〕、陳〔珍〕、張〔貫〕、馮〔允〕〔中〕、董〔寧〕、潘〔威〕、孟〔準〕、宋〔禮〕、葛〔瑩〕，雖各有司存，而作興文事，其志一也。至於甄別去取，拔其尤以進于場屋者，則提學副使楊〔一〕〔清〕有專職焉。
先是，御史瀚以進賢，朝廷第一事，諜諸藩臬，聘四方儒紳典文柄。百凡政務，稽按條格而慎行之。又以校文之室幽隘弗展，乃飭所司拓而
translation_en:
…The Left and Right Assistant Administration Commissioners were Geng Wenchun, Qiu Lang, Zhai Tong, and Li Zhuo. The Surveillance Commissioner was Yang Sheng. The Vice Surveillance Commissioners were Li Xun, Zhu Han, Li Long, Tao Yan, Li Min, Ma Long, and Han Ming. The Assistant Surveillance Commissioners were Xie Xian, Chen Zhen, Zhang Guan, Feng Yunzhong, Dong Ning, Pan Wei, Meng Zhun, Song Li, and Ge Ying. Although each had his own official responsibilities, they shared a single purpose in promoting literary learning. As for assessing candidates, deciding whom to reject or retain, and selecting the outstanding to advance to the examination halls, this was the particular responsibility of Yang Yiqing, Vice Surveillance Commissioner for Education.
Previously, Censor Han, regarding the recommendation of worthy men as the foremost business of the imperial court, communicated with the provincial administration and surveillance commissions [?] and invited learned gentlemen from all quarters to take charge of evaluating the examination writings. In every administrative matter, he consulted the regulations and proceeded with care. Moreover, finding the rooms for grading papers dark and cramped, with insufficient space, he ordered the responsible officials to enlarge them and…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
新之試期且屆八郡三邊之
士所嘗簡拔於提學者後先
繼至藉數之得千三百人有
奇御史〔瀚文〕仍覆試焉已而
〔原〕等應柄文之聘者偕至御
史例為監臨官提調官則〔道〕
〔重〕領之監試官則〔明顯〕領之
===
考試同考試官則〔文原〕及教
諭〔聰讓拱辰〕訓導〔王瞠一鳳〕
領之與凡為掌卷為受卷為
彌封謄錄對讀官者咸擇其
人以充試期前二日入院顧
天矣辭聞者色動越二十日
撤棘遵
punctuated: 新之。試期且屆，八郡三邊之士，所嘗簡拔於提學者，後先繼至。藉數之，得千三百人有奇。御史〔瀚文〕仍覆試焉。已而，〔原〕等應柄文之聘者偕至。御史例為監臨官，提調官則〔道〕〔重〕領之，監試官則〔明顯〕領之，考試、同考試官則〔文原〕及教諭〔聰讓拱辰〕、訓導〔王瞠一鳳〕領之。與凡為掌卷、為受卷、為彌封、謄錄、對讀官者，咸擇其人以充。試期前二日入院。顧天矣，辭聞者色動。越二十日，撤棘，遵
translation_en:
…and renovated it. As the examination approached, candidates from the eight prefectures and three frontier regions who had previously been selected by the education intendant arrived in succession. A count of the register yielded somewhat more than 1,300 men. The censor or censors named in the annotation as Han and Wen [?] then examined them again. Soon afterward, Yuan and the others who had accepted invitations to preside over the examination arrived together.

By established practice, the censor served as Supervising Official. Dao and Zhong [?] served as Proctors, and Ming and Xian [?] as examination monitors. Wen and Yuan [?], together with the Instructors Cong, Rang, and Gongchen [?] and the Assistant Instructors whose names are transcribed as Wangcheng and Yifeng [?], served as Examiners and Associate Examiners. Suitable men were likewise selected to serve as officials responsible for custody and receipt of examination papers, sealing candidates’ identifying particulars, transcription, and checking the transcripts against the originals by reading them aloud.

They entered the examination compound two days before the examination. They looked toward Heaven [?]; those who heard the words changed countenance [?]. Twenty days later, the thorn enclosure was removed, and, in accordance with …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
制額棭士六十有五人故事試
畢必錄其所取士姓名以
獻而及其百執事者紀所嘗與
力也及其文之合程度者示
士子知所嚮方也必有序者
言錄之所為作也於是〔文原〕
當序諸首簡慨惟古帝王設
為庠序學校以居天下之學
者化理之隆率於是焉致我
國家兩畿十三省荒陬絶徼莫
不有學田野戎伍閒有佳子
弟皆得籍名於學三代而降
未有若是其盛者養之也無
遺法矣取士之制虞夏敷納
banxin: 鄉試錄 前序 四
punctuated:
制額棭士六十有五人。故事，試畢，必錄其所取士姓名以獻，而及其百執事者，紀所嘗與力也；及其文之合程度者，示士子知所嚮方也。必有序者，言錄之所為作也。於是〔文原〕當序諸首簡。
慨惟古帝王設為庠序學校，以居天下之學者，化理之隆，率於是焉致。我國家兩畿十三省，荒陬絶徼，莫不有學。田野戎伍閒有佳子弟，皆得籍名於學。三代而降，未有若是其盛者，養之也無遺法矣。取士之制，虞夏敷納
translation_en:
… under the prescribed quota, sixty-five men were selected [?]. By established practice, once the examination is concluded, the names of the successful candidates must be recorded for presentation to the throne. The various officials who served are also included, to record their contributions; compositions that meet the prescribed standards are included to show candidates the direction they should follow. A preface is required to explain why the record was compiled. Thus I, 〔Wenyuan〕, am charged with writing the preface on its opening leaves.
I reflect with deep feeling that the ancient emperors and kings established schools of various kinds to accommodate the scholars of the realm. The flourishing of moral transformation and good government generally arose from these institutions. In our dynasty’s two metropolitan regions and thirteen provinces, even remote corners and distant frontiers have schools. Promising young men from farming communities and military ranks can all enroll in them. Since the Three Dynasties, there has never been such flourishing provision: no means of nurturing talent has been omitted. As for the system of selecting men for office, under Yu and Xia there was the broad solicitation and reception of counsel …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
商無方周賓興之典大備自
漢以來則有科歷晉隋唐宋
其為科代各不同我
太祖高皇帝起而兼采之著為令
百三十年莫之有改取之也
無遺術矣小大之臣祗承法
令慎關防嚴條貫嚴事庀物
===
科增嚴加行之也無遺力矣
比占仕籍自
朝著藩臬下逮郡若邑政教長
貳惟科目是崇他途幾廢即
有之不倚以為重是其用之
也又可謂無遺愛矣然則士
之所以圖報於後來者智所
banxin: 鄉試録 前序 五
punctuated:
商無方，周賓興之典大備。自漢以來則有科，歷晉隋唐宋，其為科代各不同。我太祖高皇帝起而兼采之，著為令，百三十年莫之有改，取之也無遺術矣。小大之臣祗承法令，慎關防，嚴條貫，嚴事庀物，科增嚴加，行之也無遺力矣。
比占仕籍，自朝著藩臬，下逮郡若邑政教長貳，惟科目是崇，他途幾廢。即有之，不倚以為重，是其用之也又可謂無遺愛矣。然則士之所以圖報於後來者，智所
translation_en:
…under the Shang, selection was unrestricted; under the Zhou, the institutions for honoring and recommending worthy men were fully developed. From the Han onward there were categories of recruitment. Through the Jin, Sui, Tang, and Song, these differed from dynasty to dynasty. Our Emperor Taizu Gao arose and drew upon them all, establishing them as ordinances. For one hundred and thirty years, no one has altered them: no means of selecting men of talent has been left unprovided. Officials great and small reverently uphold the laws and ordinances, carefully maintain safeguards, strictly enforce regulations, diligently attend to affairs and prepare supplies, and impose increasingly stringent requirements [?]. In carrying these arrangements out, they spare no effort.
Of late, among those entered on the official rolls—from officials at court and in the provincial administration and surveillance commissions down to the principal and deputy officials responsible for government and education in prefectures and counties—only recruitment through the examinations is esteemed. Other avenues have nearly fallen into disuse. Even where they remain, they are not relied upon or accorded importance. In employing these scholars, too, it may be said that no favor has been withheld. Thus, as for how scholars should seek to repay this favor in their subsequent careers, what their understanding…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不及力所不逮位所不與則
亦已矣智及而有遺謀力逮
而有遺才與其位而有遺政
則亦奚以自諉哉昔人論漢
之治者謂孝武好儒術而其
效顧出於文景崇尚黄老著
之下遂以爲儒術不足貴也
===
又孰知孝武所好非真儒而
公孫弘輩曲學阿世尚奚足
名儒乎哉今日
朝廷之所養所取與士子之所
應非帝王之道不陳非孔孟
程朱之學不講固已陋孝武
公孫弘於不足齒矣其進而
punctuated:
不及，力所不逮，位所不與，則亦已矣。智及而有遺謀，力逮而有遺才，與其位而有遺政，則亦奚以自諉哉？昔人論漢之治者，謂孝武好儒術，而其效顧出於文景崇尚黄老著之下，遂以爲儒術不足貴也。又孰知孝武所好非真儒，而公孫弘輩曲學阿世，尚奚足名儒乎哉？
今日朝廷之所養所取，與士子之所應，非帝王之道不陳，非孔孟程朱之學不講，固已陋孝武、公孫弘於不足齒矣。其進而
translation_en:
…does not extend, where their strength falls short, or where their position affords no authority, then the matter must rest. But if their understanding is sufficient yet plans remain unoffered, their strength is adequate yet abilities remain unused, or they hold the requisite position yet administrative duties remain neglected, what excuse can they make for themselves? Those in former times who discussed the government of the Han said that Emperor Xiaowu favored Confucian learning, yet his achievements fell below those of Emperors Wen and Jing, who honored the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi [?]. They thus concluded that Confucian learning was not worthy of esteem. Yet who recognized that those whom Xiaowu favored were not true Confucians? Men such as Gongsun Hong distorted learning to curry favor with their age: how could they deserve the name of Confucians?
Today, in the court’s cultivation and selection of scholars and in the candidates’ responses, nothing is set forth but the Way of the sage emperors and kings, and nothing is expounded but the learning of Confucius, Mencius, the Cheng brothers, and Zhu Xi. This has already rendered Xiaowu and Gongsun Hong so contemptible as to be unworthy of mention. When these scholars advance and…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
措之於用乃使後世復有儒
術不足貴之譏以遺羞於學
校遺玷於科目其可乎是則
有司者之所大懼也夫自鄉
試有司者之所大懼也夫自鄉
試有錄孰不以辭勵士要所
聽受或不盡然且豪傑之士
固有不待夫人者矣窮年之
===
所養一朝之所拔顧不以豪
傑自待又并人言莫之省也
此真何如人何如心哉〔之 爲〕
濫從主司後亦承久養精取
之餘者感
朝廷待士之盛而懼士之報有
弗稱故即其所激者爲諸士
banxin: 鄉試錄 前序 七
punctuated: 措之於用，乃使後世復有儒術不足貴之譏，以遺羞於學校，遺玷於科目，其可乎？是則有司者之所大懼也。夫自鄉試，有司者之所大懼也。夫自鄉試有錄，孰不以辭勵士？要所聽受，或不盡然。且豪傑之士，固有不待夫人者矣。窮年之所養，一朝之所拔，顧不以豪傑自待，又并人言莫之省也，此真何如人、何如心哉？〔之 爲〕濫從主司後，亦承久養精取之餘者，感朝廷待士之盛，而懼士之報有弗稱，故即其所激者爲諸士
translation_en:
…when they advance to put their learning into practice, could they then allow later generations once again to deride Confucian learning as unworthy of esteem, bringing shame upon the schools and dishonor upon the examination system? This is what the responsible officials greatly fear. Now, since the Provincial Examination—what the responsible officials greatly fear [?; the transcription repeats part of the preceding passage]. Ever since Provincial Examinations have had records, who has failed to encourage scholars through his words? Yet those who hear and receive these words may not fully heed them. Moreover, outstanding scholars surely include those who do not wait for others to stir them to action. Nurtured over many years and selected on a single occasion, if they nevertheless do not hold themselves to the standard of outstanding men, and fail even to reflect upon others’ words, what sort of people, with what sort of minds, can they truly be?

〔之 爲: unclear annotation〕 Having unworthily taken my place after the chief examiners, I too have benefited from this long cultivation and careful selection. I am moved by the court’s munificence toward scholars, yet fear that their repayment may fall short. Thus, prompted by these feelings, I address the scholars…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
子告嗚呼柳齋可謂無遺言
哉
江西南康府都昌縣儒學教
諭孫〔文 原〕謹序
banxin: 鄉試錄 前序 八
punctuated:
子告。嗚呼！柳齋可謂無遺言哉！
江西南康府都昌縣儒學教諭孫〔文 原〕謹序。
translation_en:
…to address the scholars. Ah! Liuzhai may indeed be said to have left nothing unsaid!
Respectfully composed as a preface by Sun Wenyuan 孫文原, Instructor of the Confucian School of Duchang County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
弘治八年陝西鄉試
監臨官
巡按陝西監察御史李瀚〔叔淵山西沁水縣人 辛丑進士〕
提調官
陝西等處承宣布政使司左布政使陳道〔德脩直隸盱眙縣人 甲申進士〕
陝西等處承宣布政使司右參政韓重〔淳夫山西絳州人 戊戌進士〕
監試官
陝西等處提刑按察司副使韓明〔惟遠浙江餘姚縣人 乙未進士〕
陝西等處提刑按察司僉事謝顯〔時榮浙江會稽縣人 己丑進士〕
===
考試官
江西南康府都昌縣儒學教諭孫文原〔宗道浙江慈谿縣人 己酉貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府鳳陽縣儒學教諭羅聰〔廷蔭浙江桐廬縣人 丁酉貢士〕
同考試官
河南河南府陝州閿鄉縣儒學教諭焦讓〔允恭直隸東鹿縣人 己酉貢士〕
直隸廣平府鷄澤縣儒學教諭郭拱辰〔敬之山西高平縣人 己酉貢士〕
山西澤州陽城縣儒學訓導姚玉〔德美直隸德州衛人 庚子貢士〕
直隸保定府祁州深澤縣儒學訓導黃暟〔明遠雲南臨安衛人 庚子貢士〕
浙江嚴州府桐廬縣儒學訓導談一鳳〔文瑞直隸無錫縣人 壬子貢士〕
punctuated:
弘治八年陝西鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按陝西監察御史李瀚〔叔淵，山西沁水縣人，辛丑進士〕。

提調官：
陝西等處承宣布政使司左布政使陳道〔德脩，直隸盱眙縣人，甲申進士〕。
陝西等處承宣布政使司右參政韓重〔淳夫，山西絳州人，戊戌進士〕。

監試官：
陝西等處提刑按察司副使韓明〔惟遠，浙江餘姚縣人，乙未進士〕。
陝西等處提刑按察司僉事謝顯〔時榮，浙江會稽縣人，己丑進士〕。

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
行夏之時乘殷之輅服周之冕樂則韶舞
唯天下至誠為能經綸天下之大經立天
下之大本知天地之化育夫焉有所
倚肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天苟
不固聰明聖知達天德者其孰能知
之
人有雞犬放則知求之有放心而不知求
學問之道無他求其放心而已矣
===
易
得尚于中行
君子以言有物而行有恒
是故蓍之德圓而神卦之德方以知六爻
之義易以貢聖人以此洗心退藏於
密吉凶與民同患神以知來知以藏
往其孰能與於此哉古之聰明叡知
神武而不殺者夫是以明於天之道
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

行夏之時，乘殷之輅，服周之冕，樂則韶舞。

唯天下至誠，為能經綸天下之大經，立天下之大本，知天地之化育。夫焉有所倚？肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。苟不固聰明聖知、達天德者，其孰能知之？

人有雞犬放，則知求之；有放心，而不知求。學問之道無他，求其放心而已矣。

易

得尚于中行。

君子以言有物而行有恒。

是故蓍之德圓而神，卦之德方以知，六爻之義易以貢。聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往，其孰能與於此哉？古之聰明叡知、神武而不殺者夫！是以明於天之道
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Follow the calendar of Xia, ride in the carriage of Yin, and wear the ceremonial cap of Zhou; for music, use the Shao dance.

Only one possessed of the utmost sincerity under Heaven can order the great enduring relationships of the world, establish its great foundation, and understand the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth. On what could such a person depend? How earnest his benevolence, how deep his profundity, how vast his Heaven-like greatness! Unless someone is truly perceptive, sagely, and wise, comprehending Heaven’s virtue, who could understand him?

When people’s chickens or dogs stray, they know to seek them; when their hearts stray, they do not know to seek them. The way of learning is nothing other than seeking one’s strayed heart.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

One obtains esteem by following the middle course.

The gentleman ensures that his words have substance and his conduct has constancy.

Thus the virtue of the milfoil stalks is round and numinous; the virtue of the hexagrams is square and wise; and the meaning of the six lines is changing, thereby presenting itself. With these, the sage cleanses his heart and withdraws into secrecy, sharing the people’s concern over good and ill fortune. Through numinous insight he knows what is to come; through wisdom he stores what has passed. Who could participate in this? Surely those of antiquity who were perceptive and sagacious, numinously martial yet did not kill! Thus they understood the Way of Heaven …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而察於民之故是興神物以前民用
聖人以此齋戒以神明其德夫
功業見乎變
書
輯五瑞既月乃日覲四岳羣牧班瑞于羣
后
終始惟一時乃日新任官惟賢才左右惟
其人臣為上為德為下為民其難其
愼惟和惟一德無常師主善為師善
===
無常主協于克一俾萬姓咸曰大哉
王言又曰一哉王心克綏先王之祿
永底烝民之生
乃有室大競籲俊尊上帝
用賚爾秬鬯一卣彤弓一彤矢百盧弓一
盧矢百馬四匹
詩
知子之來之雜佩以贈之知子之順之雜
佩以問之知子之好之雜佩以報之
punctuated:
而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。聖人以此齋戒，以神明其德夫！
功業見乎變。

書
輯五瑞，既月乃日，覲四岳羣牧，班瑞于羣后。
終始惟一，時乃日新。任官惟賢才，左右惟其人。臣為上為德，為下為民。其難其愼，惟和惟一。德無常師，主善為師；善無常主，協于克一。俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉，王言！」又曰：「一哉，王心！」克綏先王之祿，永底烝民之生。
乃有室大競，籲俊尊上帝。
用賚爾秬鬯一卣，彤弓一，彤矢百，盧弓一，盧矢百，馬四匹。

詩
知子之來之，雜佩以贈之；知子之順之，雜佩以問之；知子之好之，雜佩以報之。
translation_en:
…and discerned the circumstances of the people, they therefore brought forth the divine objects to guide the people in their use. Through these, the sages purified themselves and observed abstinence, making their virtue spiritually luminous!
Achievements manifest themselves through change.

Book of Documents
He gathered the five kinds of jade credentials. When the month had been determined, he fixed the day, received in audience the chiefs of the Four Mountains and the regional governors, and distributed the jade credentials to the various lords.
Be consistent from beginning to end: thus you will daily renew yourself. Appoint to office only the worthy and talented; place only suitable men at your side. A minister serves his ruler above by cultivating virtue and those below by serving the people. Treat this task as difficult and approach it cautiously; maintain harmony and unity. In cultivating virtue, there is no fixed teacher: take goodness as your teacher. Goodness has no fixed embodiment: it accords with constancy of purpose. Let all the people say, “Great are the king’s words!” and also, “Single is the king’s purpose!” Thus you can preserve the blessings of the former kings and secure the people’s livelihood forever.
Then the royal house greatly flourished, calling forth men of outstanding ability to honor the Lord on High.
I therefore bestow upon you one vessel of fragrant black-millet sacrificial wine, one red bow, one hundred red arrows, one black bow, one hundred black arrows, and four horses.

Book of Odes
Knowing that you will come to me, I give you assorted girdle pendants. Knowing that you regard me favorably, I offer you assorted girdle pendants as a greeting. Knowing that you love me, I give you assorted girdle pendants in return.

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其車三千師干之試
經營四方告成于王四方旣平王國庶定
時靡有爭王心載寧江漢之滸王命
召虎式辟四方徹我疆土匪疚匪棘
王國來極于疆于理至于南海王命
召虎來旬來宣文武受命召公維翰
無曰予小子召公是似肇敏戎公用
錫爾祉釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣告于文
人錫山土田于周受命自召祖命
===
昊天有成命二后受之成王不敢康夙夜
基命宥密於緝熙單厥心肆其靖之
春秋
公及邾儀父盟于蔑〔隱公元年〕及宋人盟于
宿〔隱公元年〕鄭人來輸平〔隱公六年〕公伐
邾〔隱公七年〕庚午宋公齊侯衛侯盟于
瓦屋〔隱公八年〕齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲〔桓〕
〔公三年〕會于蕭魚〔襄公十一年〕
遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕公至自伐楚公會齊侯
punctuated:
其車三千，師干之試。
經營四方，告成于王。四方旣平，王國庶定。時靡有爭，王心載寧。江漢之滸，王命召虎：式辟四方，徹我疆土。匪疚匪棘，王國來極。于疆于理，至于南海。王命召虎：來旬來宣。文武受命，召公維翰。無曰予小子，召公是似。肇敏戎公，用錫爾祉。釐爾圭瓚，秬鬯一卣，告于文人。錫山土田，于周受命，自召祖命。
昊天有成命，二后受之。成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。於緝熙，單厥心，肆其靖之。
春秋
公及邾儀父盟于蔑〔隱公元年〕。及宋人盟于宿〔隱公元年〕。鄭人來輸平〔隱公六年〕。公伐邾〔隱公七年〕。庚午，宋公、齊侯、衛侯盟于瓦屋〔隱公八年〕。齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲〔桓〕〔公三年〕。會于蕭魚〔襄公十一年〕。
遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕。公至自伐楚。公會齊侯
translation_en:
…His chariots numbered three thousand; his hosts and shields were put to use.

He campaigned throughout the four quarters and reported his success to the king. The four quarters were now pacified, and the royal realm was nearly settled. There was no longer any strife, and the king’s heart was at peace. On the banks of the Jiang and Han rivers, the king commanded Shao Hu: “Open up the four quarters and establish the boundaries of our territory. Neither distress the people nor act with undue haste; let the royal realm be their centre. Mark out the boundaries and order the lands, reaching to the southern sea.” The king commanded Shao Hu: “Go forth to inspect and proclaim my commands. Wen and Wu received the Mandate, and the Duke of Shao was their mainstay. Do not say, ‘I am but a young man’; emulate the Duke of Shao. Begin diligently upon your great service, and I shall bestow blessings upon you. I grant you a jade-handled libation ladle and a vessel of black-millet sacrificial wine: announce these to your illustrious ancestor. I grant you mountains, lands, and fields. Receive your charge at Zhou, following the charge given to your ancestor of Shao.”

August Heaven had a settled Mandate, which the two sovereigns received. King Cheng dared not take his ease; day and night he established the Mandate with broad and quiet deliberation. Ah, continuing in brightness, he devoted his whole heart, and thus brought peace.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The duke and Yifu of Zhu made a covenant at Mie. 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕 A covenant was made with men of Song at Su. 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕 Men of Zheng came to offer peace. 〔Sixth year of Duke Yin.〕 The duke attacked Zhu. 〔Seventh year of Duke Yin.〕 On the gengwu day, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Qi, and the Marquis of Wei made a covenant at Wawu. 〔Eighth year of Duke Yin.〕 The Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu. 〔Third year of Duke Huan.〕 A meeting was held at Xiaoyu. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕

They then attacked Chu. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 The duke returned from the campaign against Chu. The duke met with the Marquis of Qi …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯伐鄭圍新城
楚人圍許諸侯遂救許公至自伐鄭〔僖公六年〕
公如京師　公自京師遂會
晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯邾人
滕人伐秦　公至自伐秦〔成公十三年〕
天王狩于河陽〔僖公二十八年〕
遂伐楚　楚屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕　公會
齊侯于夾谷齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田
〔定公十年〕
===
禮記
天子祭天下名山大川
春誦夏弦大師詔之瞽宗秋學禮執禮者
詔之冬讀書典書者詔之禮在瞽宗
書在上庠
五者天下之大教也
凡人之所以為人者禮義也禮義之始在
於正容體齊顏色順辭令容體正顏
色齊辭令順而後禮義備以正君臣
punctuated:
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。楚人圍許，諸侯遂救許。公至自伐鄭。〔僖公六年〕
公如京師。公自京師遂會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人、滕人伐秦。公至自伐秦。〔成公十三年〕
天王狩于河陽。〔僖公二十八年〕
遂伐楚。楚屈完來盟于師。〔僖公四年〕公會齊侯于夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔定公十年〕
禮記
天子祭天下名山大川。
春誦夏弦，大師詔之瞽宗；秋學禮，執禮者詔之；冬讀書，典書者詔之。禮在瞽宗，書在上庠。
五者，天下之大教也。
凡人之所以為人者，禮義也。禮義之始，在於正容體、齊顏色、順辭令。容體正，顏色齊，辭令順，而後禮義備，以正君臣
translation_en:
…the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao attacked Zheng and besieged Xincheng. The men of Chu besieged Xu; the assembled lords then went to Xu’s rescue. The duke returned from the campaign against Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Xi〕
The duke went to the royal capital. From the royal capital, the duke then joined the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and men of Zhu and Teng in attacking Qin. The duke returned from the campaign against Qin. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Cheng〕
The Heavenly King hunted at Heyang. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi〕
They then attacked Chu. Qu Wan of Chu came to conclude a covenant at the army’s camp. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi〕 The duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. Men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕
Book of Rites
The Son of Heaven offers sacrifices to the renowned mountains and great rivers of all under Heaven.
In spring, students recite; in summer, they perform to string accompaniment. The Grand Music Master instructs them in the School of the Blind Musicians. In autumn, they study ritual, and those responsible for ritual instruct them. In winter, they read texts, and those responsible for texts instruct them. Ritual is taught in the School of the Blind Musicians; texts are taught in the Upper School.
These five are the great teachings for all under Heaven.
What makes human beings human is ritual and righteousness. Ritual and righteousness begin with making one’s bearing upright, one’s countenance composed, and one’s speech appropriate. Only after one’s bearing is upright, one’s countenance composed, and one’s speech appropriate are ritual and righteousness complete, thereby setting right the relationship between ruler and minister…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
親父子和長幼君臣正父子親長幼
和而后禮義立
第貳場
論
王者無外
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
擬唐以同州刺史姚元之為兵部尚書同
中書門下三品誥〔太極元年〕
===
擬宋以趙抃為殿中侍御史謝表〔至和二年〕
判語〔五條〕
漏使印信
賦役不均
私借官物
服舍違式
關津留難
第叄場
策五道
punctuated:
親父子，和長幼。君臣正，父子親，長幼和，而后禮義立。

第貳場
論：王者無外。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕：擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕；擬唐以同州刺史姚元之為兵部尚書、同中書門下三品誥〔太極元年〕；擬宋以趙抃為殿中侍御史謝表〔至和二年〕。
判語〔五條〕：漏使印信；賦役不均；私借官物；服舍違式；關津留難。

第叄場
策五道。
translation_en:
…to foster affection between fathers and sons and harmony between elders and juniors. When rulers and ministers stand in their proper relations, fathers and sons are affectionate, and elders and juniors are harmonious, then ritual propriety and righteousness are established.

Second Session
Discourse: “For the true king, nothing lies outside his realm.”
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials [one topic from among these [?]]:
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor granting the people remission of half of this year’s land tax [second year of Emperor Wen’s reign].
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Yao Yuanzhi, Prefect of Tongzhou, as Minister of War and concurrently as an official with the standing of the third-ranking officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery [first year of Taiji].
Compose a Song memorial of thanks for Zhao Bian’s appointment as Palace Censor [second year of Zhihe].
Legal judgments [five cases]: Failure to use official seals [?]; unequal assessment of taxes and labor services; unauthorized borrowing of government property; clothing and dwellings that violate prescribed regulations; obstruction and delay at checkpoints and ferries.

Third Session
Five policy questions.

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
問自古帝王之創造天下必制禮明刑以
新天下之耳目唐虞三代載諸經秦漢
而下備諸史其所因所革或寬或猛槩
可見矣漢高帝以甕秦之功開炎劉之
運當時非不急於禮也若祠祭一詔則
蹈襲如故其後雖有叔孫綿蕞之制亦
未之變非不究於刑也若入關一諭乃
反苛以寬其後遂使官吏論決之獄亦
不之報史稱高祖寛仁大度又曰以馬
上得天下良謂此也故嘗以是驗諸
當代竊有疑焉我
太祖高皇帝垂統貽則明明有訓定鼎之初嘗
合祭
天地矣而其
制文有曰南北之壇終不會祀於禮未然是蓋
裁自
聖心以義而起至於他所刊定一刻有元之陋
無少襲也即位之久嘗肆
punctuated: 問：自古帝王之創造天下，必制禮明刑，以新天下之耳目。唐虞三代載諸經，秦漢而下備諸史，其所因所革，或寬或猛，槩可見矣。漢高帝以甕秦之功，開炎劉之運。當時非不急於禮也，若祠祭一詔，則蹈襲如故；其後雖有叔孫綿蕞之制，亦未之變。非不究於刑也，若入關一諭，乃反苛以寬；其後遂使官吏論決之獄，亦不之報。史稱高祖寛仁大度，又曰以馬上得天下，良謂此也。故嘗以是驗諸當代，竊有疑焉。我太祖高皇帝垂統貽則，明明有訓。定鼎之初，嘗合祭天地矣，而其制文有曰：「南北之壇，終不會祀，於禮未然。」是蓋裁自聖心，以義而起。至於他所刊定，一刻有元之陋，無少襲也。即位之久，嘗肆
translation_en:
Question: Since antiquity, whenever emperors and kings founded their rule over the realm, they necessarily established rites and clarified punishments, thereby renewing what the people of the realm saw and heard. The affairs of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties are recorded in the Classics; those from the Qin and Han onward are fully documented in the histories. What they retained and what they changed, whether lenient or stern, can generally be discerned.

Emperor Gao of Han, through his achievement in overthrowing Qin [?], inaugurated the reign of the Liu house under the virtue of Fire. At the time, he certainly treated ritual as an urgent concern. Yet his edict on sacrifices followed established practice unchanged; even the later ceremonial arrangements devised by Shusun using bundles of reeds as markers did not alter it. Nor did he neglect to examine penal matters. His proclamation upon entering the passes replaced harshness with leniency; subsequently, cases adjudicated by officials were not even reported for imperial confirmation. The histories describe Gaozu as lenient, benevolent, and magnanimous, and also say that he won the realm on horseback. Surely this is what they mean.

I have therefore tried to test these precedents against our own dynasty, and privately find something puzzling. Our Emperor Taizu Gao bequeathed the succession and handed down standards, leaving teachings of manifest clarity. At the beginning of his founding of the dynasty, he offered joint sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. His decree stated: “At the northern and southern altars, they are never worshipped together; this is not proper according to ritual.” This decision surely arose from his sagely judgment and was instituted in accordance with righteousness. In his other revisions and determinations, he entirely eliminated [?] the defective practices of the Yuan, retaining not the slightest trace of them. Long after ascending the throne, he once extended …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
有臣民矣而其
聖詔有曰詿誤盡赦若果真犯雖笞不原是蓋
用其義殺以威而治至於他所刑戮一
反有元之縱無少假也由是薄海內外
仰
日月之麗天拱
雷霆之在上百年之腥穢一旦去而為衣冠
文物之世矣說者謂漢高帝之起沛中
我
===
太祖之龍飛淮甸其開基創業大略可擬矣然
而因革寬猛之間相去甚遠有如此者
蓋
天縱聖神宏謀淵筭度越千古其所以挾時乘
遠雖三代以來亦不可誣也爾諸士子
頌
用夏變夷之
駿功講
天冠地履之嚴分非一日矣其敬述以對以
punctuated: 有臣民矣，而其聖詔有曰：「詿誤盡赦，若果真犯，雖笞不原。」是蓋用其義殺，以威而治。至於他所刑戮，一反有元之縱，無少假也。由是薄海內外，仰日月之麗天，拱雷霆之在上，百年之腥穢，一旦去而為衣冠文物之世矣。說者謂漢高帝之起沛中，我太祖之龍飛淮甸，其開基創業，大略可擬矣。然而因革寬猛之間，相去甚遠，有如此者。蓋天縱聖神，宏謀淵筭，度越千古，其所以挾時乘遠，雖三代以來，亦不可誣也。爾諸士子，頌用夏變夷之駿功，講天冠地履之嚴分，非一日矣。其敬述以對，以
translation_en:
…[extended clemency to?] his officials and people. Yet his sacred edict stated: “Pardon entirely those drawn into wrongdoing through error; but if they truly committed an offense, do not pardon it, even if punishable only by beating with the light stick.” This was to employ righteous execution and govern through awe. In his other punishments and executions, he completely reversed the laxity of the Yuan, allowing not the slightest indulgence. Thus, throughout the lands within and beyond the seas, people looked up to him as to the sun and moon shining in heaven, and stood with hands respectfully clasped before him as before thunder overhead. A century’s foul pollution was swept away in a single day, bringing an age of civilized dress, institutions, and culture.

Commentators say that Emperor Gao of the Han rose in Pei, while our Taizu rose like a dragon in the Huai region; in founding their dynasties and establishing their enterprises, their broad outlines may be compared. Yet in what they retained or changed, and in their leniency or severity, the differences were as great as these. Heaven endowed our Taizu with sagely and divine qualities; his grand plans and profound calculations surpassed all antiquity. His ability to seize the times and “ride the distant” [?] cannot be denied, even when compared with rulers since the Three Dynasties.

You examination candidates have long praised his magnificent achievement in transforming the barbarians through Chinese civilization, and have discussed the strict distinction between the positions of heaven above and earth below. Respectfully set this forth in your replies, so as to…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
觀
億萬年太平之盛
問王祀夫子而以名賢大儒為之配盖所
以崇德報功古今之禮莫大於此請以
所疑與諸士子論之四配十哲之議定
於何時東廡西廡之數椽夫何代以顏
孫補十哲固也然則言行氣象彷彿聖
人者不及乎以名教出揚雄是也然則
以性為惡以禮為偽者猶賢乎以二十
===
二人並為先師以六十七人並為列伯
皆盛舉也而今則有因有革矣石室所
載七十二賢宋祀因之通典所載八十
三賢唐祀因之而今則增至百有餘人
矣自漢而上有為季孫之愬者有宗莊
老之學者或建議短喪或黨附勢穿皆
得與俎豆之列何若是其易由宋而下
有文章節義名配昌黎者有忠孝大節
為第一等人物者乃自許吳之外有清
punctuated:
觀億萬年太平之盛。
問：王祀夫子，而以名賢大儒為之配，盖所以崇德報功，古今之禮莫大於此。請以所疑與諸士子論之。四配十哲之議定於何時？東廡西廡之數椽，夫何代？以顏孫補十哲，固也；然則言行氣象彷彿聖人者不及乎？以名教出揚雄，是也；然則以性為惡、以禮為偽者猶賢乎？以二十二人並為先師，以六十七人並為列伯，皆盛舉也，而今則有因有革矣。石室所載七十二賢，宋祀因之；通典所載八十三賢，唐祀因之；而今則增至百有餘人矣。自漢而上，有為季孫之愬者，有宗莊老之學者，或建議短喪，或黨附勢穿，皆得與俎豆之列，何若是其易？由宋而下，有文章節義名配昌黎者，有忠孝大節為第一等人物者，乃自許吳之外，有清
translation_en:
…to behold the flourishing of Great Peace for countless millions of years.
Question: The sovereign offers sacrifices to the Master, with renowned worthies and great Confucian scholars accompanying him in worship. This honors virtue and requites meritorious service; among the rites of antiquity and the present, none is greater. Let me discuss the points in doubt with you examination candidates. When was the arrangement of the Four Associates and Ten Philosophers settled? In what dynasty were the several rafters of the eastern and western side halls established [?]? It was certainly proper to add Yan and Sun [?] to the Ten Philosophers; but was the man whose words, deeds, and bearing resembled those of the Sage not their equal? It was right to exclude Yang Xiong on grounds of moral orthodoxy; but was the man who held human nature to be evil and ritual to be artificial still worthy? To designate twenty-two men alike as Former Masters, and sixty-seven alike as earls, were both grand undertakings. Yet today some provisions have been retained and others altered. The sacrifices of the Song followed the list of seventy-two worthies recorded in the Stone Chamber; those of the Tang followed the eighty-three worthies recorded in the Comprehensive Institutions (Tongdian). Today, however, the number has risen to over a hundred.
From the Han back into antiquity, there were men who made accusations to Jisun [?], and men who followed the teachings of Zhuangzi and Laozi. Some proposed shortening the mourning period; others attached themselves to powerful factions [?]. All were admitted to the ranks receiving sacrificial offerings. Why was admission so easy? From the Song onward, there were men whose literary achievement, integrity, and righteousness earned them reputations equal to Changli [Han Yu], and men whose outstanding loyalty and filial devotion placed them in the foremost rank of human beings. Moreover, beyond Xu and Wu, there are men of pure …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
修高節之徵士欲列之而不果我
國家百年以來有文學直躬之名臣嘗議及
而報罷何若是其難或謂通天下配祀
者惟顔曾思孟餘雖七十二子止當於
國學及其鄉祀之其說然歟或謂子雖
齊聖不先父食而顔曾子思偃然其父
之上爲非宜者其論當歟夫議禮
朝廷事也而參考折衷不能不資天下之公
論不知今日
===
定制之外因革損益誠有可議者乎請遂言
之勿讓
問御史古官也在成周時猶記事之任爾
歷秦至漢始以圖書兼彈劾之事自是
以至魏晉則專以糾察爲職焉唐自彈
糾之外得兼獄訟之事宋自彈劾之外
得兼諫諍之職由是觀之莫加備者唐
貞元以後制也而或者以爲未若任兼
諫諍者之爲善豈前此皆略至是而始
punctuated:
修高節之徵士，欲列之而不果。我國家百年以來，有文學直躬之名臣，嘗議及而報罷，何若是其難？或謂通天下配祀者惟顔、曾、思、孟，餘雖七十二子，止當於國學及其鄉祀之，其說然歟？或謂子雖齊聖，不先父食，而顔、曾、子思偃然其父之上，爲非宜者，其論當歟？夫議禮，朝廷事也，而參考折衷，不能不資天下之公論。不知今日定制之外，因革損益，誠有可議者乎？請遂言之，勿讓。

問：御史，古官也。在成周時，猶記事之任爾。歷秦至漢，始以圖書兼彈劾之事，自是以至魏晉，則專以糾察爲職焉。唐自彈糾之外，得兼獄訟之事；宋自彈劾之外，得兼諫諍之職。由是觀之，莫加備者，唐貞元以後制也。而或者以爲未若任兼諫諍者之爲善，豈前此皆略，至是而始
translation_en:
…a scholar of pure conduct and lofty integrity, summoned to office: there was a desire to include him among those receiving sacrifices, but it came to nothing. In the century and more since our dynasty’s founding, there have been eminent ministers distinguished for literary learning and upright conduct. Their inclusion was once proposed, but the proposal was rejected. Why should it be so difficult? Some say that only Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, Zisi, and Mengzi should receive accompanying sacrifices throughout the realm; the others, even the seventy-two disciples, should receive sacrifices only at the Directorate of Education and in their native places. Is this view correct? Others say that even a son who equals a sage must not partake of offerings before his father, and that it is improper for Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, and Zisi to occupy places of honor above their fathers. Is this argument sound? Deliberation on ritual is the court’s responsibility, yet comparison of precedents and determination of the proper course cannot dispense with the considered opinion of the realm. Beyond today’s established regulations, are there indeed matters of retention or reform, diminution or addition, that merit discussion? Please state your views fully, without reserve.

Question: The Censor is an ancient office. In the Zhou period, its responsibility was still merely to record events. Through the Qin and into the Han, responsibility for documents and records first came to be combined with impeachment. From then through the Wei and Jin, investigating and censuring misconduct became its exclusive duty. Under the Tang, beyond impeachment and censure, Censors could also handle criminal cases and litigation; under the Song, beyond impeachment, they could also undertake remonstrance. Viewed in this light, no arrangement was more comprehensive than the system in effect after the Tang’s Zhenyuan era. Yet some consider it inferior to the arrangement that combined the office with responsibility for remonstrance. Could all earlier arrangements have been incomplete, and only at this point begun to…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
備乎莫善盤者蕭望之以後諸人也而
或者又以未若得言之主者之為難豈
前此皆默至是而有言乎昔人論御史
之職要不輕受必居之以人責之以言
假之以拳豈其然乎歷代之君皆必任
是以樑內重之弊其間知是道者可類
舉乎我
國家稽古為治建都察院有都御史以為之
長又分十三道監察御史以為之屬蓋
倣秦漢之官名兼唐宋之職任內以振
===
舉
朝綱外以總領諸道法制不為不備矣委任
不為不專矣嘗竊思之在內之職莫難
於諫諍然犯顏則有逆鱗之懼循默則
有仗馬之嫌若之何其兩全歟在外之
職莫先於糾察然尚風力者或貽過中
之譏崇寬厚者或來不及之誚若之何
其盡善歟夫今之御史多取之科目之
punctuated: 備乎？莫善盤者，蕭望之以後諸人也，而或者又以未若得言之主者之為難。豈前此皆默，至是而有言乎？昔人論御史之職，要不輕受，必居之以人，責之以言，假之以拳，豈其然乎？歷代之君皆必任是以樑內重之弊，其間知是道者，可類舉乎？我國家稽古為治，建都察院，有都御史以為之長，又分十三道監察御史以為之屬，蓋倣秦漢之官名，兼唐宋之職任，內以振舉朝綱，外以總領諸道。法制不為不備矣，委任不為不專矣。嘗竊思之，在內之職莫難於諫諍，然犯顏則有逆鱗之懼，循默則有仗馬之嫌，若之何其兩全歟？在外之職莫先於糾察，然尚風力者或貽過中之譏，崇寬厚者或來不及之誚，若之何其盡善歟？夫今之御史，多取之科目之
translation_en:
…complete? None were better at this [?] than Xiao Wangzhi and those who followed him. Yet some also hold that the greater difficulty lies in finding a ruler to whom one may speak. Were all those before them silent, and did they only then begin to speak? In discussing the censor’s office, men of former times held that one should not lightly accept it: it must be filled with suitable men, who must be held responsible for speaking out and granted authority [?; the transcription reads “fists”]. Is this indeed so? Rulers of successive dynasties invariably employed these officials to remedy abuses arising from excessive power within [?; this passage is garbled]. Can examples of those among them who understood this principle be cited by category?

Our dynasty looks to antiquity in governing. It established the Censorate, with Censors-in-Chief at its head, and appointed Investigating Censors organized into thirteen circuits as its subordinate officials. Thus it adopted the official titles of Qin and Han while combining the duties of Tang and Song: within the capital, they uphold discipline at court; outside it, they exercise general oversight over the various circuits. Its laws and institutions certainly cannot be called incomplete, nor can the authority entrusted to these officials be called insufficiently concentrated.

I have ventured to reflect upon this. Of their duties within the capital, none is harder than remonstrance. Yet confronting the ruler risks touching the dragon’s sensitive scales, while remaining silent invites comparison with the mute horses of the imperial guard. How can both obligations be satisfied? Of their duties outside the capital, none takes precedence over investigating and impeaching misconduct. Yet those who prize forceful action may incur criticism for exceeding the proper mean, while those who esteem generosity and lenience may invite reproach for falling short. How can they achieve excellence in every respect? Now, many of today’s censors are recruited from among those of the civil-service examinations…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
傑諸士子繇此乎進也如或知爾則何
以哉
問進賢退不肖天下大事也治忽之機常
必由之粤稽諸古虞闢四門商立無方
卓不可及已自漢而下郡守公府皆得
舉士直指金吾皆得薦賢爲君者或以
久無所舉咎其臣爲士者或以獨必明
揚責其相薦賢之路若是其廣也然觀
寧受百欺之語則賢者不能無誤觀使
人求已之譏則下吏不免私謁所謂進
賢者安能一一皆當乎小宰六計太宰
八柄邈不可及已自漢而下有以六條
按郡國有以六條制守令有以五術察
風俗有以八計聽吏治黜陟之典若是
其嚴也然郡民知化者或以催科政拙
考其下三年無囚者或以官無異稱書
其殿所謂退不肖者安能一一無失乎
我
punctuated:
傑，諸士子繇此乎進也。如或知爾，則何以哉？

問：進賢退不肖，天下大事也，治忽之機常必由之。粤稽諸古，虞闢四門，商立無方，卓不可及已。自漢而下，郡守、公府皆得舉士，直指、金吾皆得薦賢。爲君者或以久無所舉咎其臣，爲士者或以獨必明揚責其相。薦賢之路若是其廣也，然觀寧受百欺之語，則賢者不能無誤；觀使人求已之譏，則下吏不免私謁。所謂進賢者，安能一一皆當乎？小宰六計，太宰八柄，邈不可及已。自漢而下，有以六條按郡國，有以六條制守令，有以五術察風俗，有以八計聽吏治。黜陟之典若是其嚴也，然郡民知化者，或以催科政拙考其下；三年無囚者，或以官無異稱書其殿。所謂退不肖者，安能一一無失乎？我
translation_en:
…the outstanding men selected through the examinations; you candidates advance by this same route. If someone were to recognize your abilities, what would you do?

Question: Advancing the worthy and dismissing the unworthy are great matters of the realm: the pivotal distinction between order and disorder invariably depends upon them. Looking back into antiquity, the ruler of Yu opened the four gates to worthy men, and the Shang appointed men without restriction as to their origins. These were lofty achievements beyond our reach. From the Han onward, commandery governors and the offices of the Three Dukes could all nominate scholars, while investigating censors and the Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia could all recommend worthy men. Some rulers reproached their ministers for having long failed to nominate anyone; some scholars reproached their chief ministers for insisting that men first be conspicuously distinguished before recommending them [?]. So broad were the avenues for recommending the worthy. Yet the remark that one would rather be deceived a hundred times shows that even worthy men could not avoid errors; the criticism that someone made others solicit him shows that subordinate officials could not avoid private appeals. How could every instance of what was called advancing the worthy have been appropriate?

The six criteria of the Junior Steward and the eight instruments of authority of the Grand Steward are remote precedents beyond our reach. From the Han onward, some used six articles to inspect commanderies and kingdoms; others used six articles to regulate governors and magistrates, five methods to examine customs, or eight criteria to assess officials’ administration. So stringent were the rules for demotion and promotion. Yet an official whose commandery’s people had benefited from his transforming influence might receive a low evaluation for ineptitude in collecting taxes; one who had had no prisoners for three years might be ranked last because he had earned no exceptional reputation in office. How could every instance of what was called dismissing the unworthy have been free from error? Our…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
國家之用人也尊卑大小者注
授委任責成固無容議矣然行之既久
則賢愚同滯涇渭混淆之弊或不能無
故曩歲輔臣建白欲令三品以上各舉
所知毋循資格蓋以矯積習之弊也然
論者又病其起奔競之風開偏私之徑
將來流弊殆有甚焉伊欲所進必賢君
子滿朝以上企有虞之盛如之何其可
我
===
國家之課吏也要諸三載考績有殿最
朝覲有黜陟綜核名實固無遺法矣然法久
弊乘則是非出傳聞愛憎生毀譽之誚
或未能免故比者
天語丁寧欲撫按藩臬之臣備陳實跡且被
黜而枉者聽其自訴蓋深懲偏聽之失
也然識者又恐執筆之人難乎爲辭而
貪婪之徒因以倖免姑息遷就將自茲
始焉伊欲退皆不肖不仁者遠以比隆
punctuated:
國家之用人也，尊卑大小者注授委任，責成固無容議矣。然行之既久，則賢愚同滯、涇渭混淆之弊，或不能無。故曩歲輔臣建白，欲令三品以上各舉所知，毋循資格，蓋以矯積習之弊也。然論者又病其起奔競之風，開偏私之徑，將來流弊殆有甚焉。伊欲所進必賢，君子滿朝，以上企有虞之盛，如之何其可？
我國家之課吏也，要諸三載考績，有殿最；朝覲，有黜陟。綜核名實，固無遺法矣。然法久弊乘，則是非出傳聞、愛憎生毀譽之誚，或未能免。故比者，天語丁寧，欲撫按藩臬之臣備陳實跡，且被黜而枉者，聽其自訴，蓋深懲偏聽之失也。然識者又恐執筆之人難乎爲辭，而貪婪之徒因以倖免，姑息遷就將自茲始焉。伊欲退皆不肖，不仁者遠，以比隆
translation_en:
…In the state's employment of men, appointments and assignments to offices high and low, great and small, and the requirement that appointees fulfill their responsibilities, certainly admit of no objection. Yet after these arrangements have long been in operation, abuses may inevitably arise: worthy and foolish alike languish without advancement, and the clear and turbid become confused, like the Jing and Wei rivers. Thus, some years ago, the grand secretaries submitted a proposal that officials of the third rank and above each recommend men they knew, without adhering to prescribed qualifications and seniority. This was intended to remedy entrenched abuses. Critics, however, objected that it would encourage frantic competition for advancement and open a path to favoritism, with potentially still worse abuses to follow. If we wish every man advanced to be worthy, and the court to be filled with gentlemen, aspiring to the flourishing age of Youyu, how can this be achieved?
In our state's evaluation of officials, the essentials are performance evaluations every three years, with rankings of the worst and best, and court audiences, with dismissals and promotions. In scrutinizing whether actual performance matches professed merit, no procedure has been omitted. Yet as procedures grow old and abuses take advantage of them, we may still incur the criticism that judgments of right and wrong derive from hearsay, and affection and aversion arise from slander and praise. Thus, recently, the Emperor earnestly instructed the grand coordinators, regional inspectors, provincial administration commissioners, and provincial surveillance commissioners to report actual performance fully, and also to allow those unjustly dismissed to appeal on their own behalf. This was intended firmly to correct the error of hearing only one side. Yet discerning men fear that those drafting the reports will find it difficult to frame their statements, while the avaricious will thereby escape punishment through good fortune, and indulgence and accommodation will begin from this point. If we wish all those removed to be unworthy, and those lacking benevolence to be kept far away, so as to match the grandeur of…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
帝王之治如之何其可夫公道大行風
俗醇厚當其薦者無親讐退避之嫌罹
其黜者無流言疑似之惑亦爾諸生所
當與聞而獻于
上者也毋徒諉曰此廟堂大計則吾豈敢
問治天下之道有二曰興學曰勸農夫學
以崇教化農以厚民生此古帝王已然
之迹行之萬世而不可易者也然三代
之學莫備於成周以言其教法也有六
===
德六行之數有樂語樂舞之節以言其
考校也有三年九年之條有小成大成
之類可歷舉乎由周而下或建學郡國
或大召名儒或徧立學舍或月書歲試
其於興學之意似矣然不知當時近乎
古者安在三代之農莫重於成周其在
君上也有躬親稼穡勤於疆理出入
畝而不爲屈者矣其在臣下也有教以
土宜勸以時器相忘巨觴而不爲恥者
punctuated:
帝王之治，如之何其可？夫公道大行，風俗醇厚，當其薦者，無親讐退避之嫌；罹其黜者，無流言疑似之惑，亦爾諸生所當與聞而獻于上者也。毋徒諉曰：「此廟堂大計，則吾豈敢？」

問：治天下之道有二，曰興學，曰勸農。夫學以崇教化，農以厚民生，此古帝王已然之迹，行之萬世而不可易者也。然三代之學，莫備於成周。以言其教法也，有六德六行之數，有樂語樂舞之節；以言其考校也，有三年九年之條，有小成大成之類，可歷舉乎？由周而下，或建學郡國，或大召名儒，或徧立學舍，或月書歲試，其於興學之意似矣。然不知當時近乎古者安在？三代之農，莫重於成周。其在君上也，有躬親稼穡，勤於疆理，出入畝而不爲屈者矣；其在臣下也，有教以土宜，勸以時器，相忘巨觴而不爲恥者
translation_en:
…the government of emperors and kings—how can this be achieved? When impartial justice prevails widely and customs are pure and generous, those recommended for office should occasion no suspicion concerning kinship, enmity, or avoidance [?], and those dismissed should leave no doubts arising from rumors or ambiguous evidence. These too are matters in which you students ought to take an informed interest and offer your views to the throne. Do not merely evade the issue by saying: “This is a great matter of state policy; how could I presume?”

Question: There are two ways to govern the realm: promoting learning and encouraging agriculture. Learning advances moral instruction, while agriculture enriches the people’s livelihood. These are practices already established by the emperors and kings of antiquity, to be followed for ten thousand generations without alteration. Yet among the schools of the Three Dynasties, none were more fully developed than those of Zhou. In their methods of instruction, there were the categories of the Six Virtues and Six Forms of Conduct, and the prescribed forms of musical discourse and dance. In their examinations and assessments, there were provisions for the third and ninth years, and distinctions between Lesser Accomplishment and Greater Accomplishment. Can you enumerate these in detail? After Zhou, some established schools in the commanderies and kingdoms; some summoned eminent Confucian scholars in great numbers; some established school buildings everywhere; and some recorded progress monthly and conducted examinations annually. These seem to accord with the intention of promoting learning. Yet which practices of those times approached those of antiquity?

Among the Three Dynasties, none placed greater importance on agriculture than Zhou. Among its rulers were those who personally sowed and harvested, diligently attended to the demarcation and ordering of fields, and went among the cultivated plots without considering it beneath their dignity. Among its ministers were those who taught what crops suited the soil, encouraged farming according to the seasons and with appropriate implements, and forgot distinctions over great drinking vessels [?] without considering it shameful…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
矣可悉數乎由周而降或多方勸率或
蠲罪給符或法駕親視或繪圖左右其
於勸農之意似矣然不知當時復乎古
者奚在我
國家立養士之法內而胄監外而庠序無一
地而非學上而公卿下而庶人無一人
而不學歷年既久宜其人材之倍出也
夫何攻乎業者未必皆體驗乎身心致
乎用者未必皆通達乎政事甚至出入
===
經史之莫講砥礪名節之罕聞士習如
此豈今日振起之者尚未至乎我
國家立養民之法田有差等口分世業無不
授田之人賦有限期夏斂秋征無不出
賦之家歷歲滋久宜其農事之大修也
夫何去南畝而游市井者官不禁戢未
耜而適四方者關不譏甚至富者田連
阡陌貧者囊無錙銖民力如此豈今日
勸相之者尚未周乎茲欲使士勤于習
punctuated:
矣，可悉數乎？由周而降，或多方勸率，或蠲罪給符，或法駕親視，或繪圖左右，其於勸農之意似矣，然不知當時復乎古者奚在？
我國家立養士之法，內而胄監，外而庠序，無一地而非學；上而公卿，下而庶人，無一人而不學。歷年既久，宜其人材之倍出也。夫何攻乎業者未必皆體驗乎身心，致乎用者未必皆通達乎政事，甚至出入經史之莫講，砥礪名節之罕聞？士習如此，豈今日振起之者尚未至乎？
我國家立養民之法，田有差等，口分世業，無不授田之人；賦有限期，夏斂秋征，無不出賦之家。歷歲滋久，宜其農事之大修也。夫何去南畝而游市井者官不禁，戢未耜而適四方者關不譏，甚至富者田連阡陌，貧者囊無錙銖？民力如此，豈今日勸相之者尚未周乎？茲欲使士勤于習
translation_en:
… Can all these instances be enumerated? From the Zhou onward, some encouraged and guided farming by various means; some remitted offenses and issued certificates; some personally inspected the fields with the imperial procession; and some had pictures of farming placed beside them. Their intention to encourage agriculture seems similar to that of antiquity, yet it is unclear which practices of those times truly restored the ancient ways.
Our dynasty has established methods for nurturing scholars. Within the capital there is the Directorate of Education, and outside it there are local schools: no place lacks a school. From dukes and ministers above to commoners below, no one is without learning. After so many years, men of talent ought to have emerged in increasing numbers. Why, then, do those who pursue their studies not necessarily put their learning into practice in their own persons and minds, while those who enter service do not necessarily understand governmental affairs? Indeed, thorough engagement with the classics and histories goes untaught, and efforts to strengthen personal honor and integrity are seldom heard of. If scholars’ habits are like this, could present efforts to revive them still be inadequate?
Our dynasty has established methods for nurturing the people. Fields are graded, with allotments per person and hereditary holdings, so that no one goes without an allocation of land. Taxes have fixed deadlines, with summer collections and autumn levies, so that no household fails to pay tax. After so many years, agriculture ought to have been greatly improved. Why, then, do officials fail to restrain those who abandon the southern fields to idle in the marketplaces, while checkpoint officials fail to question those who put away their plows [?] and travel in every direction? Indeed, the rich possess fields stretching across ridge after ridge, while the poor have not the smallest coin in their purses. If the people’s resources are in such a state, could present efforts to encourage and assist them still be incomplete? Now we wish to make scholars diligent in their studies…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而咸詠乎菁莪之化農勤於耕而胥服
乎襏襫之事稽古而不泥於陳腐濟時
而不近於鄙俗非疏通知遠之才孰能
與於斯執事者願有聞也
punctuated: 而咸詠乎菁莪之化，農勤於耕而胥服乎襏襫之事，稽古而不泥於陳腐，濟時而不近於鄙俗，非疏通知遠之才，孰能與於斯？執事者願有聞也。
translation_en: …and all sing the praises of the nurturing influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Wormwood”; to make farmers diligent in cultivation, all devoting themselves to the work for which they don rain capes; to draw upon antiquity without becoming mired in outworn practices, and to meet the needs of the times without descending into vulgarity—who could accomplish this without broad understanding and far-reaching insight? We who administer this examination wish to hear your views.

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
行夏之時乘殷之輅服周之冕樂則韶舞
張子渭
同考試官訓導黄　批〔說出聖人斟酌四代禮樂之意纖悉明白蓋嘗究心於用世之學者〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔通篇鋪敘平正當是作手〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔融會傳註獨異衆作是用錄出〕
禮取諸三王之所制者樂取諸大聖之所作者
===
聖人為大賢告然也蓋三王制禮代各不同而
韶樂則非虞舜之大聖不能作也斟酌其間而
取用之於致治也何有昔顔淵問為邦聖人以
治天下之法告之如此意謂禮樂治之法也古
先帝王孰不有所制之禮亦孰不有所作之樂
顧擇而用之者何如耳是故頒朔授民惟時是
急求之於古吾得夏時焉蓋周正建子則生物
之功未著商正建丑則改歲之義未明惟夏正
建寅以人為紀盛德在木而生物於是乎始時
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「行夏之時，乘殷之輅，服周之冕，樂則韶舞。」
張子渭
同考試官訓導黄批〔說出聖人斟酌四代禮樂之意，纖悉明白，蓋嘗究心於用世之學者。〕
考試官教諭孫批〔通篇鋪敘平正，當是作手。〕
考試官教諭羅批〔融會傳註，獨異衆作，是用錄出。〕
禮取諸三王之所制者，樂取諸大聖之所作者。
聖人為大賢告然也。蓋三王制禮，代各不同，而韶樂則非虞舜之大聖不能作也。斟酌其間而取用之，於致治也何有？昔顔淵問為邦，聖人以治天下之法告之如此。意謂禮樂，治之法也。古先帝王，孰不有所制之禮，亦孰不有所作之樂？顧擇而用之者何如耳。是故頒朔授民，惟時是急。求之於古，吾得夏時焉。蓋周正建子，則生物之功未著；商正建丑，則改歲之義未明。惟夏正建寅，以人為紀，盛德在木，而生物於是乎始。時
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Follow the calendar of Xia, ride in the carriage of Yin, wear the ceremonial cap of Zhou; for music, use the Shao dance.”
Zhang Ziwei
Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He explains the sage’s intention in weighing the rites and music of the four dynasties, making even the finest details clear. He must have devoted serious thought to learning directed toward service in the world.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition throughout is balanced and sound. He must be an accomplished writer.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔He integrates the commentaries and annotations, standing apart from the other compositions. For this reason, it has been selected for inclusion.〕
For rites, select from what the kings of the Three Dynasties instituted; for music, select from what the great sage composed.
Such was the sage’s instruction to the great worthy. The kings of the Three Dynasties instituted rites that differed from one dynasty to another, whereas the Shao music could have been composed only by a great sage such as Shun of Yu. If one weighs these traditions and selects among them for use, what difficulty can there be in achieving good government? When Yan Yuan once asked about governing a state, the sage instructed him in this way in the methods of governing all under Heaven. His meaning was that rites and music are the means of government. Among the emperors and kings of antiquity, who did not institute rites, and who did not compose music? The question is simply how one selects and employs them. Thus, in promulgating the calendar and communicating it to the people, correct timing is the most urgent concern. Seeking it in antiquity, I find it in the calendar of Xia. The first month of Zhou fell in the month designated zi, when the work of bringing living things into being was not yet manifest; the first month of Shang fell in the month designated chou, when the significance of the year’s renewal was not yet clear. Only Xia placed its first month in the month designated yin, taking humanity as its calendrical reference: the flourishing potency resides in Wood, and the generation of living things begins at this point. As for its timing…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
莫有正焉者也三陽始備而歲歲事於是乎新令
莫有善焉者也玆欲表歲首以定統瞻斗柄而
紀年可不行夏之時乎繼夏而王者商商之所
制有輅焉朴素渾堅而等威已辨爲質而得其
中者矣古非無車也太朴則無文過侈則易敗
不若商之輅爲可乗也繼商而王者周周之制
有冕焉華不爲靡貴不及奢爲文而得其中者
矣古非無冕也制度之未詳儀等之未備不若
周之冕爲可服也夫三代之禮其可取者如此
===
禮備則樂作樂之用當孰取乎彼商之大濩猶
有慙德周之大武猶未盡善惟虞舜以大聖之
人作大韶之樂暢中和於九德之歌文備而情
亦備也宣至德於九韶之舞善盡而美亦盡也
故欲薦之郊廟必用帝舜之韶于以治神人和
上下無感不通矣欲奏之朝廷必用韶舞之樂
于以定民志育人材無用不違矣是則取帝王
之制酌可用之宜治天下如指諸掌爲邦何足
言哉抑爲治必用禮樂古之帝王槩是頁□□
punctuated: 莫有正焉者也。三陽始備，而歲歲事於是乎新，令莫有善焉者也。玆欲表歲首以定統，瞻斗柄而紀年，可不行夏之時乎？繼夏而王者商，商之所制有輅焉，朴素渾堅而等威已辨，爲質而得其中者矣。古非無車也，太朴則無文，過侈則易敗，不若商之輅爲可乗也。繼商而王者周，周之制有冕焉，華不爲靡，貴不及奢，爲文而得其中者矣。古非無冕也，制度之未詳，儀等之未備，不若周之冕爲可服也。夫三代之禮，其可取者如此。禮備則樂作，樂之用當孰取乎？彼商之大濩猶有慙德，周之大武猶未盡善。惟虞舜以大聖之人作大韶之樂，暢中和於九德之歌，文備而情亦備也；宣至德於九韶之舞，善盡而美亦盡也。故欲薦之郊廟，必用帝舜之韶，于以治神人、和上下，無感不通矣。欲奏之朝廷，必用韶舞之樂，于以定民志、育人材，無用不違矣。是則取帝王之制，酌可用之宜，治天下如指諸掌，爲邦何足言哉！抑爲治必用禮樂，古之帝王槩是頁□□
translation_en: …none is more correct. The three yang lines have just become complete, and the year's affairs are thereby renewed [?]; no seasonal ordinance is better. Thus, if one wishes to mark the year's beginning to establish the calendrical succession, and to reckon the year by observing the Dipper's handle, how could one fail to follow the calendar of Xia? Shang succeeded Xia in kingship. Among Shang's institutions was its royal carriage: plain, simple, solid, and sturdy, yet already distinguishing the dignity of the various ranks. In its simplicity it attained the proper mean. Earlier times had certainly possessed carriages, but excessive simplicity lacked refinement, while excessive extravagance made them liable to break down. None was as suitable to ride in as the Shang carriage. Zhou succeeded Shang in kingship. Among Zhou's institutions was its ceremonial crown: splendid without being ostentatious, dignified without reaching extravagance. In its refinement it attained the proper mean. Earlier times had certainly possessed crowns, but their specifications were not yet fully detailed, and their ceremonial distinctions of rank were incomplete. None was as suitable to wear as the Zhou crown. Such were the features worth adopting from the rites of the Three Dynasties. Once rites are complete, music is performed. What music, then, should one adopt? Shang's Great Huo still reflected a cause for shame in its ruler's virtue, while Zhou's Great Wu was still not perfectly good. Only Yu Shun, a person of supreme sagehood, created the music of the Great Shao. He gave full expression to equilibrium and harmony in the songs of the nine virtues: its artistic form and its feeling were both complete. He proclaimed consummate virtue in the ninefold Shao dance: its goodness and its beauty were both perfect. Thus, to present music at the suburban sacrifices and in the ancestral temples, one must use Emperor Shun's Shao. Through it, spirits and human beings are brought into order, and those above and below into harmony; no impulse fails to elicit a response. To perform music at court, one must use the music of the Shao dance. Through it, the people's aspirations are steadied and human talent nurtured; the following phrase reads, doubtfully, 'no application fails to contravene' [?]. Thus, by adopting the institutions of emperors and kings and weighing what is suitable for use, one can govern All under Heaven as readily as pointing to one's palm. What need, then, even to speak of governing a single state? Moreover, governing necessarily requires rites and music; the emperors and kings of antiquity all … [the concluding text is garbled and includes two illegible characters: 槩是頁□□].

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
時異則勢殊法久則弊生當時固加損益而後
世寧無可否聖人有憂之特取歷代之制而斟
酌之擇其經久可行者以立萬世常行之道爲
百王不易之法焉然惟顏子得聞之而卒不得
位又徒托之空言然則欲措孔顏之道之法而
達之天下者必有聖人之德而在天子之位
唯天下至誠爲能經綸天下之大經立天
下之大本知天地之化育夫焉有所倚
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天苟不固
聰明聖知達天德者其孰能知之
楊樛
===
同考試官訓導談　批〔說至誠之道非至聖不能知之意殆無餘蘊必潛心於理學者〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔題長而辭不贅佳作也〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔理明詞簡可嘉〕
論誠之至者功用極其妙惟聖之至者爲能契
其妙蓋至誠之道至聖之德本非二物也然而
至誠功用之妙非至聖其孰能與知哉中庸三
punctuated:
時異則勢殊，法久則弊生。當時固加損益，而後世寧無可否？聖人有憂之，特取歷代之制而斟酌之，擇其經久可行者，以立萬世常行之道，爲百王不易之法焉。然惟顏子得聞之，而卒不得位，又徒托之空言。然則欲措孔顏之道之法而達之天下者，必有聖人之德而在天子之位。
唯天下至誠，爲能經綸天下之大經，立天下之大本，知天地之化育。夫焉有所倚？肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。苟不固聰明聖知、達天德者，其孰能知之？
楊樛
同考試官訓導談，批〔說至誠之道非至聖不能知之意，殆無餘蘊，必潛心於理學者〕
考試官教諭羅，批〔題長而辭不贅，佳作也〕
考試官教諭孫，批〔理明詞簡，可嘉〕
論誠之至者，功用極其妙，惟聖之至者爲能契其妙。蓋至誠之道、至聖之德，本非二物也。然而至誠功用之妙，非至聖，其孰能與知哉？《中庸》三
translation_en:
…When times differ, circumstances change; when institutions endure long, abuses arise. Even in their own day, additions and reductions were made: could later ages have no grounds for approving or rejecting them? The sage was concerned about this. He therefore selected and weighed the institutions of successive dynasties, choosing those that could remain practicable over time, to establish a Way for constant observance through myriad generations and an unchanging standard for all kings. Yet only Master Yan heard this teaching, and in the end he obtained no position; it remained entrusted merely to words. Thus, whoever would put into practice the Way and methods of Kongzi and Yan Hui and extend them throughout the realm must possess the virtue of a sage and occupy the position of the Son of Heaven.
Only one of utmost sincerity under Heaven can order the great guiding relationships of the world, establish its great foundation, and understand the transforming and nourishing processes of Heaven and Earth. On what could he depend? How earnest his benevolence, how deep his profundity, how vast his heaven! Unless one is truly perceptive, sagely, and wise, comprehending Heaven’s virtue, who could understand him?
Yang Jiu 楊樛
Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation that only the utmost sage can understand the Way of utmost sincerity leaves scarcely any meaning unexplored. The writer must be someone who has devoted himself deeply to the Learning of Principle.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔Although the topic is long, the wording is not prolix. An excellent composition.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔The principles are clear and the language concise: commendable.〕
I submit that, in one whose sincerity reaches its utmost, its efficacy is supremely subtle; only one whose sageliness reaches its utmost can comprehend that subtlety. For the Way of utmost sincerity and the virtue of utmost sageliness are fundamentally not two separate things. Yet who but the utmost sage could understand the subtle efficacy of utmost sincerity? The Doctrine of the Mean, chapter thirty…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
十二章推言大德敦化以明天道如此且夫誠
者天之道也謂之曰天下至誠豈非聖人之德
極誠無妄舉天下莫能加乎誠不可加用斯妙
矣是故人之秉彝有大經焉於天下大經爲能
經綸之各盡人倫當然之實而爲天下後世之
法者在是大經所由出有大本焉於天下大本
爲能建立之全具性分本然之體而爲千變萬
化之原者在是大本所從出有化育焉爲能與
之默契一誠脗合而聞見俱泯全體渾融而形
===
迹不露是皆至誠自然之功用夫豈有所倚著
於物而後能哉然自經綸言之五品之倫一天
理之純全肫肫懇到是仁而已矣自立本言之
所性之中爲物理歸會之地淵淵靜深是淵而
已矣自知化言之一念之運爲萬物資始之妙
浩浩廣大是天而已矣至誠之功用一至此哉
夫是道也苟非固聰明聖智出於天性而具生
知之資仁義禮智由於自然而達天德之奧則
體之未至見之未真不免裂事物爲殊途岐性
punctuated: 十二章推言大德敦化，以明天道如此。且夫誠者，天之道也。謂之曰天下至誠，豈非聖人之德極誠無妄，舉天下莫能加乎？誠不可加，用斯妙矣。是故人之秉彝有大經焉，於天下大經爲能經綸之，各盡人倫當然之實，而爲天下後世之法者在是。大經所由出有大本焉，於天下大本爲能建立之，全具性分本然之體，而爲千變萬化之原者在是。大本所從出有化育焉，爲能與之默契，一誠脗合而聞見俱泯，全體渾融而形迹不露。是皆至誠自然之功用，夫豈有所倚著於物而後能哉？然自經綸言之，五品之倫，一天理之純全，肫肫懇到，是仁而已矣。自立本言之，所性之中爲物理歸會之地，淵淵靜深，是淵而已矣。自知化言之，一念之運爲萬物資始之妙，浩浩廣大，是天而已矣。至誠之功用一至此哉！夫是道也，苟非固聰明聖智出於天性而具生知之資，仁義禮智由於自然而達天德之奧，則體之未至，見之未真，不免裂事物爲殊途，岐性
translation_en:
…the thirty-second chapter develops the statement that great virtue brings about profound transformation, thereby illuminating the Way of Heaven in this manner. Now sincerity is the Way of Heaven. To speak of “the utmost sincerity under Heaven”—does this not mean that the sage’s virtue is supremely sincere and free from falsity, such that nothing throughout the world can surpass it? When sincerity cannot be surpassed, its operation is wondrous. Thus, within the constant moral nature endowed in human beings, there are the great guiding relationships. Only one of utmost sincerity can order these great relationships under Heaven, fully realizing what is proper to each human relationship; herein lies the model for the world and later generations. There is a great foundation from which these guiding relationships arise. Only one of utmost sincerity can establish this great foundation of the world, possessing in full the original substance of one’s endowed nature; herein lies the source of the myriad changes and transformations. There is the transforming and nourishing activity from which this great foundation proceeds. Only one of utmost sincerity can accord with it silently: united through a single sincerity, with distinctions of hearing and seeing entirely effaced, the whole substance blends harmoniously without revealing outward traces. These are all the spontaneous effects of utmost sincerity. How could they depend on attachment to external things before becoming possible?

Yet, viewed in terms of ordering the relationships, the five human relationships embody the pure completeness of the single principle of Heaven. Earnest and thoroughly sincere, this is simply benevolence. Viewed in terms of establishing the foundation, the equilibrium inherent in one’s nature is where the principles of things converge. Profoundly still and deep, this is simply the abyss. Viewed in terms of knowing transformation, the activity of a single thought constitutes the wondrous source from which the myriad things take their beginning. Vast and expansive, this is simply Heaven. Can the operation of utmost sincerity reach such heights!

As for this Way, unless one’s keenness of hearing, clarity of sight, sagacity, and wisdom arise inherently from one’s heavenly nature, giving one the capacity for innate knowledge, and unless benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom proceed spontaneously, enabling one to penetrate the profundities of Heaven’s virtue, then one’s embodiment of it will be incomplete and one’s perception of it inexact. One will inevitably split affairs and things into divergent paths and sunder human nature…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
命於二致其於天下大經已不知所以經綸之
矣孰知所謂肫肫其仁乎天下大本已不知所
以立之矣孰知所謂淵淵其淵乎天地化育已
判乎不相契矣孰知所謂浩浩其天乎吁至誠
之道惟聖人而後知則至誠之道盡聖人之能
事畢矣大抵自爲而言曰誠誠非聖不能知自
知而言曰聖聖非誠不能爲名異而道不異德
同而妙亦同若是者其視溥博淵泉猶以爲小
德焉莫不尊親猶以爲有迹焉上天之載無聲
===
無臭極矣至矣不可以有加矣中庸發明聖人
之天道至是其無餘蘊矣哉
人有雞犬放則知求之有放心而不知求
學問之道無他求其放心而已矣
石鼐
同考試官訓導談　批〔孟子有餘不盡之意朱子於集註足之是篇善發明而結尤警策讀之令人自奮〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔立論極至重上且詞語謹嚴〕
是必知所求者
punctuated:
命於二致。其於天下大經，已不知所以經綸之矣，孰知所謂肫肫其仁乎？天下大本，已不知所以立之矣，孰知所謂淵淵其淵乎？天地化育，已判乎不相契矣，孰知所謂浩浩其天乎？吁！至誠之道，惟聖人而後知，則至誠之道，盡聖人之能事畢矣。大抵自爲而言曰誠，誠非聖不能知；自知而言曰聖，聖非誠不能爲。名異而道不異，德同而妙亦同。若是者，其視溥博淵泉，猶以爲小德焉；莫不尊親，猶以爲有迹焉。上天之載，無聲無臭，極矣，至矣，不可以有加矣。《中庸》發明聖人之天道，至是其無餘蘊矣哉！
人有雞犬放，則知求之；有放心，而不知求。學問之道無他，求其放心而已矣。
石鼐
同考試官訓導談　批〔孟子有餘不盡之意，朱子於集註足之。是篇善發明，而結尤警策，讀之令人自奮。〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔立論極至重上，且詞語謹嚴。〕
是必知所求者
translation_en:
…and destiny into two distinct principles. As for the great relationships under Heaven, such a person no longer knows how to order them: how could he understand what is meant by “how earnest his benevolence”? As for the great foundation of all under Heaven, he no longer knows how to establish it: how could he understand what is meant by “how deep his profundity”? He stands apart from the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth, no longer in accord with it: how could he understand what is meant by “how vast his Heaven”? Ah! Only a sage can understand the Way of utmost sincerity; thus this Way encompasses all that a sage can accomplish. Broadly speaking, considered from the standpoint of action, it is called sincerity, and only a sage can understand sincerity; considered from the standpoint of knowledge, it is called sagehood, and only through sincerity can sagehood be realized. The names differ, but the Way does not; the virtue is the same, and so too is its subtle efficacy. One who has reached this state regards even all-encompassing breadth and fountain-like depth as lesser virtues, and universal reverence and affection as still bearing visible traces. “The workings of Heaven have neither sound nor scent”: this is the utmost limit, the highest attainment, to which nothing can be added. In elucidating the sage’s Way of Heaven, has not the Doctrine of the Mean here left nothing unrevealed?

“When people’s chickens and dogs stray, they know to seek them; yet when their heart strays, they do not know to seek it. The Way of learning is nothing other than seeking the heart that has strayed.”

Shi Nai

Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor: 〔Mencius leaves implications that are not fully expressed; Master Zhu supplies them in his Collected Commentaries. This essay elucidates them well, and its conclusion is especially incisive and admonitory. Reading it spurs one to exert oneself.〕

Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: 〔The argument reaches the utmost and places emphasis on the preceding portion [?]; moreover, its wording is careful and rigorous.〕

This must be one who knows what to seek…

以立之矣孰知所謂淵淵其淵乎天地化育已
判乎不相契矣孰知所謂浩浩其天乎吁至誠

知而言曰聖聖非誠不能為名異而道不異德

德焉莫不尊親猶以為有迹焉上天之載無聲
===

之天道至是其無餘藴矣哉
人有雞犬放則知求之有放心而不知求
學問之道無他求其放心而已矣

考試官教諭羅　批〔立論在至重上且詞語謹嚴是必知所求者〕
punctuated:
命於二，致其於天下大經，已不知所以經綸之矣，孰知所謂肫肫其仁乎？天下大本，已不知所以立之矣，孰知所謂淵淵其淵乎？天地化育，已判乎不相契矣，孰知所謂浩浩其天乎？吁！至誠之道，惟聖人而後知，則至誠之道盡，聖人之能事畢矣。大抵自為而言曰誠，誠非聖不能知；自知而言曰聖，聖非誠不能為。名異而道不異，德同而妙亦同。若是者，其視溥慱淵泉，猶以為小德焉；莫不尊親，猶以為有迹焉。上天之載，無聲無臭，極矣，至矣，不可以有加矣。《中庸》發明聖人之天道，至是其無餘藴矣哉！

「人有雞犬放，則知求之；有放心，而不知求。」「學問之道無他，求其放心而已矣。」
石鼐
同考試官訓導談　批〔孟子有餘不盡之意朱子於集註足之是篇善發出而結尤警策讀之令人自奮〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔立論在至重上且詞語謹嚴是必知所求者〕
translation_en:
…assigned to two [?], with the result that, regarding the great guiding principles of all under Heaven, one no longer knows how to order them. Who, then, could understand what is meant by “how earnest his benevolence”? Regarding the great foundation of all under Heaven, one no longer knows how to establish it. Who, then, could understand what is meant by “how deep his profundity”? One has become separated from the transforming and nurturing processes of Heaven and Earth, no longer in accord with them. Who, then, could understand what is meant by “how vast his Heaven”? Ah! Only a sage can understand the Way of utmost sincerity. Thus, when the Way of utmost sincerity is fully realized, all that a sage can accomplish is complete. Generally speaking, viewed in terms of practice, it is called sincerity: only a sage can understand sincerity. Viewed in terms of understanding, it is called sagehood: only through sincerity can one attain sagehood. The names differ, but the Way does not; the virtue is the same, and so too is its subtle efficacy. One who has attained this regards even breadth and depth like a deep-flowing spring as a lesser virtue, and universal reverence and affection as still bearing visible traces. “The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” This is the utmost, the ultimate; nothing can be added to it. In elucidating the sage’s Way of Heaven, has the Doctrine of the Mean not, at this point, left nothing undisclosed?

“When people’s chickens and dogs stray, they know to seek them; when their minds stray, they do not know to seek them.” “The Way of learning is nothing other than seeking one’s strayed mind.”
By Shi Nai 石鼐.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tan 談, Assistant Instructor: 〔Mencius leaves some of his meaning unexpressed; Master Zhu supplies it in the Collected Commentaries. This essay brings it out well, and its conclusion is especially stirring and admonitory. Reading it moves one to exert oneself.〕

Comment by Examiner Luo 羅, Instructor: 〔The argument rests on what is of utmost importance, and the wording is careful and rigorous. This must be someone who knows what to seek.〕

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭孫　批〔講有輕重足見所學〕
大賢歎人不知求其所重必示人當知求其所
重蓋人心至重而或放之則當知所以求之也
然則爲學之道其要豈外是哉昔孟子論仁義
之切於人及此謂夫天下之事有重有輕重者
當急而輕者在所緩也然人亦有不審而倒施
焉者何邪彼雞犬特一物之微耳得之不足以
爲重失之不足以爲輕其所繫甚小也人有雞
犬之放則皇皇焉即知所以求之焉心乃一身
===
之主也存之則進於聖賢失之則入於禽獸其
所繫甚重也人於此心之放顧貿貿焉不知所
以求之焉是豈愛其至輕而忘其至重哉夫思
而已矣彼學問之事若博學若審問固非一端
也然其道則在於靜而存養之于以斂放心於
一腔不使頃刻之間有所馳騖於外焉是要領
所在而爲學者持循之地也若慎思若明辨固
亦多術也然其道則在於動而省察之于以約
放心于方寸不使須臾之際有所牽引於外焉
punctuated:
考試官教諭孫　批〔講有輕重，足見所學。〕

大賢歎人不知求其所重，必示人當知求其所重。蓋人心至重，而或放之，則當知所以求之也。然則爲學之道，其要豈外是哉？昔孟子論仁義之切於人，及此謂夫天下之事有重有輕，重者當急，而輕者在所緩也。然人亦有不審而倒施焉者，何邪？彼雞犬特一物之微耳，得之不足以爲重，失之不足以爲輕，其所繫甚小也。人有雞犬之放，則皇皇焉，即知所以求之焉。心乃一身之主也，存之則進於聖賢，失之則入於禽獸，其所繫甚重也。人於此心之放，顧貿貿焉，不知所以求之焉。是豈愛其至輕而忘其至重哉？夫思而已矣。彼學問之事，若博學，若審問，固非一端也。然其道則在於靜而存養之，于以斂放心於一腔，不使頃刻之間有所馳騖於外焉。是要領所在，而爲學者持循之地也。若慎思，若明辨，固亦多術也。然其道則在於動而省察之，于以約放心于方寸，不使須臾之際有所牽引於外焉。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: 〔The exposition distinguishes between what is of lesser and greater importance, amply revealing the author's learning.〕

The great worthy lamented that people did not know to seek what mattered most to them, and therefore had to show them that they ought to know to seek it. For the human mind is of the utmost importance; if one lets it stray, one ought to know how to recover it. Could the essential principle of learning, then, lie outside this? When Mengzi discussed how urgently benevolence and righteousness concern human beings, he reached this point: among the affairs of the world, some are weighty and some slight. Weighty matters deserve urgent attention, while slight ones may be deferred. Yet there are people who fail to discern this and reverse their priorities. Why is this?

Chickens and dogs are merely insignificant creatures. Gaining them does not make one more worthy, nor does losing them make one less worthy; very little depends upon them. Yet when people's chickens or dogs stray, they become anxious and immediately know to seek them. The mind, however, is the master of one's entire person. By preserving it, one advances toward the sages and worthies; by losing it, one sinks to the level of birds and beasts. What depends upon it is exceedingly weighty. Yet when this mind strays, people remain oblivious and do not know how to seek it. How can they cherish what matters least and forget what matters most? It is simply a matter of reflection.

The work of learning and inquiry—such as studying broadly and questioning carefully—certainly comprises more than one activity. Yet its way lies in preserving and nourishing the mind in stillness, thereby gathering the straying mind back within one's breast and preventing it from racing outward even for an instant. Here lies the essential principle, the ground upon which learners must maintain their practice. Likewise, careful reflection and clear discrimination certainly involve many methods. Yet their way lies in examining the mind during activity, thereby restraining the straying mind within the heart and preventing it from being drawn outward even for a moment…
