title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
是樞機所在而為學者據守之方也能如是則
志氣清明義理昭著而可以上達不然則昏昧
放逸雖曰從事于學終亦不能有所發明矣大
抵人有生則有心而心實身之主也能求放心
則不違於仁而義在其中矣此孟子開示學者
之深意也然所謂求放心者亦正謂此心既存
則學之為有益耳如以求放心之外更無餘事
遂廢讀書窮理為無所用之則是陸象山之教
其徒者所以卒流異端禪學而莫之覺也此又
朱子發明孟子言外之意學者其服膺而勿失
之哉
===
易
君子以言有物而行有恒
閻佩
同考試官訓導黃　批〔君子體易以修身治家之道此作〕〔發揮明白錄之以範後學〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔文理切當〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔善言體易之事〕
punctuated:
是樞機所在，而為學者據守之方也。能如是，則志氣清明，義理昭著，而可以上達；不然，則昏昧放逸，雖曰從事于學，終亦不能有所發明矣。大抵人有生則有心，而心實身之主也。能求放心，則不違於仁，而義在其中矣。此孟子開示學者之深意也。然所謂求放心者，亦正謂此心既存，則學之為有益耳。如以求放心之外更無餘事，遂廢讀書窮理，為無所用之，則是陸象山之教其徒者，所以卒流異端禪學而莫之覺也。此又朱子發明孟子言外之意，學者其服膺而勿失之哉！

《易》
君子以言有物而行有恒。
閻佩
同考試官訓導黃　批〔君子體易以修身治家之道，此作〕〔發揮明白，錄之以範後學。〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔文理切當。〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔善言體易之事。〕
translation_en:
…This is where the crucial mechanism lies, and it is the method by which learners hold their ground. If they can do this, their purpose and vital energy will be clear, moral principles will become manifest, and they can advance to higher understanding. Otherwise, they will remain benighted and unrestrained; although they may claim to engage in learning, ultimately they will gain no illumination. In general, wherever there is human life there is a mind, and the mind is indeed the master of the person. If one can recover the strayed mind, one will not depart from benevolence, and righteousness will be contained within it. This is the profound intention behind Mencius’s instruction to learners. Yet what is called recovering the strayed mind means precisely that, once this mind is preserved, learning becomes beneficial. If one supposes that there is nothing further to do beyond recovering the strayed mind, and consequently abandons reading and investigating principle as useless, this is how Lu Xiangshan taught his disciples, and why they ultimately drifted into heterodox Chan learning without realizing it. This, moreover, is Master Zhu’s elucidation of the meaning beyond Mencius’s words. Let learners cherish it in their hearts and never lose it!

Book of Changes
“The noble man accordingly gives substance to his words and constancy to his conduct.”
Yan Pei

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: “This composition clearly expounds the way in which the noble man embodies the Changes to cultivate himself and govern his household. It is recorded here as a model for later learners.”

Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: “The composition and its reasoning are apt and sound.”

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: “It speaks well of putting the Changes into practice.”

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
君子體易卦之象必盡脩身之道焉蓋家之本
在身而謹言行所以脩身也言行旣謹此身之
所以脩而家之所以治也歟昔吾夫子傳象之
意謂夫巽上離下卦名家人有風自火出由內
及外之象君子體之知風自火而出則知家之
本自身而出故欲治其家惟在謹言行以脩其
身焉彼出諸口者謂之言言而无物則為虛言
非脩身也君子則无稽弗言所言者鑿鑿皆實
而无妄非法不道所道者恂恂可信而不欺言
===
必中倫否則寧艮其輔也言必顧行否則寧括
其囊也言有物如此則言脩於身而教於家者
有持循據守之則矣見於身者謂之行行而无
恒則為僞行非脩身也君子則凡行己也體夫
當然之道不以今昔而有間凡處物也循其一
定之理不以彼此而或渝踐履有常確然其篤
實也力行不怠毅然其持久也行有恒如此則
行脩於身而刑於家者有觀感興起之機矣君
子脩身治家其道若是則倫理以正恩義以篤
punctuated:
君子體易卦之象，必盡脩身之道焉。蓋家之本在身，而謹言行所以脩身也。言行旣謹，此身之所以脩，而家之所以治也歟！昔吾夫子傳象之意，謂夫巽上離下，卦名家人，有風自火出、由內及外之象。君子體之，知風自火而出，則知家之本自身而出，故欲治其家，惟在謹言行以脩其身焉。
彼出諸口者謂之言。言而无物，則為虛言，非脩身也。君子則无稽弗言，所言者鑿鑿皆實而无妄；非法不道，所道者恂恂可信而不欺。言必中倫，否則寧艮其輔也；言必顧行，否則寧括其囊也。言有物如此，則言脩於身，而教於家者有持循據守之則矣。
見於身者謂之行。行而无恒，則為僞行，非脩身也。君子則凡行己也，體夫當然之道，不以今昔而有間；凡處物也，循其一定之理，不以彼此而或渝。踐履有常，確然其篤實也；力行不怠，毅然其持久也。行有恒如此，則行脩於身，而刑於家者有觀感興起之機矣。
君子脩身治家，其道若是，則倫理以正，恩義以篤
translation_en:
When the gentleman embodies the image of a hexagram in the Book of Changes, he must fully carry out the way of cultivating himself. For the foundation of the family lies in oneself, and care in speech and conduct is the means of self-cultivation. Once speech and conduct are made careful, is this not how the self is cultivated and the family put in order? The meaning of our Master’s commentary on the image was this: with Xun above and Li below, the hexagram is named Jiaren, “The Family,” and presents the image of wind issuing from fire, proceeding from within to without. Embodying this image, the gentleman understands that wind issues from fire and thus understands that the foundation of the family proceeds from himself. Therefore, if he wishes to put his family in order, he must attend carefully to speech and conduct in order to cultivate himself.
What issues from the mouth is called speech. If speech has no substance, it is empty speech, not self-cultivation. The gentleman says nothing without grounds: everything he says is firmly substantiated, true and free of falsehood. He speaks nothing that does not accord with proper standards: what he says is sincere, trustworthy and without deceit. His words must accord with proper principles; otherwise, he would rather “keep his jaws still.” His words must take account of his conduct; otherwise, he would rather “tie up his sack.” When speech has substance in this way, his own speech is cultivated, and his teaching within the family has standards to follow and uphold.
What manifests itself in one’s person is called conduct. If conduct lacks constancy, it is feigned conduct, not self-cultivation. In all his personal conduct, the gentleman embodies the way of what is right, without allowing any discrepancy between past and present. In all his dealings with things, he follows their fixed principles, without changing them to suit one case or another. Constant in his practice, he is firmly sincere; tireless in putting principles into action, he is resolute in persevering. When conduct has constancy in this way, his own conduct is cultivated, and his example within the family provides the means for others to observe, be moved and be stirred to emulate him.
When the gentleman follows such a way in cultivating himself and ordering his family, human relationships are set right, and affection and moral obligation are deepened…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
一家之人焉有不治齊哉聖人示人體易之意
至明切矣雖然謹言行者固脩身之要而身也
者實家國天下之本能脩其身則推之无不準
動之无不化國以之而治天下以之而平不但
家齊而已故孟子曰君子之守脩其身而天下
平
是故蓍之德圓而神卦之德方以知六爻
之義易以貢聖人以此洗心退藏於密
吉凶與民同患神以知來知以藏往其
===
孰能與於此哉古之聰明叡知神武而
不殺者夫是以明於天之道而察於民
之故是興神物以前民用聖人以此齋
戒以神明其德夫
張子渭
同考試官訓導黄　批〔說聖人以易窮理與作易用易處〕〔貫徹無遺工於易者也宜冠本房〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔造理精潔可取〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔通暢得旨〕
punctuated:
一家之人焉有不治齊哉？聖人示人體易之意，至明切矣。雖然，謹言行者固脩身之要，而身也者，實家國天下之本。能脩其身，則推之无不準，動之无不化，國以之而治，天下以之而平，不但家齊而已。故孟子曰：「君子之守，脩其身而天下平。」
是故蓍之德圓而神，卦之德方以知，六爻之義易以貢。聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往，其孰能與於此哉？古之聰明叡知、神武而不殺者夫！是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。聖人以此齋戒，以神明其德夫！
張子渭
同考試官訓導黄　批〔說聖人以易窮理與作易用易處，貫徹無遺，工於易者也，宜冠本房。〕〔〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔造理精潔，可取。〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔通暢得旨。〕
translation_en:
…how could the members of a single family fail to be well governed and brought into order? The sage’s intention in teaching people to embody the Changes is perfectly clear and explicit. Nevertheless, although care in speech and conduct is essential to cultivating oneself, the self is truly the foundation of the family, the state, and all under Heaven. If one can cultivate oneself, then wherever one extends this cultivation, it accords with the proper standard; wherever one acts, transformation follows. Through it the state is governed and all under Heaven is brought to peace—not merely the family brought into order. Thus Mengzi said: “What the gentleman holds to is cultivating himself, and all under Heaven is brought to peace.”
“Therefore, the virtue of the milfoil stalks is round and numinous; the virtue of the hexagrams is square and wise; and the significance of the six lines lies in changing and providing guidance. With these the sage cleanses his heart and withdraws into hidden profundity, sharing with the people their concern over good and ill fortune. Through numinous insight he knows what is to come; through wisdom he preserves what has gone before. Who could attain this? Surely those of antiquity who were perceptive, discerning, sagacious, and wise, possessed of numinous martial power yet not killing! Thus they understood the Way of Heaven and discerned the circumstances of the people, and so brought forth these numinous objects to guide the people’s use of them. With these the sage purifies himself and observes abstinence, making his virtue numinous and enlightened!”
Zhang Ziwei.
Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “His discussion of how the sage uses the Changes to fathom principles, and of his composing and employing the Changes, is thorough and leaves nothing out. He is accomplished in the Changes and should rank first in this examining room.”
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “His exploration of principles is refined and lucid; worthy of selection.”
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “Fluent and clear, and captures the essential meaning.”

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
易具於聖人而有作易之本易作於聖人而極
用易之妙甚矣聖人之心易理之所具也旣具
此理以爲之本則夫作易以妙其用者抑豈外
於此哉且夫易非聖人不能作亦非聖人不能
用而其所以作易則有其本焉是故蓍乃神物
也變化无方其德則圓而神卦乃易象也事有
定理其德則方以知以至效天下之動者爻也
六爻之義變易告人非易以貢乎聖人體具三
者之德而无一塵之累方其无事也則退藏於
===
至靜之中而人莫測其機收斂於至密之地而
人莫窺其妙及其有事也吉欲民趨凶欲民避
惟患趨避之不知知來以神藏往以知隨其所
感而必應是可謂得夫蓍卦爻之理而不假夫
蓍卦爻之物矣其孰能與於此哉惟古之聰明
天賦叡知夙成之聖存其神武而不假殺伐之
器者能之也聖人具所以作易之本如此是以
上焉天道如陰陽消長之理无一而不明下焉
人事如云爲吉凶之故无一而不察明天道故
punctuated: 易具於聖人，而有作易之本；易作於聖人，而極用易之妙。甚矣，聖人之心，易理之所具也！旣具此理以爲之本，則夫作易以妙其用者，抑豈外於此哉？且夫易非聖人不能作，亦非聖人不能用，而其所以作易，則有其本焉。是故蓍乃神物也，變化无方，其德則圓而神；卦乃易象也，事有定理，其德則方以知。以至效天下之動者，爻也。六爻之義，變易告人，非易以貢乎？聖人體具三者之德，而无一塵之累。方其无事也，則退藏於至靜之中，而人莫測其機；收斂於至密之地，而人莫窺其妙。及其有事也，吉欲民趨，凶欲民避，惟患趨避之不知。知來以神，藏往以知，隨其所感而必應。是可謂得夫蓍卦爻之理，而不假夫蓍卦爻之物矣。其孰能與於此哉？惟古之聰明天賦、叡知夙成之聖，存其神武而不假殺伐之器者，能之也。聖人具所以作易之本如此，是以上焉天道，如陰陽消長之理，无一而不明；下焉人事，如云爲吉凶之故，无一而不察。明天道，故
translation_en: The Changes is fully present within the sage, providing the foundation for composing the Changes; composed by the sage, the Changes realizes the utmost subtlety of its application. How profound it is that the sage’s mind contains the principles of the Changes! Since these principles are already present as its foundation, how could composing the Changes to achieve its wondrous application lie outside them? Only a sage can compose the Changes, and only a sage can employ it; yet his ability to compose it has a foundation. Thus, milfoil is a numinous thing: its transformations have no fixed direction, and its potency is round and numinous. Hexagrams are the images of the Changes: affairs have determinate principles, and their potency is square and knowing. As for what models the movements of all under Heaven, these are the lines. The meanings of the six lines inform people through their changes: do they not thereby readily disclose things? The sage embodies the potencies of all three, unburdened by even a speck of dust. When there is no affair to address, he withdraws into utter stillness, and no one can fathom his workings; he gathers himself into the deepest concealment, and no one can glimpse his subtlety. When affairs arise, he wishes the people to pursue good fortune and avoid misfortune, concerned only that they may not know what to pursue and what to avoid. Through numinous insight he knows what is to come; through wisdom he stores what has passed. Whatever moves him invariably elicits a response. This may be called possessing the principles of milfoil, hexagrams, and lines without relying on those things themselves. Who could attain this? Only the sages of antiquity, whose perceptiveness was Heaven-given and whose sagely wisdom matured early, could do so: they possessed numinous martial power without resorting to instruments of killing and warfare. Such was the foundation the sages possessed for composing the Changes. Therefore, above, in the Way of Heaven, there was nothing they did not comprehend, such as the principles governing the waxing and waning of yin and yang; below, in human affairs, there was nothing they did not discern, such as the causes of good and ill fortune in speech and action. They comprehended the Way of Heaven, and therefore…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
知神物之可興察民故故知民用所當前于是
興蓍之神物而立夫揲之之法以前吾人李至
之吉凶興龜之神物而制爲鑽之之法以先斯
民未來之趨避聖人既作易以教人豈但已哉
又於此焉湛然純一而致齋以考其占使吾之
清明在躬亦如鬼神之能知來也肅然警惕而
致戒以稽其占使吾之志氣如神亦若蓍龜之
能前知也如此可謂極用易之妙矣是知易之
未作而其理已具於聖人之心易之既作而其
理亦不外於聖人之心聖人其有心之易乎雖
然易爲卜筮之書卜筮未立易在造化而具於
聖人卜筮既立易在卜筮而周於民用天下之
志以通天下之業以定天下之疑以斷厥功大
矣彼以卜筮小吾易者烏足以語此
書
輯五瑞既月乃日覲四岳羣牧班瑞于羣
后
===
羅循
punctuated:
知神物之可興，察民故，故知民用所當前。于是興蓍之神物，而立夫揲之之法，以前吾人李至之吉凶；興龜之神物，而制爲鑽之之法，以先斯民未來之趨避。聖人既作易以教人，豈但已哉？又於此焉湛然純一而致齋，以考其占，使吾之清明在躬，亦如鬼神之能知來也；肅然警惕而致戒，以稽其占，使吾之志氣如神，亦若蓍龜之能前知也。如此，可謂極用易之妙矣。是知易之未作，而其理已具於聖人之心；易之既作，而其理亦不外於聖人之心。聖人其有心之易乎？雖然，易爲卜筮之書，卜筮未立，易在造化而具於聖人；卜筮既立，易在卜筮而周於民用。天下之志以通，天下之業以定，天下之疑以斷，厥功大矣！彼以卜筮小吾易者，烏足以語此？

書

輯五瑞，既月乃日，覲四岳羣牧，班瑞于羣后。

羅循
translation_en:
…he knew that the numinous objects could be brought into use; by examining the circumstances of the people, he knew what needed to be anticipated for their use. Thus he brought into use the numinous milfoil and established the method of counting its stalks, to foretell the good and ill fortune awaiting us [?]; he brought into use the numinous tortoise and devised the method of drilling its shell, to anticipate what the people should pursue or avoid in the future. Having made the Changes to instruct people, could the sage simply stop there? He further attained serene purity and singleness of mind through ritual purification, to examine its prognostications, so that his own embodied clarity could know what was to come, just as ghosts and spirits could. With solemn vigilance he exercised ritual caution to scrutinize its prognostications, making his purpose and vital energies numinous, capable of foreknowledge like the milfoil and tortoise. This may be called realizing to the utmost the subtle efficacy of using the Changes.

We thus know that, before the Changes was made, its principles were already complete in the sage’s mind; after it was made, its principles likewise remained within the sage’s mind. Did the sage not possess a Changes within his mind? Nevertheless, the Changes is a book of divination by tortoise shell and milfoil. Before these forms of divination were established, the Changes existed in the processes of creation and transformation and was fully embodied in the sage. Once they were established, the Changes resided in divination and extended to every practical need of the people. Through it, the purposes of all under Heaven were brought into communication, their undertakings were settled, and their doubts resolved. Great indeed was its achievement! How could those who belittle our Changes because it concerns divination be qualified to discuss this?

Book of Documents

“He gathered the five tokens of jade. When the month was over, he then, on the appointed day, received in audience the Four Overseers of the Peaks and the various regional governors, and distributed the jade tokens to the assembled lords.”

Luo Xun

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭郭　批〔塲中率以斂玉頒玉分析作義其於徵諸侯盡詢察隨先後以與正始之意皆畧而〕
〔不講惟此篇辭氣豊贍形容殆盡可嘉可嘉〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔言廣廷統御諸侯氣象宛然〕
〔在目〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔義整齊而氣亦舂容〕
聖人徵諸侯必詳於詢察而與之正始也蓋天
下不可一日無統也聖人於諸侯旣徵之詢之
而復與之正始焉其所以統御之者一何至哉
===
昔史臣紀大舜於攝位之初行朝覲之事意謂
人君之錫命也有五等之爵諸侯之受命也有
五等之圭若桓圭若信圭若躬圭公侯伯之所
執者也今則發綸音而輯之于以徵其來朝若
穀璧若蒲璧子男之所執者也今則渙大命而
斂之于以召其入覲夫國有大小固皆以一時
斂而地有遠近不能以一時來故旣盡正月則
四方之諸侯有至者矣至則日日見之而詢察
之致詳無遠無近一瑁冒圭頭之斜銳而刻之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭郭批〔塲中率以斂玉、頒玉分析作義，其於徵諸侯、盡詢察、隨先後以與正始之意，皆畧而不講。惟此篇辭氣豊贍，形容殆盡，可嘉！可嘉！〕
考試官教諭羅批〔言廣廷統御諸侯氣象，宛然在目。〕
考試官教諭孫批〔義整齊而氣亦舂容。〕
聖人徵諸侯，必詳於詢察，而與之正始也。蓋天下不可一日無統也。聖人於諸侯，旣徵之、詢之，而復與之正始焉，其所以統御之者，一何至哉！
昔史臣紀大舜於攝位之初行朝覲之事，意謂人君之錫命也，有五等之爵；諸侯之受命也，有五等之圭。若桓圭，若信圭，若躬圭，公、侯、伯之所執者也。今則發綸音而輯之，于以徵其來朝；若穀璧，若蒲璧，子、男之所執者也。今則渙大命而斂之，于以召其入覲。夫國有大小，固皆以一時斂，而地有遠近，不能以一時來。故旣盡正月，則四方之諸侯有至者矣。至則日日見之，而詢察之致詳。無遠無近，一瑁冒圭頭之斜銳，而刻之
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor: 〔Candidates generally divide their interpretation into the collection and redistribution of jade tokens. They all pass over without discussion the purposes of summoning the feudal lords, questioning and examining them fully, and giving them a proper new beginning in order of arrival. This essay alone is rich in expression and ample in scope, describing these matters almost exhaustively. Commendable! Commendable!〕
Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: 〔Its account vividly brings before our eyes the scene of governing the feudal lords in the great court.〕
Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: 〔The argument is orderly, and its expression is also measured and expansive.〕
When the sage summons the feudal lords, he must question and examine them thoroughly and give them a proper new beginning. For All-under-Heaven cannot go a single day without unified authority. Having summoned and questioned the feudal lords, the sage then gives them a proper new beginning. How consummate are his means of governing them!
In former times, the court historian recorded how the great Shun conducted court audiences when he first assumed the regency. The meaning was this: when the ruler confers appointments, there are five ranks of nobility; when the feudal lords receive their appointments, there are five grades of jade tablets. The huan, xin, and gong tablets are those held by dukes, marquises, and earls. Now he issues his royal words and gathers these tokens, thereby summoning their holders to court. The grain-patterned and rush-patterned jade discs are those held by viscounts and barons. Now he promulgates his great command and collects these tokens, thereby summoning their holders to an audience. Although their states differ in size, the tokens are all to be collected at the same time; but because their territories lie at different distances, they cannot all arrive at the same time. Thus, once the first month has ended, some of the feudal lords from the four quarters have arrived. As they arrive, he receives them day by day, questioning and examining them with the utmost thoroughness. Whether they come from far or near, he uses a jade gauge, the mao, to fit over the sloping, pointed heads of their tablets, and their incised markings …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
長短於是乎别焉九州之牧伯有來者矣來則
日日覲之而考覈之必審無小無大一皆合瑞
玉之符信而刻之廣狹於是乎驗焉既見之後
審知非僞則桓也信也躬也穀也載須于陛辭之項
穀也蒲也載錫于言旋之時來之先者須之先
與之正始而飭遣就國使知統御之有在來之
後者須之後與之更始而往即乃封使知宰制
之有歸天下之耳目自是而一新天下之心志
自是而一定聖人撫世酬物居重馭輕之道有
===
如是乎抑是玉也舜既驗之於攝位之初矣其
後巡狩四方而諸侯復執此以各朝于方岳至
於夏禹南巡塗山之會諸侯執玉而來者萬國
是知玉者人臣受命于上朝覲會同之所有事
者也君人者之所以示大信於天下可不慎重
之耶後世以玉爲節篆刻文字而中分之彼此
各藏其半有故則左右相合以爲信者亦其遺
意也
乃有室大競顯俊尊上帝
punctuated:
長短，於是乎别焉。九州之牧伯有來者矣，來則日日覲之，而考覈之必審。無小無大，一皆合瑞玉之符信，而刻之廣狹，於是乎驗焉。既見之後，審知非僞，則桓也、信也、躬也、穀也，載須于陛辭之項；穀也、蒲也，載錫于言旋之時。來之先者，須之先，與之正始，而飭遣就國，使知統御之有在；來之後者，須之後，與之更始，而往即乃封，使知宰制之有歸。天下之耳目，自是而一新；天下之心志，自是而一定。聖人撫世酬物、居重馭輕之道，有如是乎！抑是玉也，舜既驗之於攝位之初矣。其後巡狩四方，而諸侯復執此以各朝于方岳。至於夏禹南巡，塗山之會，諸侯執玉而來者萬國。是知玉者，人臣受命于上、朝覲會同之所有事者也。君人者之所以示大信於天下，可不慎重之耶？後世以玉爲節，篆刻文字而中分之，彼此各藏其半，有故則左右相合以爲信者，亦其遺意也。

乃有室大競，顯俊尊上帝。
translation_en:
…the lengths of their carved portions were thereby distinguished. When the regional lords of the Nine Provinces arrived, he received them in audience day after day, taking utmost care in examining and verifying their credentials. Whether their domains were small or great, all had their jade tokens of authority matched for authentication; the widths of their carved portions were thereby verified. After receiving them and ascertaining that their credentials were genuine, the huan, xin, gong, and gu jade tokens were held pending their farewell audience [?]; the gu and pu jade disks were bestowed when they set out for home. Those who arrived first were attended to first [?]: he gave them a proper new beginning and formally dispatched them to their states, so that they would know where supreme authority lay. Those who arrived later were attended to later [?]: he granted them a fresh beginning and sent them to their fiefs, so that they would know the source of sovereign control. Thus all under Heaven saw and heard things anew, and their hearts and purposes became settled in unity. Such was the sage’s way of tending the world and responding to affairs, occupying the position of paramount authority and directing those subordinate to him!

Now Shun had already verified these jades when he first assumed the regency. Later, when he made inspection tours through the four quarters, the regional lords again carried them to attend his audiences at the sacred mountain of each region. When Yu of the Xia toured the south and held the assembly at Tushan, lords from ten thousand states came bearing jade. Thus we know that jade was used by subjects when receiving authority from above and when attending court audiences and assemblies. It was the means by which the ruler demonstrated his great trustworthiness to all under Heaven: could he fail to treat it with the utmost care? In later ages, jade was used for credentials, inscribed in seal script and divided in two, with each party retaining one half. When occasion required, the left and right halves were fitted together as authentication. This, too, preserved the intention of the ancient practice.

“Then the ruling house grew greatly strong, promoted men of outstanding talent, and honored the Lord on High.”

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
史紀
同考試官教諭郭　批〔言詞平正有不盡之意〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔詞語豐贍不為題意所窘其〕
善作者乎
考試官教諭孫　批〔能言大禹事天之意可嘉〕
當國家之極盛而求賢以事天惟前王然也夫
賢才乃天生之以遺人國者也然則當國家極
盛之時而求賢以為事天之實非前王之知恤
能然乎昔周公戒成王以任用賢才之道至此
===
乃舉有夏知恤之君以告之謂夫有夏之時文
命四敷聲教訖于無外矣㢸成五服封疆至於
無際矣巡狩舉也來塗山之會者殆萬國其多
征伐行也感有苗之格者殆七旬其速九功惟
叙而天下之大皆不距於朕行九叙惟歌而億
兆之衆皆無有乎反側庶土之財賦納于王畿
者蓋異地而同心遠夷之貢篚入于王國者蓋
殊方而一志王室之大彊有如此斯時也有夏
之君以為明明在朝百官若脩輔矣而三事之
punctuated:
史紀
同考試官教諭郭批〔言詞平正，有不盡之意。〕
考試官教諭羅批〔詞語豐贍，不為題意所窘，其〕善作者乎！
考試官教諭孫批〔能言大禹事天之意，可嘉。〕
當國家之極盛，而求賢以事天，惟前王然也。夫賢才，乃天生之以遺人國者也。然則當國家極盛之時，而求賢以為事天之實，非前王之知恤，能然乎？昔周公戒成王以任用賢才之道，至此乃舉有夏知恤之君以告之，謂夫有夏之時，文命四敷，聲教訖于無外矣；㢸成五服，封疆至於無際矣。巡狩舉也，來塗山之會者，殆萬國其多；征伐行也，感有苗之格者，殆七旬其速。九功惟叙，而天下之大皆不距於朕行；九叙惟歌，而億兆之衆皆無有乎反側。庶土之財賦納于王畿者，蓋異地而同心；遠夷之貢篚入于王國者，蓋殊方而一志。王室之大彊有如此。斯時也，有夏之君以為明明在朝，百官若脩輔矣，而三事之
translation_en:
Shi Ji 史紀

Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor: “The language is balanced and correct, with meaning extending beyond what is explicitly said.”

Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: “The diction is rich and ample, unconstrained by the meaning of the topic. Surely he is an accomplished writer!”

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: “He succeeds in expressing the intention with which Yu the Great served Heaven. This deserves praise.”

To seek worthy men in order to serve Heaven when the state was at the very height of prosperity—such was the conduct of the former kings alone. Worthy and talented men are born of Heaven as gifts to human states. Thus, to seek worthy men at the height of a state's prosperity as the substantive means of serving Heaven—could this have been achieved without the former kings' understanding of care and concern? Formerly, the Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng concerning the way to employ worthy and talented men. At this point, he cited a ruler of Xia who understood such concern, telling him that in the time of Xia, civil virtue and commands spread in all four directions, and the influence of its teachings reached everywhere, leaving nothing outside. The five service zones were established [?], and the realm's boundaries extended without limit. When inspection tours were undertaken, those who came to the assembly at Tushan numbered as many as ten thousand states. When punitive campaigns were conducted, the people of Youmiao were moved to submit in as short a time as seventy days. The nine achievements were duly ordered, and throughout the vast realm none opposed ‘my conduct.’ The ordering of those nine achievements was celebrated in song, and among the countless people none were disloyal or unsettled. The wealth and taxes of the various lands were delivered to the royal domain: though their lands differed, their hearts were one. The tribute baskets of distant foreign peoples entered the royal kingdom: though their regions differed, their purpose was one. Such was the greatness and strength of the royal house.

At this time, the ruler of Xia considered that illustrious men stood at court and the hundred officials seemed to be diligently providing assistance; yet, of the three affairs …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
長所繫尤重也可不慎擇其人乎濟濟在廷羣
后若德讓矣而三宅之官所任尤難也可不旁
求其人乎由是顯于有位惟克俊之是舉揚于
側陋惟即俊之是求以之任天事也以之子天
民也以之守天法也而所以尊乎上帝者無貳
爾心焉與之共天位也與之治天職也與之食
天祿也而所以事乎上帝者不遺餘力焉嚴敬
奉持之心常存於夢寐得賢之頃齊明盛服之
念不忘于側席見賢之時王者之事天有如此
===
吁不以國家之極盛爲已足而以賢俊之當顯
爲未至此有夏之君所以爲不可幾及也今王
可不知所重哉嗟夫成王賢君也周公作立政
以戒之既舉禹湯文武得人之盛復言夏桀商
紂用人之非至於篇終則又以去憸人用吉士
爲言蓋公之意以成王爲守成之主也使用人
一有所失則必將有如暴德罔後帝欽罰之之
者矣故舉得人之盛者欲其以先王知恤爲法
也言用人之非者欲其以夏商〔䲭〕〔亚〕不知恤爲
punctuated:
長所繫尤重也，可不慎擇其人乎？濟濟在廷，羣后若德讓矣，而三宅之官所任尤難也，可不旁求其人乎？由是顯于有位，惟克俊之是舉；揚于側陋，惟即俊之是求。以之任天事也，以之子天民也，以之守天法也，而所以尊乎上帝者，無貳爾心焉。與之共天位也，與之治天職也，與之食天祿也，而所以事乎上帝者，不遺餘力焉。嚴敬奉持之心，常存於夢寐得賢之頃；齊明盛服之念，不忘于側席見賢之時。王者之事天有如此。
吁！不以國家之極盛爲已足，而以賢俊之當顯爲未至，此有夏之君所以爲不可幾及也。今王可不知所重哉？嗟夫！成王，賢君也。周公作《立政》以戒之，既舉禹湯文武得人之盛，復言夏桀商紂用人之非。至於篇終，則又以去憸人、用吉士爲言。蓋公之意，以成王爲守成之主也。使用人一有所失，則必將有如「暴德罔後，帝欽罰之」之者矣。故舉得人之盛者，欲其以先王知恤爲法也；言用人之非者，欲其以夏商〔䲭〕〔亚〕不知恤爲
translation_en:
…the heads of the three principal services bear especially weighty responsibilities: could he fail to choose their holders carefully? The many lords assembled at court seemed virtuous and deferential, yet the duties entrusted to the three principal offices were especially difficult: could he fail to search widely for suitable men? Thus, when advancing those already in office, he promoted only men capable of recognizing outstanding talent; when raising men from humble obscurity, he sought only those who drew close to outstanding talent. He employed them to undertake Heaven’s affairs, to nurture Heaven’s people as his children, and to uphold Heaven’s laws. In honoring the Lord on High, they were to have no divided loyalty. He shared Heaven’s positions with them, administered Heaven’s duties with them, and enjoyed Heaven’s emoluments with them. In serving the Lord on High, they spared no effort. His solemn, reverent devotion remained with him even when he dreamed of finding worthy men; his resolve to be purified, discerning, and properly robed never left him when he sat expectantly awaiting an audience with the worthy. Such was this king’s service to Heaven.
Ah! He did not regard the utmost prosperity of his state as sufficient, but felt that he had not yet done enough to bring worthy and outstanding men to prominence. This is why the ruler of Xia was almost beyond emulation. Can the present king fail to know what deserves priority? Alas! King Cheng was a worthy ruler. The Duke of Zhou composed “Establishing Government” to admonish him. Having cited the flourishing success of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu in obtaining suitable men, he also spoke of the errors of Jie of Xia and Zhou of Shang in employing men. At the chapter’s end, he again urged the dismissal of crafty men and the employment of good men. The duke’s intention reflected his view of King Cheng as a ruler charged with preserving an inherited achievement. Should he make even a single error in employing men, there would surely follow a case like that described in the words, “His conduct was violent, and he had no successors; the Lord on High sternly punished him.” Thus, in citing flourishing examples of obtaining suitable men, he wished the king to take as his model the former kings’ understanding of the need for care. In speaking of errors in employing men, he wished him to take the failure of Xia and Shang 〔䲭〕〔亚〕 [annotations unclear: ?] to understand the need for care as …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
監也老成事少主忠愛之心如此此噫三代而下
有君如是其忍負之可勝歎𢪔
詩
其車三千師干之試
楊椮
同考試官訓導談　批〔字義森然氣象雄壯眞王者　藹金之師也捧誦令人凜然〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔形容方叔車徒之盛不浮不　艶足以超諸作矣〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔文整氣昌蓋必熟於經學者　宜取以魁多士〕
===
詩人於大將南征必極道其車徒之盛焉蓋兵
事所尚則威也大將之威而備見於車徒宜詩
人咏以爲言也歟昔宣王之時蠻荊背叛王命
方叔南征故詩人作此謂夫出師必以車車焉
不盛不足以言戰方叔涖止其車何如其盛邪
戎車既飭如霆如雷馳驅於新田菑畝之間嘽
嘽乎三千其衆也戎車既駕如輊如軒閒闗於
punctuated:
監也。老成事少主，忠愛之心如此此。噫！三代而下，有君如是，其忍負之？可勝歎𢪔！

詩
其車三千，師干之試。
楊椮
同考試官訓導談　批〔字義森然，氣象雄壯，眞王者　藹金之師也。捧誦令人凜然。〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔形容方叔車徒之盛，不浮不　艶，足以超諸作矣。〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔文整氣昌，蓋必熟於經學者，宜取以魁多士。〕

詩人於大將南征，必極道其車徒之盛焉。蓋兵事所尚則威也，大將之威而備見於車徒，宜詩人咏以爲言也歟！昔宣王之時，蠻荊背叛，王命方叔南征，故詩人作此。謂夫出師必以車，車焉不盛，不足以言戰。方叔涖止，其車何如其盛邪？戎車既飭，如霆如雷，馳驅於新田菑畝之間，嘽嘽乎三千，其衆也！戎車既駕，如輊如軒，閒闗於
translation_en:
…as a warning. Such was the loyal devotion of an experienced elder serving a young ruler [the final 此 is repeated]. Alas! After the Three Dynasties, if one had such a ruler, how could one bear to fail him? How could one sigh enough over this [?]!

Book of Odes
“His chariots numbered three thousand; his hosts and shields were put to use.”
Yang Sen 楊椮
Associate Examiner Tan, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “The wording and meaning are imposingly ordered, the bearing grand and powerful: truly the army of a true king, ‘ai jin’ [?]. Holding and reciting this essay inspires awe.”
Examiner Luo, an Instructor, comments: “It describes the magnificence of Fang Shu’s chariots and troops without superficiality or ornamentation. It is sufficient to surpass the other compositions.”
Examiner Sun, an Instructor, comments: “The composition is orderly and its spirit abundant. Its author must surely be well versed in classical learning; he should be selected to head the many candidates.”

When the poet describes the great commander’s southern campaign, he necessarily recounts to the utmost the magnificence of his chariots and troops. For what military affairs prize is awe-inspiring power, and the great commander’s power is fully displayed in his chariots and troops. Surely it is fitting that the poet should sing of these! Formerly, in the time of King Xuan, the Man of Jing rebelled, and the king ordered Fang Shu to campaign southward. Thus the poet composed these lines. They mean that dispatching an army necessarily requires chariots; unless the chariots are abundant, one cannot speak of battle. When Fang Shu arrived, how magnificent were his chariots? The war chariots, already put in order, were like thunderbolts and thunder, racing among newly cultivated fields and newly reclaimed plots. In their multitude they numbered three thousand—how numerous they were! The war chariots, already harnessed, dipped forward and tilted back, rumbling along …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遠者近郊之外烝烝乎三千其多也輕車重車
前後相襲不但元戎十乘而已臨車衝車遠近
相續不但革車三百而已車之盛也如此吾知
所至無敵所謂有不攻攻必取者有矣有車必
有徒徒焉不盛不足以威敵方叔涖止其徒何
如其盛邪我師我旅奮武以扞外者一皆教閱
有素而肄習乎坐作進退之節我徒我御畜勇
以待戰者一皆訓練有常而夙閑乎攻殺擊刺
之方或為甲士或為步卒貔貅山立無失伍也
===
或以御輕或以將重介冑雲屯無離次也徒之
盛也如此吾知所向無前所謂有不戰戰必勝
者有矣吁車盛則有無敵之勢徒盛則無可乘
之隙此所以雖未至蠻荊之地而風聲氣焰先
已懾其心矣不戰而收來威之功宜乎抑考先
王之於夷狄也撫之以仁馭之以義雖獻琛納
贄而不弛圉守雖跋扈跳梁而不事窮追故玁
狁內侵而文武之吉甫止於薄伐蠻荊背叛而
元老之方叔但使來威後世不知乎此以雄才
punctuated: 遠者近郊之外，烝烝乎三千其多也。輕車重車，前後相襲，不但元戎十乘而已；臨車衝車，遠近相續，不但革車三百而已。車之盛也如此，吾知所至無敵，所謂有不攻，攻必取者有矣。有車必有徒，徒焉不盛，不足以威敵。方叔涖止，其徒何如其盛邪？我師我旅，奮武以扞外者，一皆教閱有素，而肄習乎坐作進退之節；我徒我御，畜勇以待戰者，一皆訓練有常，而夙閑乎攻殺擊刺之方。或為甲士，或為步卒，貔貅山立，無失伍也；或以御輕，或以將重，介冑雲屯，無離次也。徒之盛也如此，吾知所向無前，所謂有不戰，戰必勝者有矣。吁！車盛則有無敵之勢，徒盛則無可乘之隙。此所以雖未至蠻荊之地，而風聲氣焰先已懾其心矣。不戰而收來威之功，宜乎！抑考先王之於夷狄也，撫之以仁，馭之以義，雖獻琛納贄而不弛圉守，雖跋扈跳梁而不事窮追。故玁狁內侵，而文武之吉甫止於薄伐；蠻荊背叛，而元老之方叔但使來威。後世不知乎此，以雄才
translation_en: …beyond the distant and nearby outskirts [?], a multitude of three thousand! Light chariots and heavy chariots follow one another, front and rear: there are more than merely ten great war chariots. Overlooking chariots and assault chariots form an unbroken succession, far and near: there are more than merely three hundred leather-armored chariots. Such is the strength of the chariots that I know they will meet no match wherever they go. Here indeed is what is meant by: “They may refrain from attacking, but whenever they attack, they take their objective.” Where there are chariots, there must be troops; unless the troops are strong, they cannot overawe the enemy. When Fang Shu arrives, how magnificent are his troops! Our armies and our brigades, exerting their martial strength to ward off external enemies, have all long been instructed and reviewed, and have practiced the prescribed movements of sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating. Our foot soldiers and our charioteers, storing up their courage for battle, have all trained regularly and long been versed in the methods of assault, killing, striking, and thrusting. Some are armored warriors, others infantrymen: fierce as wild beasts, they stand like mountains, none straying from his squad. Some drive the light chariots, others command the heavy ones: armored and helmeted, they mass like clouds, none leaving his position. Such is the strength of the troops that I know no one can stand before them wherever they turn. Here indeed is what is meant by: “They may refrain from fighting, but whenever they fight, they win.” Ah! Strong chariots give them an invincible advantage; strong troops leave no opening for the enemy to exploit. Thus, even before they reach the lands of the Man and Jing, their reputation and formidable bearing have already struck fear into those peoples’ hearts. It is fitting that they should bring them into awed submission without fighting! Now consider how the former kings dealt with the Yi and Di: they soothed them with benevolence and governed them with righteousness. Even when these peoples presented treasures and offerings, the kings did not relax their frontier defenses; even when they acted defiantly and ran rampant, the kings did not pursue them to exhaustion. Thus, when the Xianyun invaded, Jifu, accomplished in both civil and military affairs, confined himself to a limited punitive expedition; when the Man and Jing rebelled, the elder statesman Fang Shu merely brought them into awed submission. Later generations did not understand this; with outstanding talent…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
大畧之君而專事窮兵以龍姿日表之主而甘
爲可汗使輪臺之詔不下遼東之役未息竟不
知其何如也嗚呼吾於是有取乎宣王
經營四方告成于王四方旣平王國庶定
時靡有爭王心載寧江漢之滸王命召
虎式辟四方徹我疆土匪疚匪棘王國
來極于疆于理至于南海王命召虎來
旬來宣文武受命召公維翰無曰予小
子召公是似肇敏戎公用錫爾祉釐爾
圭瓚秬鬯一卣告于文人錫山土田于
周受命自召祖命
===
同考試官訓導談　批〔約鍊詳簡而文理充足此必〕
明經之士高薦何忝
羅琛
考試官教諭羅　批〔融會詩人大意而一時成功〕
報功之盛藹然可見
考試官教諭孫　批〔鋪叙齊整意脉流通非老筆〕
不能到此
punctuated:
大畧之君而專事窮兵，以龍姿日表之主而甘爲可汗，使輪臺之詔不下，遼東之役未息，竟不知其何如也。嗚呼！吾於是有取乎宣王。
經營四方，告成于王。四方旣平，王國庶定。時靡有爭，王心載寧。江漢之滸，王命召虎：「式辟四方，徹我疆土。匪疚匪棘，王國來極。于疆于理，至于南海。」王命召虎：「來旬來宣。文武受命，召公維翰。無曰予小子，召公是似。肇敏戎公，用錫爾祉。釐爾圭瓚，秬鬯一卣，告于文人。錫山土田，于周受命，自召祖命。」
同考試官訓導談批〔約鍊詳簡，而文理充足，此必〕明經之士，高薦何忝！
羅琛
考試官教諭羅批〔融會詩人大意，而一時成功〕報功之盛，藹然可見。
考試官教諭孫批〔鋪叙齊整，意脉流通，非老筆〕不能到此。
translation_en:
…rulers of great strategic ability devoted themselves exclusively to exhausting their military resources, while a sovereign with a dragon’s bearing and the sun’s countenance willingly became a khan. Had the edict of Luntai not been issued, and had the campaigns in Liaodong not ceased, there is no knowing how matters would ultimately have turned out. Ah! Herein lies my reason for approving of King Xuan.
He brought order to the four quarters and reported his accomplishment to the king. With the four quarters pacified, the royal realm was at last secure. There was no longer contention, and the king’s heart was at peace. On the banks of the Jiang and Han rivers, the king commanded Shao Hu: “Open up the four quarters and establish the boundaries of our lands. Neither cause distress nor act with undue haste; let the royal realm be their guiding standard. Mark out the boundaries and put the lands in order, as far as the Southern Sea.” The king commanded Shao Hu: “Come, make your rounds and proclaim my commands. When Wen and Wu received the Mandate, the Duke of Shao was their mainstay. Do not say, ‘I am but a young man’; emulate the Duke of Shao. Begin diligently to perform your great service, and I shall bestow blessings upon you. I grant you a jade-handled libation ladle and a vessel of black-millet sacrificial wine, to announce this to your cultivated ancestor. I grant you mountains and fields. Receive your command at Zhou, continuing the charge of your ancestor, the Duke of Shao.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor: “Concise and refined, judicious in detail and brevity, yet fully developed in its literary reasoning: this must be a scholar thoroughly versed in the Classics. What could be undeserved in recommending him highly?”
Luo Chen
Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: “The poet’s main meaning is comprehensively grasped; the splendor of the achievement and its reward on that occasion is vividly apparent.”
Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: “The exposition is orderly and well arranged, and the train of thought flows smoothly. Only a seasoned writer could attain this level.”

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
詩人美世臣成平夷之功必備述王者厚報功
之典蓋歴賞所以報大功也今世臣平夷而克
成其功王者厚褒賞以報之不亦宜乎昔宣王
命召穆公平淮南之夷詩人美之至此謂夫淮
夷來求所以經營四方也其功既集穆公則歸
告于王庭焉淮夷來鋪所以經營四國也厥績
既成穆公則入奏于天子焉王國以四方為安
危四方既平則王國其庶定矣王心以天下為
憂樂時靡有爭則王心其載寧矣江漢既平王
===
又命召虎以為四方之侵地未闢也爾其闢之
四方之疆土未徹也爾其徹之然非以病乎民
也惟欲其取正於王國非以急其欲也惟欲其
歸極於我周於是遂疆之以正其大界盡南海
而止焉遂理之以別其條理極海濵而已焉夫
以穆公之成功如此則宣王之報功當何如邪
又言王命召虎來此江漢于以徧治乎王事于
以敷布乎王命而曰昔我文王受命惟爾祖召
公為翰今女無曰以予小子之故但自為嗣女
punctuated: 詩人美世臣成平夷之功，必備述王者厚報功之典，蓋歴賞所以報大功也。今世臣平夷而克成其功，王者厚褒賞以報之，不亦宜乎？昔宣王命召穆公平淮南之夷，詩人美之，至此謂夫淮夷來求，所以經營四方也。其功既集，穆公則歸告于王庭焉。淮夷來鋪，所以經營四國也。厥績既成，穆公則入奏于天子焉。王國以四方為安危，四方既平，則王國其庶定矣。王心以天下為憂樂，時靡有爭，則王心其載寧矣。江漢既平，王又命召虎，以為四方之侵地未闢也，爾其闢之；四方之疆土未徹也，爾其徹之。然非以病乎民也，惟欲其取正於王國；非以急其欲也，惟欲其歸極於我周。於是遂疆之，以正其大界，盡南海而止焉；遂理之，以別其條理，極海濵而已焉。夫以穆公之成功如此，則宣王之報功當何如邪？又言王命召虎來此江漢，于以徧治乎王事，于以敷布乎王命，而曰：「昔我文王受命，惟爾祖召公為翰。今女無曰以予小子之故，但自為嗣女
translation_en:
When the poet praises a hereditary minister for accomplishing the pacification of the Yi peoples, he invariably recounts in full the king’s provisions for generously rewarding merit, for successive rewards recompense great achievements. Now that a hereditary minister has successfully pacified the Yi, is it not fitting that the king should repay him with lavish commendations and rewards? Formerly, King Xuan commanded Duke Mu of Shao to pacify the Yi south of the Huai River, and the poet praised him. At this point, the poem speaks of coming to seek out the Huai Yi, thereby bringing order to the four quarters. Once his achievement was complete, Duke Mu returned to report at the royal court. It speaks of coming to spread authority among the Huai Yi, thereby bringing order to the states of the four quarters. Once his work was accomplished, Duke Mu entered to make his report to the Son of Heaven. The security or peril of the royal realm depends on the four quarters; once they were pacified, the royal realm could surely be settled. The king’s sorrow or joy depends on all under Heaven; when there was no contention, the king’s heart could at last be at peace.

Once the Jiang and Han regions had been pacified, the king further commanded Shao Hu, declaring that lands encroached upon in the four quarters had yet to be opened up: “Open them up.” The territories of the four quarters had yet to be put in order: “Put them in order.” Yet this was not intended to burden the people, but only to have them take their standards from the royal realm; nor was it intended to press for the satisfaction of his desires, but only to have them turn to our Zhou as their supreme standard. Accordingly, he established boundaries to rectify the principal territorial divisions, extending as far as the Southern Sea. He then ordered the land to distinguish its subdivisions, reaching all the way to the seacoast. With Duke Mu’s accomplishments being such, how should King Xuan have rewarded his service?

The poem further says that the king commanded Shao Hu to come to these Jiang and Han regions, there to attend comprehensively to royal affairs and promulgate royal commands. He said: “Formerly, when our King Wen received the Mandate, it was your ancestor, the Duke of Shao, who served as his mainstay. Now do not say that you act for the sake of me, the little child; simply act to carry on your …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
君公之功耳昔我武王為君惟爾祖康公是做
令女無曰以予小子之為但自為纘女康公之
續耳且女能開敏其功以爾祖之事文武者事
我則我當大建厥福以我祖之報康公者報爾
是故報功當推恩也必釐爾圭瓚秬鬯一卣使
得以祀其先祖報功當加地也必告于文人錫
山土田使得以廣其封邑然又使爾往受策命
於岐周從爾祖康公受策命之所以昭爾之世
功也使爾往受冊書於祖廟自其祖康公受冊
===
書之地以彰爾之世美也吁臣有盛大之功君
有盛大之賞此功此賞可謂兩無愧矣大抵人
臣以建功為忠國家以報功為禮故康公有關
國之功而武王封以北燕周公與敦商之功成
王建其元子明良德業之盛卓乎其不可及至
若穆公成經營疆理之功而宣王又有策命寵
錫之厚蓋亦明良相逢功賞交盡真有得祖宗
之家法也噫君臣上下誠意交孚此所以內修
外攘光復舊物而成中興之大業也歟
punctuated:
君公之功耳。昔我武王為君，惟爾祖康公是做。令女無曰以予小子之為，但自為纘女康公之續耳。且女能開敏其功，以爾祖之事文武者事我，則我當大建厥福，以我祖之報康公者報爾。是故報功當推恩也，必釐爾圭瓚、秬鬯一卣，使得以祀其先祖；報功當加地也，必告于文人，錫山土田，使得以廣其封邑。然又使爾往受策命於岐周，從爾祖康公受策命之所，以昭爾之世功也；使爾往受冊書於祖廟，自其祖康公受冊書之地，以彰爾之世美也。
吁！臣有盛大之功，君有盛大之賞，此功此賞，可謂兩無愧矣。大抵人臣以建功為忠，國家以報功為禮。故康公有關國之功，而武王封以北燕；周公與敦商之功，成王建其元子。明良德業之盛，卓乎其不可及！至若穆公成經營疆理之功，而宣王又有策命寵錫之厚，蓋亦明良相逢，功賞交盡，真有得祖宗之家法也。噫！君臣上下，誠意交孚，此所以內修外攘，光復舊物，而成中興之大業也歟！
translation_en:
…merely carrying on the achievements of your lord duke. In former times, when our King Wu ruled, it was your ancestor, Duke Kang, whom he emulated [?]. Now [?], do not say that you act for the sake of me, the young king, but regard yourself simply as continuing Duke Kang’s legacy. Moreover, if you can vigorously advance your achievements and serve me as your ancestor served Kings Wen and Wu, then I shall bestow great blessings upon you, rewarding you as my ancestor rewarded Duke Kang. Thus, rewarding achievement calls for extending favor: I must grant you a jade libation ladle and a vessel of fragrant black-millet wine, enabling you to sacrifice to your ancestors. Rewarding achievement calls for additional territory: I must announce it to the cultivated ancestor and grant you mountains and fields, enabling you to enlarge your fief. Furthermore, I shall have you go to Qizhou to receive your formal investiture, proceeding to the place where your ancestor Duke Kang received his investiture, to make manifest your lineage’s achievements. I shall have you receive the written patent in the ancestral temple, at the place where your ancestor Duke Kang received his patent, to display your lineage’s excellence.
Ah! The minister has magnificent achievements, and the ruler has magnificent rewards. These achievements and rewards may indeed be called equally worthy. Generally, a minister expresses loyalty by achieving merit, and the state fulfills ritual propriety by rewarding it. Thus, Duke Kang rendered service to the state [?], and King Wu enfeoffed him in northern Yan; the Duke of Zhou rendered service in subduing Shang [?], and King Cheng established his eldest son as a feudal lord. How outstanding and unequaled were the virtue and accomplishments of these enlightened rulers and worthy ministers! Likewise, Duke Mu accomplished the work of administering and demarcating the territories, while King Xuan honored him generously with investiture and gifts. Here too an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister met, and achievement and reward each found their fullest expression. They truly grasped the traditions handed down by their ancestors. Ah! Ruler and ministers, superiors and subordinates, trusted one another in complete sincerity. Was this not how they brought order within, repelled threats from without, gloriously recovered their former possessions, and accomplished the great work of dynastic restoration?

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
春秋
天王狩于河陽〔僖公二十八年〕
李朝陽
同考試官教諭焦　批〔意本胡傳而文氣老成宜取〕
為本房之冠
考試官教諭羅　批〔以尊周全晉立說最當〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔得旨〕
春秋假天王巡狩之名寓尊王全霸之意此狩
于河陽之書有以見春秋之忠恕也何則五載
===
一巡狩有虞之制也十二年王乃時巡成周之
法也時而春秋王靈不振而巡狩之禮不行久
矣令僖公之世胡為而有狩于河陽之書哉蓋
是時晉文繼伯威合諸侯因衡雍罷朝之餘欲
再舉朝王之典乃自嫌强大不敢擁衆於京師
故請王出狩天王俯從以就見以人臣之卑坐
致萬乘之寵臨以天子之尊俯就諸侯之請召
鑾輿至止諸侯盡尊事之儀而實非天王之意
迎警蹕載臨列辟肅會朝之禮而實由晉文之
punctuated:
春秋
天王狩于河陽〔僖公二十八年〕
李朝陽
同考試官教諭焦，批〔意本胡傳，而文氣老成，宜取〕為本房之冠。
考試官教諭羅，批〔以尊周全晉立說，最當〕。
考試官教諭孫，批〔得旨〕。
春秋假天王巡狩之名，寓尊王全霸之意。此狩于河陽之書，有以見春秋之忠恕也。何則？五載一巡狩，有虞之制也；十二年王乃時巡，成周之法也。時而春秋，王靈不振，而巡狩之禮不行久矣。令僖公之世，胡為而有狩于河陽之書哉？蓋是時晉文繼伯，威合諸侯，因衡雍罷朝之餘，欲再舉朝王之典，乃自嫌强大，不敢擁衆於京師，故請王出狩。天王俯從，以就見。以人臣之卑，坐致萬乘之寵臨；以天子之尊，俯就諸侯之請召。鑾輿至止，諸侯盡尊事之儀，而實非天王之意；迎警蹕載臨，列辟肅會朝之禮，而實由晉文之
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals
“The Heavenly King went on a hunting tour at Heyang.” 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi〕
Li Chaoyang
Associate Examiner Jiao, Instructor, comments: 〔The interpretation rests on Hu’s Commentary, while the writing is mature and assured. It should be selected〕 as the best answer in this examining section.
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔It is most appropriate to base the argument on honoring Zhou and preserving Jin’s standing.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the essential meaning.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals uses the designation of a royal inspection tour to convey the intention of honoring the king and preserving the hegemon’s standing. This record of a hunting tour at Heyang reveals the conscientiousness and sympathetic understanding of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why is this so? An inspection tour once every five years was the institution of Youyu; the king’s making a seasonal inspection tour in the twelfth year was the rule of the established Zhou dynasty. By the Spring and Autumn period, royal authority had declined, and the rites of inspection tours had long ceased to be performed. In the time of Duke Xi [?], why, then, was there a record of a hunting tour at Heyang?
At this time, Duke Wen of Jin had succeeded to the hegemony and assembled the feudal lords through his might. After the audience at Hengyong had concluded, he wished to hold another ceremony of paying court to the king. Yet, concerned that his own power was too great, he did not dare bring his forces into the royal capital. He therefore requested that the king go out on a hunting tour. The Heavenly King condescended to comply and went to meet them. From the lowly station of a subject, Duke Wen remained in place and brought about the gracious visit of the ruler of ten thousand chariots; from the exalted station of the Son of Heaven, the king condescended to answer a feudal lord’s invitation and summons. The royal carriage arrived, and the feudal lords fully performed the ceremonies of reverent service, but this was not actually the Heavenly King’s intention. They welcomed his arrival amid cries clearing the way [?], and the assembled rulers solemnly observed the rites of a court audience, but this in fact resulted from Duke Wen of Jin’s …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
召也以尊臨卑而王室之屈辱已極以下召上
而臣子之不恭已甚名分于焉而蕩然禮制于
焉而掃地聖人修經垂憲萬世以爲周室雖衰
人主之名猶在也晉文雖强人臣之義當存也
以臣召君名義隳矣其可訓乎以君就臣綱常
易矣尚忍言乎故原其自嫌之心嘉其尊王之
義不據事以直書乃變文而書狩使若天子自
至而有虞巡狩之制復見於天下非無事而空
行也萬乘自臨而成周時巡之法再舉於今日
===
非無故而慢遊也上焉王室無降尊之失下焉
晉霸免不臣之罪天冠地屨之分不泯上衣下
裳之義猶存而周之與晉豈不於是乎兩全也
訖春秋原情爲制以誠變禮之意至矣雖然于
溫之事與踐土事同而書法異者何訖蓋
踐土之會王實自往非晉罪也故爲王諱而足
矣溫之會晉則有罪而其情順矣故旣爲王諱
之又爲晉解之春秋之忠恕何如訖噫非聖人
莫能修此類可見
punctuated:
召也。以尊臨卑，而王室之屈辱已極；以下召上，而臣子之不恭已甚。名分于焉而蕩然，禮制于焉而掃地。聖人修經，垂憲萬世，以爲周室雖衰，人主之名猶在也；晉文雖强，人臣之義當存也。以臣召君，名義隳矣，其可訓乎？以君就臣，綱常易矣，尚忍言乎？故原其自嫌之心，嘉其尊王之義，不據事以直書，乃變文而書狩，使若天子自至，而有虞巡狩之制復見於天下，非無事而空行也；萬乘自臨，而成周時巡之法再舉於今日，非無故而慢遊也。上焉，王室無降尊之失；下焉，晉霸免不臣之罪。天冠地屨之分不泯，上衣下裳之義猶存，而周之與晉豈不於是乎兩全也訖？《春秋》原情爲制，以誠變禮之意至矣。

雖然，于溫之事與踐土事同，而書法異者何訖？蓋踐土之會，王實自往，非晉罪也，故爲王諱而足矣。溫之會，晉則有罪，而其情順矣，故旣爲王諱之，又爲晉解之。《春秋》之忠恕何如訖？噫！非聖人莫能修，此類可見。
translation_en:
…summons. For the exalted ruler to come to his inferior brought the humiliation of the royal house to its utmost extreme; for an inferior to summon his superior was an egregious act of disrespect by a subject. The distinctions of status were thereby dissolved, and the ritual order swept away. In compiling the classic to transmit a standard for ten thousand generations, the Sage considered that, although the royal house of Zhou had declined, its designation as sovereign remained; although Duke Wen of Jin was powerful, his obligations as a subject must still be preserved. When a subject summons his ruler, the duties attaching to their respective stations are destroyed: could this serve as an example? When a ruler goes to his subject, the cardinal relationships and constant norms are overturned: could one even bear to speak of it? Thus, taking account of the duke’s misgivings and commending his intention to honor the king, the Sage did not record the event directly according to the facts. Instead, he altered the wording and wrote of a royal tour of inspection. This made it appear that the Son of Heaven had come of his own accord, and that the inspection tours instituted under Yu were once again manifest throughout the realm—not that he had traveled idly without business to conduct. The sovereign of ten thousand chariots had come in person, and the Zhou practice of seasonal inspection tours was being enacted anew—not that he had gone wandering heedlessly without cause. Above, the royal house was spared the fault of lowering its dignity; below, the hegemon of Jin escaped the charge of acting in defiance of his position as a subject. The distinction between Heaven as the crown and Earth as the shoes was not effaced, and the significance of the upper garment and lower skirt remained intact. Were not both Zhou and Jin thereby preserved from reproach [?]? The Spring and Autumn Annals takes underlying intentions into account in establishing its standards; its principle of allowing sincere intent to justify modifications of ritual is here expressed to the fullest.

Nevertheless, if the affair at Wen was the same as that at Jiantu, why was it recorded differently [?]? At the meeting at Jiantu, the king had indeed gone of his own accord, and Jin was not at fault. It therefore sufficed to veil the matter for the king’s sake. At the meeting at Wen, Jin was at fault, but its underlying intention accorded with proper duty. Thus the text both veiled the matter for the king’s sake and offered an explanation in Jin’s defense. How profound are the conscientiousness and sympathetic understanding of the Spring and Autumn Annals [?]! Ah! Examples of this kind show that none but the Sage could have compiled it.

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遂伐楚　楚屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕公會
齊侯于夾谷齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕
張守
同考試官教諭焦　批〔聖人以天自處之意此作能發明之是用錄此〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔胡傳意正如此〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔能推原聖人之心是善觀春秋者〕
===
聖人修經既因霸主以義服夷而特序其績復
因在己以禮化强而自序其績此見聖人以天
自處而序績之文無嫌於人己之分也且春秋
夫子之筆削而以天自處夫子之本心何以見
之有如僖公之時暴橫中國者莫如楚能攘之
者功無大於此也齊桓身安攘之任使其義以
責之八國雲集鼓勇而南包茅不貢之罰其義
正矣王祭不供之徵其義明矣楚雖不義寧不
有所動邪由是屈完來請服恐後微與同好
punctuated:
「遂伐楚，楚屈完來盟于師。」〔僖公四年〕「公會齊侯于夾谷，齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。」〔定公十年〕
張守
同考試官教諭焦，批〔聖人以天自處之意，此作能發明之，是用錄此。〕
考試官教諭羅，批〔胡傳意正如此。〕
考試官教諭孫，批〔能推原聖人之心，是善觀春秋者。〕
聖人修經，既因霸主以義服夷而特序其績，復因在己以禮化强而自序其績。此見聖人以天自處，而序績之文無嫌於人己之分也。且《春秋》，夫子之筆削，而以天自處，夫子之本心，何以見之？有如僖公之時，暴橫中國者莫如楚，能攘之者，功無大於此也。齊桓身安攘之任，使其義以責之，八國雲集，鼓勇而南。包茅不貢之罰，其義正矣；王祭不供之徵，其義明矣。楚雖不義，寧不有所動邪？由是屈完來，請服恐後，微與同好
translation_en:
“They then attacked Chu. Qu Wan of Chu came to conclude a covenant with the army.” 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 “The duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Zhang Shou.
Associate Examiner Jiao, Instructor, commented: 〔This composition elucidates the sage’s intention in taking Heaven as his own standpoint; for this reason it is included here.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, commented: 〔This is precisely the meaning of Hu’s Commentary.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, commented: 〔He can trace matters back to the sage’s mind: he is one who reads the Spring and Autumn Annals well.〕
In compiling the classic, the sage gave special recognition to a hegemon’s achievements because he subdued the barbarians through righteousness. He also recorded his own achievements because he himself transformed the powerful through ritual propriety. This shows that the sage took Heaven as his standpoint: in recording achievements, he had no misgivings arising from the distinction between others and himself. Now, the Spring and Autumn Annals embodies the Master’s editorial judgments. But how can we see that taking Heaven as his standpoint was the Master’s underlying intention?
In Duke Xi’s time, for example, none was more violent and overbearing toward the central states than Chu. No achievement could surpass that of whoever could repel it. Duke Huan of Qi personally assumed [?] the responsibility of repelling it, invoking righteousness to call it to account. The eight states gathered like clouds and, mustering their courage, marched south. In punishing the failure to present bundles of thatching grass as tribute, their cause was just; in demanding an accounting for the failure to supply the king’s sacrifices, their righteousness was manifest. Though Chu lacked righteousness, could it remain unmoved? Thus Qu Wan came, seeking submission and fearing to lag behind, with a faint wish for shared amity [?] …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之歡鵲然於納款之餘敢不供給之對怡然於
聽命之下曾何敢有向日之暴横彊然桓公義
以服楚如此使人之自私者觀之孰不為服楚
之功功之在人者也已何與焉聖人之心天也
功在可序則序之初何知其在人沒而弗序焉
故於屈完之服特書曰來所以序桓之績也若
夫定公之世凌駕我魯者莫如齊能化之者功
莫加於此也聖人攝相事於夾谷之會秉大禮
以責之兩君就壇禍在不測聖人歷階而升不
===
盡一等裔不謀夏夷不亂華之言禮何謹也俘
不干盟兵不偪好之語禮何嚴也齊雖無禮寧
不有所感邪由是愧悔不遑謝過以貿鄆讙之
田雖昔為齊有也今則章章而來歸龜陰之地
雖向為齊奪也今則唯唯而獻納曾何敢有昔
日之凌駕彊然聖人禮以化齊如此使人之避
嫌者處之孰不為化齊之功功之在已者也何
足紀焉聖人之心天也功在可紀則紀之初何
計其在已而嫌於弗紀焉故於三邑之歸亦書
punctuated:
之歡，鵲然於納款之餘；敢不供給之對，怡然於聽命之下。曾何敢有向日之暴横彊然？桓公義以服楚如此，使人之自私者觀之，孰不為服楚之功，功之在人者也，已何與焉？聖人之心，天也。功在可序則序之，初何知其在人，沒而弗序焉？故於屈完之服，特書曰「來」，所以序桓之績也。
若夫定公之世，凌駕我魯者莫如齊，能化之者，功莫加於此也。聖人攝相事於夾谷之會，秉大禮以責之。兩君就壇，禍在不測，聖人歷階而升，不盡一等。「裔不謀夏，夷不亂華」之言，禮何謹也！「俘不干盟，兵不偪好」之語，禮何嚴也！齊雖無禮，寧不有所感邪？由是愧悔不遑，謝過以貿。鄆讙之田，雖昔為齊有也，今則章章而來歸；龜陰之地，雖向為齊奪也，今則唯唯而獻納。曾何敢有昔日之凌駕彊然？聖人禮以化齊如此，使人之避嫌者處之，孰不為化齊之功，功之在已者也，何足紀焉？聖人之心，天也。功在可紀則紀之，初何計其在已而嫌於弗紀焉？故於三邑之歸，亦書
translation_en:
…the delight of shared amity was expressed joyfully after the submission; the reply, “Would we dare not furnish the supplies?” was offered gladly in obedience to the command. How could Chu dare display its former violence and overbearing force [?]? Such was Duke Huan’s use of righteousness to bring Chu into submission. If a person governed by selfish considerations viewed this, who would not say, “The achievement of subduing Chu belongs to someone else. What part have I in it?” But the sage’s heart is Heaven itself. If an achievement deserves to be recounted, he recounts it. Why should he concern himself with its belonging to someone else and suppress it rather than recount it? Thus, in recording Qu Wan’s submission, he expressly wrote “came,” thereby recounting Duke Huan’s achievement.
In Duke Ding’s time, no state overawed our Lu more than Qi; no achievement could surpass bringing about its transformation. Acting as minister at the meeting at Jiagu, the sage invoked the great principles of ritual propriety to hold Qi to account. When the two rulers mounted the platform, disaster threatened unpredictably. The sage ascended the steps, without completing a single flight. In declaring, “Peoples of the distant borders must not scheme against the Xia; the Yi must not disrupt the Hua,” how scrupulously he upheld ritual propriety! In saying, “Captives must not interfere with a covenant; weapons must not menace friendly relations,” how strictly he upheld it! Though Qi lacked ritual propriety, could it fail to be moved? Thereupon, overwhelmed with shame and remorse, it apologized for its faults [?]. The fields of Yun and Huan, though formerly held by Qi, were now openly returned; the territory of Guiyin, though previously seized by Qi, was now yielded with ready assent. How could Qi dare display its former domineering force [?]? Such was the sage’s use of ritual propriety to transform Qi. If someone anxious to avoid suspicion were in his position, who would not say, “The achievement of transforming Qi is my own achievement. How could it merit recording?” But the sage’s heart is Heaven itself. If an achievement deserves to be recorded, he records it. Why should he concern himself with its being his own and, fearing suspicion, leave it unrecorded? Thus, in recording the return of the three towns, he likewise wrote…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
曰來所以序已之績也吁聖人會人物於一身
萬象異形而同體通古今於一息百王異世而
同神於土皆安而無所避也於我皆真而無所
忘也一惟天之至公耳夫何避嫌之有我雖然
聖人修經以天自處豈特序績一事而已我他
如襃善貶惡命德討罪與夫尊君而抑臣內夏
而外夷或婉其辭或章其實一皆天之至公無
我之心也豈有一毫私意於其間我故曰春秋
非聖人莫能修
===
禮記
天子祭天下名山大川
溫應璧
同考試官訓導姚　批〔此題作者多失於冗泛能認理明白而措詞詳整者僅見此篇〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔文賸意足讀之可愛〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔得天子祭山川之旨〕
以天下生民之主祀天下生物之神所以報其
功也蓋山川以生物為功而天子以生民為心
punctuated:
曰「來」，所以序已之績也。吁！聖人會人物於一身，萬象異形而同體；通古今於一息，百王異世而同神。於土皆安而無所避也，於我皆真而無所忘也，一惟天之至公耳。夫何避嫌之有我？雖然，聖人修經，以天自處，豈特序績一事而已我？他如襃善貶惡、命德討罪，與夫尊君而抑臣、內夏而外夷，或婉其辭，或章其實，一皆天之至公無我之心也。豈有一毫私意於其間我？故曰：「春秋非聖人莫能修。」

禮記
天子祭天下名山大川
溫應璧

以天下生民之主，祀天下生物之神，所以報其功也。蓋山川以生物為功，而天子以生民為心
translation_en:
… says “came,” thereby recording his own achievement. Ah! The sage unites human beings and all things in his own person: the myriad forms differ in shape but share one body. He comprehends past and present in a single breath: the hundred kings belong to different ages but share one spirit. In every situation [?], he is at ease and avoids nothing; within himself, all is authentic and nothing is forgotten. This is solely Heaven’s utmost impartiality. What concern could there be about avoiding suspicion [?]? Yet when the sage edited the Classic, he took Heaven as his standpoint. How could this apply only to recording achievements [?]? Other matters—praising goodness and condemning evil, appointing the virtuous and punishing the guilty, honoring rulers and restraining ministers, treating the Xia as insiders and the Yi as outsiders—are expressed sometimes through subtle wording and sometimes through explicit presentation of the facts. All proceed from Heaven’s utterly impartial and selfless mind. Could there be the slightest private intention among them [?]? Thus it is said: “None but a sage could compile the Spring and Autumn Annals.”

Book of Rites
“The Son of Heaven sacrifices to the renowned mountains and great rivers throughout the realm.”
Wen Yingbi
Associate Examiner Yao, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “Most who wrote on this topic erred through prolixity and vagueness. This is the only essay I have seen that apprehends the principle clearly and expresses it fully and coherently.”
Examiner Luo, an Instructor, comments: “The writing is ample and the meaning fully expressed; it is a pleasure to read.”
Examiner Sun, an Instructor, comments: “It grasps the purport of the Son of Heaven’s sacrifices to mountains and rivers.”

For the lord of the people throughout the realm to sacrifice to the spirits that bring forth living things throughout the realm is to repay their services. For the service of mountains and rivers lies in bringing forth living things, while the Son of Heaven sets his heart upon giving life to the people…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
也天子主萬民而祭及乎山川則所以報其功
也為何如哉王制著先王祭祀之禮其旨如此
謂夫天子以一人之尊主百神之祭故既郊社
於天地矣而名山之祭豈可緩乎既禘嘗於宗
廟矣而大川之祀豈容後乎是故名山不外於
五嶽而五嶽之在天下寶藏興焉材木出焉利
民之生宜有以祭之也故必視三公饗餼牢禮
之數而為牲器之數于以陳其犧牲設其鼎俎
將誠於對越之際焉大川不外於四瀆而四瀆
===
之在天下魚鱉生焉貨財殖焉資民之養當有
以祀之也故必視諸侯饔餼牢禮之等而為牲
器之等于以薦其薦俎備其禮樂致敬於昭假
之頃焉然所以祭乎名山者非諂也報功之禮
當如此也所以祀乎大川者非瀆也報功之典
當如是也噫以天下之主而後得祀天下之神
非惟重民之意可見而名分之正一何嚴哉抑
天子固祭天下名山大川矣下文又曰諸侯祭
名山大川之在其地者蓋在上者可以兼乎下
punctuated: 也。天子主萬民而祭及乎山川，則所以報其功也，為何如哉？《王制》著先王祭祀之禮，其旨如此。謂夫天子以一人之尊，主百神之祭，故既郊社於天地矣，而名山之祭豈可緩乎？既禘嘗於宗廟矣，而大川之祀豈容後乎？是故名山不外於五嶽，而五嶽之在天下，寶藏興焉，材木出焉，利民之生，宜有以祭之也。故必視三公饗餼牢禮之數而為牲器之數，于以陳其犧牲，設其鼎俎，將誠於對越之際焉。大川不外於四瀆，而四瀆之在天下，魚鱉生焉，貨財殖焉，資民之養，當有以祀之也。故必視諸侯饔餼牢禮之等而為牲器之等，于以薦其薦俎，備其禮樂，致敬於昭假之頃焉。然所以祭乎名山者，非諂也，報功之禮當如此也；所以祀乎大川者，非瀆也，報功之典當如是也。噫！以天下之主而後得祀天下之神，非惟重民之意可見，而名分之正一何嚴哉！抑天子固祭天下名山大川矣，下文又曰：「諸侯祭名山大川之在其地者。」蓋在上者可以兼乎下，
translation_en:
…such is the case. When the Son of Heaven, who presides over the myriad people, extends his sacrifices to the mountains and rivers, how does he thereby repay their service? The “Royal Regulations” chapter records the sacrificial rites of the former kings, and this is their purport. The Son of Heaven, in his unique exalted position, presides over sacrifices to the hundred spirits. Having performed the suburban and soil-altar sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, how could he delay sacrificing to the renowned mountains? Having performed the di and chang sacrifices in the ancestral temple, how could he put off offerings to the great rivers?

The renowned mountains are none other than the Five Sacred Peaks. Throughout the realm, these peaks yield precious resources and timber, benefiting the people's livelihood; they ought therefore to receive sacrifices. Accordingly, the number of sacrificial animals and vessels must follow the prescribed numbers of animals used in ceremonial feasts and provisions for the Three Dukes. The sacrificial animals are thus arrayed and the tripods and offering stands set out, expressing sincerity when approaching the spirits. The great rivers are none other than the Four Watercourses. Throughout the realm, these watercourses produce fish and turtles and generate goods and wealth, sustaining the people; they ought therefore to receive offerings. Accordingly, the grades of sacrificial animals and vessels must follow the prescribed grades of animals used in gifts of prepared food and provisions for the feudal lords. The offerings are thus presented on their stands, and the rites and music fully provided, expressing reverence at the moment of communion with the spirits.

Yet sacrificing to the renowned mountains is no act of flattery: this is what the rites for repaying their service require. Offering to the great rivers is no act of irreverence: this is what the institutions for repaying their service prescribe. Ah! Only the ruler of all under Heaven may sacrifice to the spirits of all under Heaven. This reveals not only the intention to value the people: how strictly it also maintains the proper distinctions of status and duty!

Moreover, while the Son of Heaven indeed sacrifices to the renowned mountains and great rivers throughout the realm, the following passage also says: “The feudal lords sacrifice to the renowned mountains and great rivers within their own territories.” For those above may encompass the prerogatives of those below…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
故天子祭天下名山大川在下者不可兼乎上
故諸侯止祭山川之在其地者于以見天子君
天下而其所報者衆諸侯君一國而其所報者
寡一祭祀之間而名分攸在先王制禮之意可
謂詳且盡矣
凡人之所以為人者禮義也禮義之始在
於正容體齊顔色順辭令容體正顔色
齊辭令順而後禮義備以正君臣親父
子和長幼君臣正父子親長幼和而后
===
禮義立
劉澄

考試官教諭孫　批〔體認禮義最明白〕
記者論人當全夫人道必推言人道所由全也
蓋義以為質禮以行之人之道也人於禮義也
而或未能盡焉則人道豈能全於巳哉記冠義
punctuated:
故天子祭天下名山大川，在下者不可兼乎上，故諸侯止祭山川之在其地者。于以見天子君天下，而其所報者衆；諸侯君一國，而其所報者寡。一祭祀之間，而名分攸在，先王制禮之意可謂詳且盡矣。

凡人之所以為人者，禮義也。禮義之始，在於正容體，齊顔色，順辭令。容體正，顔色齊，辭令順，而後禮義備。以正君臣，親父子，和長幼。君臣正，父子親，長幼和，而后禮義立。

劉澄

考試官教諭孫　批〔體認禮義最明白。〕

記者論人當全夫人道，必推言人道所由全也。蓋義以為質，禮以行之，人之道也。人於禮義也，而或未能盡焉，則人道豈能全於巳哉？記《冠義》
translation_en:
…Thus the Son of Heaven sacrifices to the famous mountains and great rivers throughout the realm. Those below cannot assume the prerogatives of those above; thus the feudal lords sacrifice only to the mountains and rivers within their own territories. This shows that the Son of Heaven rules all under Heaven and has many benefactors to repay, whereas a feudal lord rules a single state and has fewer benefactors to repay. Even in sacrificial worship, distinctions of status and duty have their place. The intentions of the former kings in establishing ritual may indeed be called detailed and exhaustive.

“What makes human beings human is ritual propriety and righteousness. Ritual propriety and righteousness begin with making one’s bearing correct, one’s expression composed, and one’s speech appropriate. Once bearing is correct, expression composed, and speech appropriate, ritual propriety and righteousness are complete. Through these, the relationship between ruler and minister is rectified, that between father and son made affectionate, and that between elder and younger made harmonious. Once ruler and minister stand in their proper relationship, father and son are affectionate, and elder and younger are harmonious, ritual propriety and righteousness are established.”

Liu Cheng

Associate Examiner Yao, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The main meaning is explained clearly and fully, without verbose or cumbersome language. This is evidently someone practiced in composing essays on the Classics. It is recorded here as a model for later students.”
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “The essay’s reasoning is pertinent and sound, and deserves praise.”
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “His understanding of ritual propriety and righteousness is exceptionally clear.”

In discussing how people should fulfill the human way, the author of the Record necessarily traces and explains the means by which that way is fulfilled. To take righteousness as one’s substance and put it into practice through ritual propriety is the human way. If a person fails to fulfill ritual propriety and righteousness, how can the human way be complete within himself? The author of “The Meaning of the Capping Ceremony”…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者知其然謂夫天地之性人為貴人之行禮義
為先人之所以為人不在四體之既正也不在
膚革之充盈也亦惟有禮義存焉耳是故禮義
始於謹容辭也容體欲其可度當有以正之顏
色欲其可觀當有以齊之辭令欲其可從當有
以順之令焉容體正而不失足於人顏色齊而
不失色於人辭令順而不失口於人則容辭之
著見禮以文乎質而蔚然其可美矣禮義其有
不備乎禮義始於正彝倫也君臣欲其有義當
===
有以正之父子欲其有恩當有以親之長幼欲
其有序當有以和之令焉君臣正而朝廷之儀
肅父子親而閨門之分定長幼和而宗族之有
禮則彝倫之交際禮以行乎義而燦然其可觀
矣禮義其有不立乎禮義備則人道以備禮義
立則人道以立人道之全孰有外於禮義者哉
考之下文有曰冠於阼醮於客位三加彌尊者
所以備其服而示以成人之禮也又曰見於母
母拜之見於兄弟兄弟拜之奠摯見於君遂以
punctuated: 者知其然，謂夫天地之性，人為貴；人之行，禮義為先。人之所以為人，不在四體之既正也，不在膚革之充盈也，亦惟有禮義存焉耳。是故禮義始於謹容辭也。容體欲其可度，當有以正之；顏色欲其可觀，當有以齊之；辭令欲其可從，當有以順之。令焉，容體正而不失足於人，顏色齊而不失色於人，辭令順而不失口於人，則容辭之著見，禮以文乎質，而蔚然其可美矣。禮義其有不備乎？禮義始於正彝倫也。君臣欲其有義，當有以正之；父子欲其有恩，當有以親之；長幼欲其有序，當有以和之。令焉，君臣正而朝廷之儀肅，父子親而閨門之分定，長幼和而宗族之有禮，則彝倫之交際，禮以行乎義，而燦然其可觀矣。禮義其有不立乎？禮義備則人道以備，禮義立則人道以立。人道之全，孰有外於禮義者哉？考之下文，有曰：「冠於阼，醮於客位，三加彌尊」者，所以備其服而示以成人之禮也。又曰：「見於母，母拜之；見於兄弟，兄弟拜之；奠摯見於君，遂以
translation_en:
…the author of “The Meaning of the Capping Ceremony” understood this, saying: “Of all beings endowed by Heaven and Earth with a nature, humans are the most noble; in human conduct, ritual propriety and righteousness come first.” What makes a human being human lies neither in having properly formed limbs nor in having well-developed flesh and skin. It lies solely in possessing ritual propriety and righteousness.

Thus, ritual propriety and righteousness begin with care in bearing and speech. If one wishes one’s bodily bearing to accord with proper standards, one must make it correct; if one wishes one’s expression to be fit to behold, one must compose it; if one wishes one’s words to be acceptable, one must make them appropriate. Let it be so [?]: when bodily bearing is correct, one makes no misstep before others; when one’s expression is composed, one shows no improper expression before others; when one’s words are appropriate, one makes no verbal lapse before others. Then, in the outward manifestation of bearing and speech, ritual propriety adorns one’s underlying substance, displaying a flourishing beauty. How could ritual propriety and righteousness fail to be complete?

Ritual propriety and righteousness begin with rectifying the enduring human relationships. If one wishes righteousness to prevail between ruler and minister, one must set their relationship right; if one wishes affection to prevail between father and son, one must foster their closeness; if one wishes order to prevail between elder and younger, one must bring them into harmony. Let it be so [?]: when ruler and minister stand in a correct relationship, court ceremonial is dignified; when father and son are close, the distinctions within the household are settled; when elder and younger are harmonious, the lineage observes ritual propriety. Then, in dealings within the enduring human relationships, ritual propriety puts righteousness into practice, presenting a splendid spectacle. How could ritual propriety and righteousness fail to be established? When ritual propriety and righteousness are complete, the human way is thereby complete; when ritual propriety and righteousness are established, the human way is thereby established. What part of the fulfillment of the human way could lie outside ritual propriety and righteousness?

text:
擧見於鄉大夫鄉先生者所以正大倫而責以
成人之禮也故曰冠者禮之始也嘉事之重者
也聖王重之其以是歟

論
王者無外

能一天下也王者豈有外哉夫天下誠大
矣其地有中國有四夷其風氣有寒暑燥

translation_en:
…being presented to the district grandee and the district’s elders serves to set the great human relationships aright and to hold him to the ritual obligations of adulthood. Thus it is said: “Capping is the beginning of ritual, and the weightiest of auspicious ceremonies.” Is this not why the sage kings attached such importance to it?

Second Session
Discourse
“The True King Regards Nothing as Outside His Realm”
Zhang Ziwei

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: “The writing has an antique vigor, and its arguments unfold one after another, like the Yangzi or the Yellow River pouring forth for a thousand li, with a surging force that seems inexhaustible. This must be a scholar who has accumulated learning and awaits his opportunity. When you compete in literary skill at the Metropolitan Examination in spring, you will surely be among the first to succeed.”

Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: “His exposition is wide-ranging, his factual references precise, and his spirit flourishing. This bears no resemblance at all to ordinary examination writing.”

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: “The discourse has a spirited, martial vigor, yet does not exceed the established standards. Surely its author has devoted himself to the study of ancient-style prose?”

If one regards it as having nothing outside it…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
則一一則華夷各得其分而大一統之治
成矣以有外視之則貳貳則爭爭則紛紛
藉藉弱之肉强之食而禍患將自玆始焉
王者亦安能晏然於天下之上而無所置
其慮哉故曰王者無外荀悅之言春秋之
義也且所謂王者孰立之乎天立之也旣
爲天所立其所舉措宜有不違夫天者矣
夫天覆乎上凡物之在其下者無遺覆也
天何嘗有外乎惟地亦然地載乎下凡物
===
之在其上者無遺載也地何嘗有外乎王
者與天地參焉者也使以戎狄爲外而不
一視之則與天地不相似矣或曰春秋之
法内中國而外夷狄惡在其無外也曰凡
吾之所謂無外而一視之者非謂純以中
國之禮禮之以中國之治治之也隨其分
而處之因其俗而施之馭之得其道俾不
失其常而已一視而無外者王道之體内
夏而外夷者王道之用二者並行而不相
punctuated: 則一，一則華夷各得其分，而大一統之治成矣。以有外視之則貳，貳則爭，爭則紛紛藉藉，弱之肉，强之食，而禍患將自玆始焉。王者亦安能晏然於天下之上，而無所置其慮哉？故曰：「王者無外。」荀悅之言，《春秋》之義也。且所謂王者，孰立之乎？天立之也。旣爲天所立，其所舉措宜有不違夫天者矣。夫天覆乎上，凡物之在其下者，無遺覆也。天何嘗有外乎？惟地亦然。地載乎下，凡物之在其上者，無遺載也。地何嘗有外乎？王者，與天地參焉者也。使以戎狄爲外而不一視之，則與天地不相似矣。或曰：「《春秋》之法，内中國而外夷狄，惡在其無外也？」曰：「凡吾之所謂無外而一視之者，非謂純以中國之禮禮之，以中國之治治之也。隨其分而處之，因其俗而施之，馭之得其道，俾不失其常而已。一視而無外者，王道之體；内夏而外夷者，王道之用。二者並行而不相
translation_en:
…then there is unity. With unity, the Hua and the Yi each attain their proper place, and the governance of grand unification is achieved. If one regards some as outside, division results; division leads to contention, and contention to turmoil and disorder, with the weak becoming meat for the strong to devour. Calamities will begin from this. How, then, could the king remain at ease above all under Heaven, with nothing to concern him? Hence the saying: “The king recognizes none as outside.” These words of Xun Yue express the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Moreover, who establishes the one called king? Heaven establishes him. Since Heaven has established him, his actions should accord with Heaven. Heaven covers from above, leaving nothing beneath it uncovered. When has Heaven ever regarded anything as outside? Earth is likewise. Earth bears from below, leaving nothing upon it unsupported. When has Earth ever regarded anything as outside? The king stands alongside Heaven and Earth as one of the Three Powers. If he treats the Rong and Di as outside and does not regard them with equal concern, he fails to resemble Heaven and Earth.

Someone asks: “The rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals is to treat the Central States as inside and the Yi and Di as outside. Where, then, is its recognition of none as outside?” The reply is: “What I mean by recognizing none as outside and regarding all with equal concern is not that one should deal with them exclusively through the rites of the Central States or govern them through the institutions of the Central States. One should deal with them according to their respective stations and apply measures suited to their customs, directing them in the proper way so that they do not lose their established order—that is all. Regarding all with equal concern and recognizing none as outside is the substance of the kingly Way; treating the Xia as inside and the Yi as outside is its application. These two operate together without mutually …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
悖春秋之所以爲春秋也歟嗚呼聖人之
道理一而分殊自其分之殊者觀之則雖
王畿之内朝廷之上貴賤賞罰死生奪予
雜施而並用不能一律齊也而况於夷狄
乎自其理之一者觀之則民吾同胞物吾
與也故一物不得其所王者與有責焉而
夷狄亦夫人耳而謂其無與於天道無關
於人事可乎蓋嘗求之經矣蠻夷率服與
萬邦咸寧並載於虞典堯舜何嘗外之哉
===
淮島萊夷之方物與青徐内郡並列於禹
貢夏禹何嘗外之哉蠻夷鎮藩與侯甸男
采衛並隸九畿之籍文武周公又何嘗外
之哉比其爭率則虞帝不能無三苗之征
商宗不能無鬼方之誅周王不能無玁狁
昆夷之伐彼堂堂全盛之世豈利其地雠
其人以勤我師旅乎哉將以一天下之不
一亦大不獲已焉者耳萬彙皆榮而一木
獨枯則造化非全功滿堂燕笑而來兔向
punctuated: 悖，春秋之所以爲春秋也歟！嗚呼！聖人之道，理一而分殊。自其分之殊者觀之，則雖王畿之内、朝廷之上，貴賤、賞罰、死生、奪予，雜施而並用，不能一律齊也，而况於夷狄乎？自其理之一者觀之，則民吾同胞，物吾與也。故一物不得其所，王者與有責焉。而夷狄亦夫人耳，而謂其無與於天道、無關於人事，可乎？蓋嘗求之經矣。「蠻夷率服」與「萬邦咸寧」並載於《虞典》，堯舜何嘗外之哉？淮島萊夷之方物，與青徐内郡並列於《禹貢》，夏禹何嘗外之哉？蠻夷鎮藩，與侯甸男采衛並隸九畿之籍，文武周公又何嘗外之哉？比其爭率，則虞帝不能無三苗之征，商宗不能無鬼方之誅，周王不能無玁狁、昆夷之伐。彼堂堂全盛之世，豈利其地、雠其人，以勤我師旅乎哉？將以一天下之不一，亦大不獲已焉者耳。萬彙皆榮，而一木獨枯，則造化非全功；滿堂燕笑，而來兔向
translation_en:
…without conflicting: is this not what makes the Spring and Autumn Annals what it is? Alas! The Way of the sages has one underlying principle, but differentiated distinctions. Viewed in terms of those distinctions, even within the royal domain and at court, noble and lowly status, rewards and punishments, death and life, deprivation and bestowal are variously applied and employed together; they cannot be made uniform by a single rule. How much more is this true of the non-Chinese peoples? Viewed in terms of its single underlying principle, the people are my siblings, and all things are my companions. Thus, if even one thing fails to find its proper place, the king shares responsibility. The non-Chinese peoples, too, are human beings. Can one say that they have no part in the Way of Heaven and no connection with human affairs?
I have sought evidence in the classics. “The Man and Yi all submitted” and “the myriad states were all at peace” are both recorded in the Canon of Yu. When did Yao and Shun ever exclude them? The local products of the Huai and island peoples and the Lai Yi [?] are listed alongside those of the interior commanderies of Qing and Xu in the Tribute of Yu. When did Yu of the Xia ever exclude them? The Man, Yi, Zhen, and Fan zones, together with the Hou, Dian, Nan, Cai, and Wei zones, all appear in the registers of the nine territorial zones. When did Kings Wen and Wu or the Duke of Zhou ever exclude them? When they became contentious and defiant [?], however, the emperor of Yu could not dispense with his campaign against the Sanmiao; the Shang ancestral ruler could not dispense with his punishment of the Guifang; and the Zhou king could not dispense with his attacks on the Xianyun and Kunyi. In those illustrious ages of full flourishing, could they have coveted those lands or hated their inhabitants, thereby putting our armies to toil? Their purpose was to unite what remained disunited under Heaven; this, too, was something undertaken only from the gravest necessity. If all things flourish but a single tree alone withers, the work of creation is incomplete; if an entire hall is feasting and laughing, yet someone [?] turns toward…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
隅之涖則君子非全仁聖王在上忍使蠻
夷猾夏延及平民為玉石之焚乎吾故曰
有大不獲已焉者耳是故王者之於戎狄
正朔不必加也瑞信不必通也同軌同文
同倫之化不必其一一不倍於我也其慕
義也則進之其猾夏也則膺之其入貢也
則禮之其悖慢也則絕之先之以文告繼
之以甲兵薄伐之而已矣羈縻之而已矣
固不肯置之度外亦不必留之度內固未
===
始不以中國視之亦未嘗純以中國視之
於無外之中實寓夫外之之法以殊視之
義而行夫一視之仁則上下相安遠近協
和邪氣不奸頌聲斯作王者大一統之氣
象固如是哉嗟乎中國之有夷狄猶陽之
有陰君子之有小人也內陽外陰然矣陰
可盡決乎內君子外小人是矣小人可盡
去乎內中國外四夷得矣夷狄可盡殄乎
後世此義不明始有欲窮兵黷武獸獮而
punctuated:
隅之涖，則君子非全仁。聖王在上，忍使蠻夷猾夏，延及平民，為玉石之焚乎？吾故曰：有大不獲已焉者耳。是故王者之於戎狄，正朔不必加也，瑞信不必通也，同軌同文同倫之化，不必其一一不倍於我也。其慕義也，則進之；其猾夏也，則膺之；其入貢也，則禮之；其悖慢也，則絕之。先之以文告，繼之以甲兵，薄伐之而已矣，羈縻之而已矣。固不肯置之度外，亦不必留之度內；固未始不以中國視之，亦未嘗純以中國視之。於無外之中，實寓夫外之之法；以殊視之義，而行夫一視之仁。則上下相安，遠近協和，邪氣不奸，頌聲斯作。王者大一統之氣象，固如是哉！

嗟乎！中國之有夷狄，猶陽之有陰，君子之有小人也。內陽外陰，然矣，陰可盡決乎？內君子外小人，是矣，小人可盡去乎？內中國外四夷，得矣，夷狄可盡殄乎？後世此義不明，始有欲窮兵黷武，獸獮而
translation_en:
…weeping in a corner [?], then the gentleman’s benevolence is incomplete. With a sage king above, could he bear to let the barbarians disturb the Chinese realm, their depredations reaching the common people, so that jade and stone alike are consumed in the flames? Thus I say: such action arises only from overwhelming necessity.

Therefore, in dealing with the Rong and Di, a king need not impose his calendar upon them or exchange tokens of credence with them. Nor need he require that, under the civilizing influence that makes carriage tracks, writing, and human relationships uniform, they conform to us in every particular. When they admire righteousness, he welcomes them; when they disturb the Chinese realm, he strikes them; when they bring tribute, he treats them with ritual courtesy; when they are rebellious and insolent, he severs relations with them. He first issues proclamations and then follows with armed force, doing no more than conducting limited punitive expeditions and maintaining loose control over them. Certainly he is unwilling to place them beyond his concern, yet he need not keep them within his administration. He has never failed to regard them as he regards the Central States, yet neither has he ever treated them entirely as the Central States.

Within the principle that none lies outside his sway, there is indeed a method for treating some as external. Through the righteousness of treating them differently, he practices the benevolence of regarding all alike. Then those above and below live at peace with one another, those far and near are in harmony, pernicious influences do not intrude, and songs of praise arise. Such indeed is the character of a king’s grand unification!

Alas! The Central States’ having Yi and Di is like yang’s having yin, or gentlemen’s having petty men. To place yang within and yin without is proper; but can yin be eliminated altogether? To place gentlemen within and petty men without is right; but can petty men all be removed? To place the Central States within and the barbarians of the four quarters without is fitting; but can the Yi and Di all be exterminated? In later ages, this principle was not understood, and so there arose those who wished to exhaust their armies and recklessly resort to warfare, hunting them down like beasts and…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
草雜之者卒之夷未及懲而華民已先敝
矣至於漢宣帝因匈奴款塞納蕭望之議
待以不臣之禮亂常失序其何以為訓乎
以若所為較諸受徵令於夷狄致金繒之
奉如賈誼之所譏置羌胡於塞內無出入
之防如江統之所論其事雖殊其為起釁
召患虧中國之體納外夷之侮一也是皆
昧於春秋之義惡足與論夫王者無外之
氣象抑洪惟我
===
朝
聖祖
神宗受
天命為四海九閩之主炎鄉瘴海日出日入之
地前代聲教所未通者皆納貢修朝禮世
膺
封𠛬比諸藩翰龍沙以北東西數千里建置
衛所幾二百餘署之官屬給以印章小大
聯絡下相爲用
punctuated:
草雜之者，卒之夷未及懲，而華民已先敝矣。至於漢宣帝因匈奴款塞，納蕭望之議，待以不臣之禮，亂常失序，其何以為訓乎？以若所為，較諸受徵令於夷狄，致金繒之奉，如賈誼之所譏；置羌胡於塞內，無出入之防，如江統之所論，其事雖殊，其為起釁召患，虧中國之體，納外夷之侮，一也。是皆昧於《春秋》之義，惡足與論夫王者無外之氣象？
抑洪惟我朝聖祖、神宗受天命，為四海九閩之主。炎鄉瘴海、日出日入之地，前代聲教所未通者，皆納貢修朝禮，世膺封𠛬，比諸藩翰。龍沙以北，東西數千里，建置衛所幾二百餘，署之官屬，給以印章，小大聯絡，下相爲用。
translation_en:
…and destroy them like weeds [?]. In the end, before the barbarians could be chastised, the Chinese people were already exhausted. As for Emperor Xuan of Han, when the Xiongnu came to the frontier seeking submission, he accepted Xiao Wangzhi’s proposal and treated them with ceremonies that did not require them to act as subjects. This disrupted established norms and upset the proper order: how could it serve as a model? Compare such conduct with accepting demands from the barbarians and presenting them with gold and silk, as Jia Yi criticized, or settling the Qiang and Hu within the frontier without precautions governing their entry and departure, as Jiang Tong discussed. Though these actions differed, they were alike in provoking conflict and inviting calamity, diminishing the dignity of the Central Kingdom and exposing it to the insults of foreign barbarians. All this arose from ignorance of the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals. How could such men be qualified to discuss the grand vision of a true king’s rule, which excludes no one?
Now, reverently considering our dynasty: Shengzu and Shenzong [?] received Heaven’s mandate to become lords of the Four Seas and the “Nine Min” [?]. The scorching lands and pestilential seas, the places where the sun rises and sets—lands never reached by the civilizing influence of earlier dynasties—all present tribute and observe the rites of attendance at court. Generation after generation, they receive enfeoffment [?], ranking alongside the realm’s protective feudatories. North of Longsha, across several thousand li from east to west, more than two hundred guards and battalions have been established, officials appointed to them, and official seals issued. Great and small are linked together, serving one another’s purposes below [?].

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
廟謨睿畧可謂極於無外者矣
朝廷以大字小之仁中覃外流無有間隔徼
之近事如交南之欲并占城哉迪以則辭
命加切責焉必悔過乃已卜則叛臣雖厚
貢求内附然非反其侵地歸其約束則不
之許至於哈密之見殘於邊境也尤軫
宵旰之慮未嘗以其無預於中國而置之
問噫視天下猶一家隆古帝王將復有過
於
===
今日者乎請以是頌我
國家大一統之盛
表
擬宋以趙抃爲殿中侍御史謝表
楊椮
同考試官訓導談　批〔騈儷之文難於雄渾此作得之〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔用事切當措詞整潔可嘉〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔讀此文者有宋君臣之美可以想見不知清獻當時有如此作否〕
punctuated:
廟謨睿畧，可謂極於無外者矣。朝廷以大字小之仁，中覃外流，無有間隔。徼之近事，如交南之欲并占城，哉迪以則辭命加切責焉，必悔過乃已。卜則叛臣雖厚貢求内附，然非反其侵地、歸其約束，則不之許。至於哈密之見殘於邊境也，尤軫宵旰之慮，未嘗以其無預於中國而置之問。噫！視天下猶一家，隆古帝王將復有過於今日者乎？請以是頌我國家大一統之盛。

表
擬宋以趙抃爲殿中侍御史謝表
楊椮
同考試官訓導談批〔騈儷之文難於雄渾，此作得之。〕
考試官教諭羅批〔用事切當，措詞整潔，可嘉。〕
考試官教諭孫批〔讀此文者，有宋君臣之美可以想見，不知清獻當時有如此作否？〕
translation_en:
The court’s counsels and sagacious strategies may truly be said to have reached the utmost extent, leaving none outside their embrace. With the benevolence by which the great nurture the small, the court’s influence spreads within and flows abroad without impediment. Consider recent events [?]: when Jiaonan sought to annex Zhancheng, the court issued stern reprimands in its diplomatic communications [preceding wording unclear], persisting until repentance was forthcoming. Although the rebellious minister Buze [?] offered lavish tribute and sought submission to the dynasty, permission was withheld unless he restored the territory he had seized and submitted to its restraints. As for Hami’s suffering devastation on the frontier, this particularly troubled the emperor in his labors from before dawn until late at night. He never neglected it merely because it had no bearing on China [?]. Ah! Regarding all under Heaven as one family—could even the emperors and kings of high antiquity have surpassed the present ruler? Let me therefore celebrate the splendor of our dynasty’s grand unification.

Memorial
A memorial of thanks, composed as if upon Zhao Bian’s appointment as Palace Censor under the Song
By Yang Sen
