Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor: 〔Vigor and grandeur are difficult to achieve in parallel prose; this composition achieves them.〕

Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: 〔The historical allusions are apt, and the wording orderly and clean. It merits praise.〕

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: 〔Readers of this composition can envision the admirable qualities of the Song ruler and his minister. I wonder whether Qingxian—Zhao Bian—wrote anything like this at the time.〕

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
伏以
桂後惠文作
君王之耳目
殿中執法振綱紀於
朝廷仰頒非分之
恩儆切殞身之懼〔臣 非〕誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊
惟黑豸峩冠在蘭臺獨難其選彤騶行道
於烏府尤謂之雄非徒整肅乎官儀職以
修明於
===
國是側
陛而坐九級爲之生風簪筆以書百僚望之
屏息行成徇補愧非廊廟之材韋絢叙遷
謬擬夔龍之武茲蓋伏遇
○○○○堯舜欽恭禹湯勤儉以文明而行健
體柔克以居高薄賦輕刑務農閑而捨末爭
而納戎帳之款捐餘積以撫遼裕之和萬
物皆受曲成匹夫咸得自盡四十年休養
生息之化千萬世重熙累洽之展然而視
punctuated:
伏以：桂後惠文，作君王之耳目；殿中執法，振綱紀於朝廷。仰頒非分之恩，儆切殞身之懼。〔臣 非〕誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟黑豸峩冠，在蘭臺獨難其選；彤騶行道，於烏府尤謂之雄。非徒整肅乎官儀，職以修明於國是。側陛而坐，九級爲之生風；簪筆以書，百僚望之屏息。行成徇補，愧非廊廟之材；韋絢叙遷，謬擬夔龍之武。
茲蓋伏遇○○○○，堯舜欽恭，禹湯勤儉，以文明而行健，體柔克以居高。薄賦輕刑，務農閑而捨末爭而納戎帳之款，捐餘積以撫遼裕之和。萬物皆受曲成，匹夫咸得自盡。四十年休養生息之化，千萬世重熙累洽之展。然而視
translation_en:
I humbly submit: Wearing the Huiwen cap, with its “gui hou” [?], one serves as the sovereign’s ears and eyes; enforcing the law within the palace, one upholds the governing order at court. I look up in gratitude for favor bestowed beyond my deserts, keenly apprehensive lest even giving my life prove insufficient. 〔Your servant Fei [?]〕 In utter fear and trembling, I bow my head to the ground again and again. I respectfully reflect that, with the black xiezhi upon their lofty caps, the officials of the Orchid Terrace are especially difficult to select; with red-clad mounted attendants proceeding along the roads, those of the Crow Office are particularly renowned for their authority. Their duty is not merely to impose decorum upon official conduct, but to clarify and uphold the guiding principles of government. Seated beside the palace steps, they inspire awe throughout its nine ascending tiers; taking up their writing brushes, they make all the officials hold their breath at the sight. “Conduct perfected, following and supplementing” [?], I am ashamed that I lack the talents required for high office; “Wei Xuan promoted in due order” [?], I am wrongly deemed capable of following in the footsteps of Kui and Long.
This is because I have humbly encountered ○○○○: reverent and respectful like Yao and Shun, diligent and frugal like Yu and Tang, vigorous in action through cultivated enlightenment, and exercising mastery through gentleness while occupying the highest position. You reduce taxes and lighten punishments, attend to agriculture—“leisure and abandoning secondary pursuits and contention” [?]—and accept professions of submission from the nomad encampments. You expend surplus stores to foster harmony in “Liao Yu” [?]. All beings receive your care, which brings each to fulfillment; every ordinary man can fully exert his abilities. For forty years, your transforming rule has enabled the people to rest, recover, and prosper; for countless generations, its flourishing peace and accumulated harmony will unfold [?]. Yet, in looking upon …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
民則無傷如傷圖治則雖盛李盛拾遺補
闕將求蹇諤之七人並蓄兼收罔棄芻蕘
之一得〔臣朴〕〔林忠〕天與戇直性成始通籍
以隨行因仍何補繼分符而出牧蹟效無
聞遲徊瘴癘之鄉躑躅孤危之跡不圖
妙簡進厠中司供奉
赤墀叅陪法從繡衣行部雖非持斧之威白
簡繩違已專橫搦之
寵幸免呈身而就列敢言正色以立
===
朝惟是君子小人之分最關理亂興衰之運
全才難得必須含垢而掩瑕餘蘖尚存勿
令投間而抵隙使衆賢得安其位斯庶績
可無不凝至于
王道之或弛或張衆論之有得有失謹當徐
陳利害公舉是非務殫尺寸之愚以荅便
蕃之
眷荀臨危授命尚當不顧以捐軀況爲善有徵
何惜盡忠而報
punctuated: 民則無傷如傷，圖治則雖盛李盛。拾遺補闕，將求蹇諤之七人；並蓄兼收，罔棄芻蕘之一得。〔臣朴〕〔林忠〕天與戇直，性成。始通籍以隨行，因仍何補？繼分符而出牧，蹟效無聞。遲徊瘴癘之鄉，躑躅孤危之跡。不圖妙簡，進厠中司，供奉赤墀，叅陪法從。繡衣行部，雖非持斧之威；白簡繩違，已專橫搦之寵。幸免呈身而就列，敢言正色以立朝。惟是君子小人之分，最關理亂興衰之運。全才難得，必須含垢而掩瑕；餘蘖尚存，勿令投間而抵隙。使衆賢得安其位，斯庶績可無不凝。至于王道之或弛或張，衆論之有得有失，謹當徐陳利害，公舉是非，務殫尺寸之愚，以荅便蕃之眷。荀臨危授命，尚當不顧以捐軀；況爲善有徵，何惜盡忠而報
translation_en:
…toward the people, You treat them as though they were suffering even when they are unharmed; in pursuing good government, even amid prosperity, [the following wording is unclear: 李盛][?]. To remedy omissions and deficiencies, You seek seven men of forthright remonstrance; embracing and accepting all, You discard not even a single useful insight from a grass-cutter or wood-gatherer.

〔Your servant Pu〕〔Lin Zhong〕: Heaven endowed us with blunt honesty, which became our nature. When first entered on the official registers to join the ranks, what contribution did we make by merely following established practice? Subsequently entrusted with tallies of office and sent out to govern, we achieved no results worthy of report. We lingered in lands of pestilential vapors and stumbled along a lonely, precarious course. Unexpectedly favored by Your discerning selection, we have advanced into the Censorate, to serve at the vermilion steps and join the officials attending upon You. Touring our jurisdictions in embroidered robes, we may lack the awe-inspiring authority of those who bear the axe; yet, with white tablets to censure wrongdoing, we have already received the special favor of authority to restrain [?]. Fortunately, we have taken our places without having to thrust ourselves forward; we dare to speak with a resolute countenance at court.

The distinction between gentlemen and petty men bears most closely upon the course of order and disorder, prosperity and decline. Since men of complete ability are hard to find, one must tolerate shortcomings and overlook blemishes. While remnants of evil still survive, they must not be allowed to exploit openings or penetrate gaps. If all worthy men can remain secure in their positions, every undertaking may thereby be brought to completion. As for whether the Kingly Way is relaxed or vigorously upheld, and whether the opinions expressed are sound or mistaken, we shall respectfully set forth benefits and harms in due course and impartially identify right and wrong. We shall strive to exhaust our meager understanding in repayment of Your abundant favor. If [?], when danger comes, we must surrender our lives, we ought even then to sacrifice ourselves without hesitation. How much less should we begrudge giving our utmost loyalty in repayment, when doing good has demonstrable effects …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
國臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
羅循
===
同考試官教諭郭　批〔鋪陳前代事實及歸重我朝用夏變夷之功詳整無遺〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔事實不遺揄揚得旨可錄〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔揄揚有據不為問目所窘〕
治法之行於前代者歷世有不同治法之
盛於
今日者無遠爲無弊甚矣自古帝王之有天
下未有不制禮明刑以爲治者禮之因革
punctuated:
國。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁塲，策，第一問。羅循。
同考試官教諭郭　批〔鋪陳前代事實及歸重我朝用夏變夷之功，詳整無遺。〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔事實不遺，揄揚得旨，可錄。〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔揄揚有據，不為問目所窘。〕
治法之行於前代者，歷世有不同；治法之盛於今日者，無遠爲無弊甚矣。自古帝王之有天下，未有不制禮明刑以爲治者。禮之因革，
translation_en:
…the state. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, is overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session: Policy Essay, First Question. Luo Xun.
Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition of the facts of preceding dynasties and the concluding emphasis on our dynasty’s achievement in transforming the barbarians through Chinese civilization are detailed, orderly, and complete.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔No relevant facts are omitted; the praise accords with the intended purport. Worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔The praise is well grounded; the candidate is not constrained by the question’s particulars.〕
The methods of government practiced under preceding dynasties differed from age to age; those flourishing today reach everywhere and are free of defects [?]. Since antiquity, no emperor or king who possessed All Under Heaven has failed to establish rites and clarify punishments as means of governing. As for the retention or alteration of rites…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
刑之寬猛則以時異世殊不能無其弊也
然而修五禮以變壞亂之風嚴五刑以救
寬縱之失如我
聖祖之制作更新規模宏遠鑿鑿乎其不可易
者質之往古固無可疑而垂之後世亦豈
復有其弊歟請因明問而陳之禮與刑相
爲表裏要在使民同歸于善而已粤自伯
夷降典折民惟刑皐陶明刑以弼五教二
者並用在唐虞之時有可見也逮至成周
===
大宗伯掌五禮以吉禮事鬼神以凶禮厚
邦國以賓禮親邦國以軍禮同邦國以嘉
禮親萬民先王之禮秩然其有序也然一
存於魯而季札之歎興再廢於秦而蕭葭
之剸作禮於是乎日隳矣成周大司寇掌
五刑野刑上功糾力軍刑上命糾守鄉刑
上德糾孝官刑上能糾職國刑上愿糾暴
先王之刑井然其有條也然自魏文侯師
李悝而科條始繁秦孝公用商鞅而蔓延
punctuated: 刑之寬猛，則以時異世殊，不能無其弊也。然而修五禮以變壞亂之風，嚴五刑以救寬縱之失，如我聖祖之制作更新，規模宏遠，鑿鑿乎其不可易者，質之往古，固無可疑，而垂之後世，亦豈復有其弊歟？請因明問而陳之。禮與刑相爲表裏，要在使民同歸于善而已。粤自伯夷降典，折民惟刑，皐陶明刑以弼五教，二者並用，在唐虞之時有可見也。逮至成周，大宗伯掌五禮：以吉禮事鬼神，以凶禮厚邦國，以賓禮親邦國，以軍禮同邦國，以嘉禮親萬民。先王之禮，秩然其有序也。然一存於魯，而季札之歎興；再廢於秦，而蕭葭之剸作，禮於是乎日隳矣。成周大司寇掌五刑：野刑上功糾力，軍刑上命糾守，鄉刑上德糾孝，官刑上能糾職，國刑上愿糾暴。先王之刑，井然其有條也。然自魏文侯師李悝，而科條始繁；秦孝公用商鞅，而蔓延
translation_en:
…and the leniency or severity of punishments vary with the times and the age, and thus cannot be free of defects. Yet consider how our Sagely Progenitor renewed institutions: he reformed the five rites to transform corrupt and disorderly customs, and made the five punishments strict to remedy the failings of excessive leniency. His design was comprehensive and far-reaching, its principles manifestly unalterable. Tested against antiquity, it surely admits of no doubt; handed down to later generations, how could it again give rise to such defects? Allow me to explain in response to your illuminating question.

Rites and punishments complement one another as outer form and inner support. Their essential purpose is simply to bring all the people alike to goodness. From the time when Bo Yi promulgated the statutes and punishments were used to restrain the people, and Gao Yao clarified punishments to support the five teachings, we can see that both were employed together in the age of Tang and Yu.

By the time of the fully established Zhou, the Minister of Rites administered the five rites: through auspicious rites he served the spirits; through mourning rites he fostered solidarity among the states; through guest rites he cultivated friendship among the states; through military rites he united the states; and through celebratory rites he fostered affection among all the people. The rites of the former kings were methodically ordered. Yet when they survived only in Lu, Ji Zha voiced his admiration; when they were subsequently abolished under Qin, there arose the “cutting of mugwort and reeds” [?]. From this point, rites deteriorated day by day.

Under the fully established Zhou, the Minister of Justice administered the five punishments: punishments in the countryside esteemed achievement and scrutinized exertion; military punishments esteemed obedience to commands and scrutinized the keeping of assigned posts; punishments in the townships esteemed virtue and scrutinized filial conduct; punishments for officials esteemed competence and scrutinized the discharge of duties; and punishments in the capital esteemed integrity and checked violence. The punishments of the former kings were systematically regulated. Yet after Marquis Wen of Wei took Li Kui as his teacher, statutory provisions began to multiply; when Duke Xiao of Qin employed Shang Yang, they proliferated…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
無際刑於是乎日增矣三代而下經國垂
遠蔚然可稱者曰漢曰唐曰宋唐之禮制
於貞觀者多蹈隋人之遺轍宋之禮成於
開寶者多拾五季之餘燼皆有因而無革
也至如漢高帝以開基之英主而於祠祭
一詔則因因秦之舊矣其後雖有叔孫綿
蕝之制猶未之講而亦何嘗變乎我
太祖之於禮也革之而無遺今伏讀
大祀之文有曰南北之壇終不會祀於禮未然
===
於是以義而起合祭之典蓋肇行於定鼎
之初焉不特此耳若禮之燦於元者則盡
取而去之觀其彰祭祀之禮則神祇之號
正定喪服之禮則父母之衰同正婚姻之
禮則同姓之辯嚴復衣冠之禮而服色改
明上下之禮而品制修是皆斷以大義行
之天下燦然著
日月之麗天也唐以仁義而縱死囚之四百
宋以大辟而行贖死之法今皆去嚴而尚
punctuated:
無際，刑於是乎日增矣。三代而下，經國垂遠，蔚然可稱者，曰漢、曰唐、曰宋。唐之禮制於貞觀者，多蹈隋人之遺轍；宋之禮成於開寶者，多拾五季之餘燼，皆有因而無革也。至如漢高帝，以開基之英主，而於祠祭一詔，則因因秦之舊矣。其後雖有叔孫綿蕝之制，猶未之講，而亦何嘗變乎？我太祖之於禮也，革之而無遺。今伏讀大祀之文，有曰：「南北之壇，終不會祀，於禮未然。」於是以義而起，合祭之典，蓋肇行於定鼎之初焉。不特此耳，若禮之燦於元者，則盡取而去之。觀其彰祭祀之禮，則神祇之號正；定喪服之禮，則父母之衰同；正婚姻之禮，則同姓之辯嚴；復衣冠之禮，而服色改；明上下之禮，而品制修。是皆斷以大義，行之天下，燦然著，日月之麗天也。
唐以仁義而縱死囚之四百，宋以大辟而行贖死之法，今皆去嚴而尚
translation_en:
…without limit; punishments thus increased day by day. After the Three Dynasties, those whose governance of the realm and enduring legacy stood out as worthy of praise were the Han, Tang, and Song. The Tang rites established during the Zhenguan era largely followed the tracks left by the Sui; the Song rites completed during the Kaibao era largely gathered up the remaining embers of the Five Dynasties. Both continued inherited practices without reforming them. As for Emperor Gao of Han, although he was an outstanding founding ruler, in one edict concerning sacrifices he simply followed the old Qin practices—the transcription repeats “followed” [?]. Later, although there were Shusun’s ritual arrangements, marked out with cords and bundles of reeds, these matters had still not been fully examined. When, indeed, had they ever been changed?
Our Taizu, in his treatment of rites, reformed them comprehensively. Now, reverently reading his text on the Great Sacrifice, I find these words: “The southern and northern altars have never held a joint sacrifice; this is not proper according to ritual.” Thereupon, acting on what was right, he instituted the ceremony of joint sacrifice, which began in the earliest days of the dynasty’s establishment. Nor was this all. As for rites that had flourished under the Yuan [?], he removed them entirely. Consider how, in giving prominence to sacrificial rites, he rectified the titles of the spirits of Heaven and Earth; in establishing mourning rites, he made the mourning garments for fathers and mothers the same; in rectifying marriage rites, he strictly enforced the distinction concerning people of the same surname; in restoring the rites governing dress and headgear, he changed the colors of garments; and in clarifying the rites governing superiors and inferiors, he revised the regulations for ranks. All these measures were decided according to overarching principles of right and put into practice throughout the realm, manifest in their brilliance like the sun and moon shining in Heaven.
The Tang, invoking benevolence and righteousness, released four hundred prisoners condemned to death; the Song instituted a law permitting redemption from capital punishment. Here the text says that all now abandoned severity and prized [?]…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
寛也至如漢高帝以創業之雄材而於入
關一論則固反苛以寛矣其後雖有官吏
論決之獄猶來之報而亦何嘗究乎我
太祖之於刑也執之而無縱令伏讀
大赦之詔有曰詿誤盡赦若果真犯雖笞不原
於是以威而治尚嚴之意盖益謹於
即位之久焉不特此耳若刑之壊於元者則
盡刻而滌之觀其刑里閭之豪俠刑闒閮
之混淆刑州縣之廢格官吏之貪墨者必
===
刑舊染之未革者必刑是皆不拘章程拖
之天下赫然若
雷霆之動物也其視前代繼世之君制禮明
刑曼乎莫能及矣而說者乃謂漢高之起
沛中與我
太祖之龍飛淮甸肇造基業大畧可擬而其因
革寛猛之間何相去若是之遠噫是盖有
其故矣元以夷狄入主中國化冠裳爲胡
服汙腥膻於俎豆豪家椽守上儗王公同
punctuated: 寛也。至如漢高帝，以創業之雄材，而於入關一論，則固反苛以寛矣。其後雖有官吏論決之獄、猶來之報，而亦何嘗究乎？我太祖之於刑也，執之而無縱。令伏讀大赦之詔，有曰：「詿誤盡赦，若果真犯，雖笞不原。」於是以威而治，尚嚴之意，盖益謹於即位之久焉。不特此耳，若刑之壊於元者，則盡刻而滌之。觀其刑里閭之豪俠，刑闒閮之混淆，刑州縣之廢格，官吏之貪墨者必刑，舊染之未革者必刑，是皆不拘章程，拖之天下，赫然若雷霆之動物也。其視前代繼世之君，制禮明刑，曼乎莫能及矣。而說者乃謂漢高之起沛中，與我太祖之龍飛淮甸，肇造基業，大畧可擬，而其因革寛猛之間，何相去若是之遠？噫，是盖有其故矣！元以夷狄入主中國，化冠裳爲胡服，汙腥膻於俎豆，豪家椽守，上儗王公，同
translation_en: …leniency. As for Emperor Gao of the Han, with his outstanding ability as the founder of a dynasty, in his pronouncement upon entering the passes he certainly replaced harshness with leniency. Although afterward there were cases adjudicated by officials and reports that still came in [?], when did he ever pursue them thoroughly? Our Taizu, in his use of punishments, enforced them without indulgence. Now, reverently reading the edict of general amnesty, we find it says: “All who have erred inadvertently shall be pardoned. Those who have truly committed offenses shall not be pardoned, even if their punishment is merely beating with the light stick.” Thus he governed through awe-inspiring authority; his commitment to severity became still more scrupulous as the years following his accession accumulated. Nor was this all. Wherever penal administration had deteriorated under the Yuan, he sternly purged its abuses. Consider how he punished the powerful local bravos, punished the confusion of distinctions at the gates [?], and punished obstruction and non-enforcement in prefectures and counties. Corrupt officials were invariably punished, as were those who had not reformed their ingrained abuses. In all this he was not constrained by established regulations, but extended his measures throughout the realm [?], as awesome as thunder stirring all living things. In establishing ritual and making punishments clear, he so surpassed the rulers who had inherited earlier dynasties that none could match him. Yet commentators say that Han Gao’s rise in Pei and our Taizu’s dragonlike ascent in the Huai region were broadly comparable in laying the foundations of their dynasties. Why, then, were they so far apart in retaining or reforming institutions, and in leniency or severity? Ah, there was surely a reason! The Yuan entered China as alien peoples and became its rulers, transforming caps and robes into foreign dress and defiling the ritual vessels with their rank, mutton-smelling ways. Powerful households and local administrators [?] presumed to rival princes and dukes above them; those of the same…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
姓婚姻內連兄弟先王之禮至是而盡亡
矣安得不變乎故漢繼秦後猶存前代之
制禮之因者不害其同也比附與制曲赦
無時姦吏盜舞文之舉而僭逸稱罔之說
先王之刑至是而大壞矣安得不嚴乎故
漢懲秦暴悉起膏火之餘刑之反者不害
其寬也雖然制度相沿歷數世而復改寬
仁未幾一再傳而已刻此漢高之治止於
焉工而畫繞可繼之道然未盡善焉由是
===
宏謨淵筭上疑乎百王
論之則知
聖德神功下兼乎萬世以刑之嚴者為肆時之
務以禮之華者為垂遠之規至於典章文
物既備見于
制書而守成尚寬復昭示于
祖訓則又有以廓
造化之至仁弘
範圍之大典質之三代以來不可誣也
punctuated: 姓婚姻，內連兄弟，先王之禮至是而盡亡矣，安得不變乎？故漢繼秦後，猶存前代之制，禮之因者不害其同也。比附與制，曲赦無時，姦吏盜舞文之舉，而僭逸稱罔之說，先王之刑至是而大壞矣，安得不嚴乎？故漢懲秦暴，悉起膏火之餘，刑之反者不害其寬也。雖然，制度相沿，歷數世而復改；寬仁未幾，一再傳而已刻。此漢高之治止於焉工，而畫繞可繼之道，然未盡善焉。由是，宏謨淵筭，上疑乎百王；論之，則知聖德神功，下兼乎萬世。以刑之嚴者為肆時之務，以禮之華者為垂遠之規。至於典章文物，既備見于制書，而守成尚寬，復昭示于祖訓，則又有以廓造化之至仁，弘範圍之大典，質之三代以來，不可誣也。
translation_en:
…marriages between people of the same surname, with marital connections extending even among brothers within the family. The rites of the former kings had by then disappeared entirely. How could they fail to be changed? The Han, however, succeeded the Qin when institutions of earlier ages still survived; in retaining inherited rites, there was no harm in preserving these similarities. Legal analogies and enactments [?], and partial pardons granted without regular timing, gave rise to corrupt clerks’ manipulation of legal texts and to claims marked by usurpation, license, and deception [?]. The punishments of the former kings had by then been thoroughly corrupted. How could severity be avoided? The Han, however, took warning from Qin brutality and arose amid the remnants of its consuming fires; in reversing its penal practices, there was no harm in leniency.

Nevertheless, its institutions were carried on only to be altered again after several generations; its generous benevolence scarcely lasted, and after one or two successions government was already harsh. Here the government of Gaozu of Han reached its limit [?]; although it outlined a course that successors could follow [?], it had not attained complete excellence. From this, the grand designs and profound calculations rivaled those of the hundred kings of antiquity [?]; considering the matter, we recognize that the sagely virtue and divine achievements embrace all succeeding ages. Severity in punishment was treated as the business of the time [?], and the splendor of ritual as a pattern to be transmitted into the distant future. The statutes, institutions, and forms of civilized governance were already fully set forth in imperial enactments, while the preference for leniency in preserving the established achievement was again clearly proclaimed in the Ancestral Instructions. Thus there was also a means to extend the supreme benevolence of the creative workings of Heaven and Earth and to enlarge the great ordering norms. Measured against the record from the Three Dynasties onward, this cannot be denied.

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖子
神孫恪遵
成憲百餘年間
朝廷上下從容乎禮制之中普天率土循行
乎法度之內
天休滋至
宗社奠安
用夏變夷之功蓋自是以至
億萬斯年與太平之基業同一無疆惟休也
愚何幸躬逢其盛
===
第二問　張子渭
同考試官訓導黃　批〔不拘拘於問目當是篆手〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔引斷切當必究心於篆學者〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔斷功罪如指諸掌雖起數子〕
〔於九京當必心服〕
從祀定於前代者不可輕議其黜從祀加
於後代者不可輕議其進蓋前代所定從
punctuated:
聖子神孫恪遵成憲，百餘年間，朝廷上下從容乎禮制之中，普天率土循行乎法度之內。天休滋至，宗社奠安。用夏變夷之功，蓋自是以至億萬斯年，與太平之基業同一無疆，惟休也。愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第二問，張子渭。
同考試官訓導黃批〔不拘拘於問目，當是篆手。〕
考試官教諭羅批〔引斷切當，必究心於篆學者。〕
考試官教諭孫批〔斷功罪如指諸掌，雖起數子〕〔於九京，當必心服。〕

從祀定於前代者，不可輕議其黜；從祀加於後代者，不可輕議其進。蓋前代所定從
translation_en:
The sagely sons and divine grandsons have reverently followed the established statutes. For more than a hundred years, all ranks at court have acted with ease within the institutions of ritual, while everyone throughout the realm has conducted themselves within the laws and regulations. Heaven’s blessings have grown ever more abundant, and the ancestral temples and altars of state have been securely established. The achievement of transforming the uncivilized through Chinese civilization will, from this time onward through countless millions of years, endure without limit alongside the foundations of the age of peace. How glorious it is! How fortunate I, in my humble capacity, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

Second policy question. Zhang Ziwei.
Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔“He does not confine himself narrowly to the question’s particulars; he must be an accomplished seal-script writer [?].”〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔“His citations and judgments are apt and precise; he must have devoted himself to the study of seal script [?].”〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔“He judges merits and faults as clearly as if pointing to things in his palm. Even if these several masters were raised”〕〔“from their graves, they would surely be convinced in their hearts.”〕

For those whose subsidiary worship was established in earlier ages, one must not lightly propose their removal; for those whose subsidiary worship is to be added in later ages, one must not lightly propose their admission. For the subsidiary worship established in earlier ages …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
祀皆有深意如洙泗及門之徒躬受聖教
故雖姓名之外他無可考亦不敢遺漢唐
專門之師傳授聖經故雖學行之疵實有
可指亦不敢棄若後世所論從祀之賢雖
不能無可取然非真有發揮聖經維持聖
道之功又安敢輕進之哉嗚呼孔廟從祀
朝廷大禮也旣有
定制矣而執事舉以下詢得無禮求之野之意
乎顧愚何足以知之雖然亦嘗聞之矣且
===
孔門諸徒如家語所載七十四賢史記所
載七十七賢文翁石室則但七十二賢而
唐祀因之杜祐通典則有八十三賢而宋
祀因之以賈逵等二十二人並爲先師則
始於唐之貞觀以曾參等六十七人並爲
列伯則昉于唐之開元至以孟子繼顏曾
思爲四配升顓孫師於十哲則又至宋而
始定焉若其封爵名位之增進代各不同
我
punctuated: 祀，皆有深意。如洙泗及門之徒，躬受聖教，故雖姓名之外他無可考，亦不敢遺；漢唐專門之師，傳授聖經，故雖學行之疵實有可指，亦不敢棄。若後世所論從祀之賢，雖不能無可取，然非真有發揮聖經、維持聖道之功，又安敢輕進之哉？嗚呼！孔廟從祀，朝廷大禮也，旣有定制矣，而執事舉以下詢，得無禮求之野之意乎？顧愚何足以知之？雖然，亦嘗聞之矣。且孔門諸徒，如《家語》所載七十四賢，《史記》所載七十七賢，文翁石室則但七十二賢，而唐祀因之；杜祐《通典》則有八十三賢，而宋祀因之。以賈逵等二十二人並爲先師，則始於唐之貞觀；以曾參等六十七人並爲列伯，則昉于唐之開元。至以孟子繼顏、曾、思爲四配，升顓孫師於十哲，則又至宋而始定焉。若其封爵名位之增進，代各不同。我
translation_en: …the arrangements for associated worship all had profound purposes. For example, the disciples who entered the Master's school by the Zhu and Si rivers personally received the Sage's instruction. Thus, even where nothing beyond their names can be ascertained, we dare not omit them. The specialist masters of the Han and Tang transmitted the sacred classics. Thus, even where definite faults in their learning and conduct can be identified, we dare not discard them. As for worthy men of later ages proposed for associated worship, although they certainly have their merits, unless they truly contributed to elucidating the sacred classics and sustaining the Way of the Sage, how could we dare admit them lightly? Alas! Associated worship in the Confucian temple is a great rite of the court, for which established regulations already exist. Yet you gentlemen have raised this matter to inquire of those below you: might your intention be to seek knowledge of ritual among the common people? But how could someone as ignorant as I be qualified to understand it? Nevertheless, I have heard something of the matter. Among the disciples of Confucius, for instance, the Family Sayings of Confucius records seventy-four worthies, and the Records of the Grand Historian seventy-seven; Wen Weng's Stone Chamber has only seventy-two, and Tang sacrificial practice followed this. Du You's Comprehensive Institutions, however, has eighty-three, and Song sacrificial practice followed this. The designation of Jia Kui and twenty-one others as Former Teachers began in the Zhenguan reign of the Tang; the ennoblement of Zeng Shen and sixty-six others as earls began in the Kaiyuan reign of the Tang. As for placing Mengzi alongside Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, and Zisi to form the Four Correlates, and elevating Zhuansun Shi to the Ten Wise Ones, these arrangements were not settled until the Song. Increases and promotions in their noble titles, designations, and ritual positions differed from dynasty to dynasty. Our…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
朝準前代之制自國學達於天下其禮無貳
正統間禮官復得
旨詳定東廡增至五十五人西廡增至五十五
人而胡文定真西山蔡仲默吳幼清皆前
代之所未及也夫與祀於前者若是其多
增祀於後者若是其寡難易之間誠若有
可疑者請竟其說世衰道微火於秦黃老
於漢佛於魏晉之間而所謂經師者守其
遺編轉相付授講說註釋各竭其材使後
===
之學者得見先王詩書典籍之盛其功固
不小也故雖劉向之無威儀王肅之好諛
佞宗莊老之王弼忽細行之賈逵杜預建
短喪之蔡馬融甘附勢之恥君子不敢輕
議其黜焉逮夫五緯聚奎諸儒闡道之後
則非其識足以明至理於毫釐行足以希
往聖之絕迹功足以為遺經之羽翼者不
得而與也故雖范希文之忠孝歐陽永叔
之節義游楊謝蔡之於學不為無傳何王
punctuated: 朝準前代之制，自國學達於天下，其禮無貳。正統間，禮官復得旨詳定，東廡增至五十五人，西廡增至五十五人，而胡文定、真西山、蔡仲默、吳幼清皆前代之所未及也。夫與祀於前者若是其多，增祀於後者若是其寡，難易之間，誠若有可疑者。請竟其說。世衰道微，火於秦，黃老於漢，佛於魏晉之間，而所謂經師者，守其遺編，轉相付授，講說註釋，各竭其材，使後之學者得見先王詩書典籍之盛，其功固不小也。故雖劉向之無威儀、王肅之好諛佞、宗莊老之王弼、忽細行之賈逵杜預、建短喪之蔡、馬融甘附勢之恥，君子不敢輕議其黜焉。逮夫五緯聚奎，諸儒闡道之後，則非其識足以明至理於毫釐、行足以希往聖之絕迹、功足以為遺經之羽翼者，不得而與也。故雖范希文之忠孝、歐陽永叔之節義，游楊謝蔡之於學不為無傳，何王
translation_en:
…the dynasty follows the institutions of earlier dynasties: from the Directorate of Education throughout the realm, the rites are uniform. During the Zhengtong reign, the ritual officials again received an imperial command to settle the details. Those honored in the eastern side hall were increased to fifty-five, and those in the western side hall to fifty-five. Hu Wending, Zhen Xishan, Cai Zhongmo, and Wu Youqing were all figures whom earlier dynasties had not included. Those admitted to the sacrifices in earlier times were so numerous, while those added later were so few. This difference in the ease or difficulty of admission does indeed seem to raise doubts. Allow me to complete the explanation.

As the age declined and the Way grew faint, there were the burning of books under the Qin, the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi under the Han, and Buddhism during the Wei and Jin. Yet the men known as masters of the Classics preserved the surviving texts and transmitted them from one to another. Through exposition and annotation, each exerted his abilities to the utmost, enabling later scholars to behold the abundance of the former kings’ Poetry, Documents, and other canonical writings. Their contribution was certainly considerable. Thus, despite Liu Xiang’s lack of dignified deportment, Wang Su’s fondness for flattery, Wang Bi’s devotion to Zhuangzi and Laozi, Jia Kui’s and Du Yu’s neglect of minor points of conduct, Cai’s advocacy of shortened mourning [?], and Ma Rong’s willingness to endure the shame of attaching himself to the powerful, gentlemen dared not lightly propose their removal from the sacrifices.

But after the five planets gathered in the constellation Kui and the various Confucian scholars elucidated the Way, no one could be admitted unless his understanding sufficed to discern ultimate principle in its finest subtleties, his conduct sufficed to aspire to the unsurpassed example of the ancient sages, and his achievements sufficed to support the transmitted Classics. Thus, despite Fan Xiwen’s loyalty and filial piety and Ouyang Yongshu’s integrity and righteousness, and although You, Yang, Xie, and Cai were by no means without a transmission of learning, He and Wang…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
金許之於道不為無見君子不敢輕議其
進焉蓋其選滋艱矣若乃元儒劉靜修德
性剛正學識明悟進退安於義命志節拔
於流俗不可謂之非賢矣我
朝薛文清直躬慕古談道淑徒進無附麗退
不留戀亦可謂之名臣矣言者遽欲儕之
從祀吾不知二公之學之功較之楊龜山
諸儒果孰先孰後乎
廷議報罷良有以也夫從祀之典參定於古
===
今不可易者如此然一得之愚竊有獻焉
有若之賢游夏謂其似聖人誠非苟然必
其言行氣象有過人者如論語所載論孝
弟論禮和數章良非群弟子可及彼宰予
晝寢短喪之失見斥於其師顓孫堂堂未
仁之病見短於其友宰予名列四科猶有
可議者以顓孫補孟軻吾不知較諸有若
為孰賢也公伯寮他無所考惟以愬子路
一事廁名魯論得參俎豆之列夫景伯在
punctuated:
金、許之於道，不為無見，君子不敢輕議其進焉。蓋其選滋艱矣。若乃元儒劉靜修，德性剛正，學識明悟，進退安於義命，志節拔於流俗，不可謂之非賢矣。我朝薛文清，直躬慕古，談道淑徒，進無附麗，退不留戀，亦可謂之名臣矣。言者遽欲儕之從祀，吾不知二公之學之功，較之楊龜山諸儒，果孰先孰後乎？廷議報罷，良有以也。夫從祀之典，參定於古今，不可易者如此。然一得之愚，竊有獻焉。
有若之賢，游、夏謂其似聖人，誠非苟然，必其言行氣象有過人者。如《論語》所載論孝弟、論禮和數章，良非群弟子可及。彼宰予晝寢、短喪之失，見斥於其師；顓孫堂堂、未仁之病，見短於其友。宰予名列四科，猶有可議者；以顓孫補孟軻，吾不知較諸有若為孰賢也。公伯寮他無所考，惟以愬子路一事廁名《魯論》，得參俎豆之列。夫景伯在
translation_en:
…Jin and Xu were not without insight into the Way, yet gentlemen dare not lightly propose their admission to the associated sacrifices to Confucius. Selection has indeed become increasingly exacting. Consider the Yuan scholar Liu Jingxiu: his moral character was firm and upright, his learning clear and perceptive. In entering or withdrawing from service, he rested content in righteousness and Heaven’s decree; his resolve and integrity rose above prevailing vulgarity. He certainly cannot be denied the designation of a worthy. Xue Wenqing of our dynasty conducted himself uprightly and admired antiquity, expounded the Way and cultivated his pupils. In office he attached himself to no powerful patron; in retirement he felt no lingering attachment to office. He too may be called an eminent minister. Those submitting proposals hastily wished to place these two among those receiving associated sacrifices. Yet I do not know how their learning and achievements actually rank against those of Yang Guishan and the other scholars. There was good reason for the court’s deliberations to result in rejection. Such are the unalterable principles governing associated sacrifices, established through consideration of past and present. Nevertheless, I venture to offer one modest insight.
You Ruo was so worthy that Ziyou and Zixia said he resembled the Sage. Surely this was no casual remark: his words, conduct, and bearing must have surpassed those of others. The several passages recorded in the Analects in which he discusses filial devotion and fraternal respect, ritual propriety and harmony, are truly beyond what the other disciples could match. Zai Yu’s faults—sleeping during the day and advocating a shorter mourning period—were condemned by his teacher. Zhuansun’s failings—his imposing manner and his lack of humaneness—were criticized by his friends. Even Zai Yu’s inclusion among the four categories of accomplished disciples leaves room for discussion. As for installing Zhuansun in the place vacated by Meng Ke, I do not know who was worthier when he is compared with You Ruo. Nothing else about Gongbo Liao can be ascertained: his name appears in the Lu Analects solely because he slandered Zilu, yet he has gained a place among those receiving sacrificial offerings. Now Jingbo, at …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
當時尚欲肆之市朝萬世之下顧從而祀
之夫子之庭其可乎至所謂荀況者以性
爲惡以禮爲僞以古先聖王爲不足法以
子思孟軻爲亂天下且其所事者奸邪之
黄歇所教者坑焚之李斯定罪行辟當不
在揚雄之下然卒未有能建議黜之者此
又不可曉之甚也草野之見所未安者如
此至於郡學削兩廡縣學並削十哲大儒
嘗有是議然自後人景行仰止者言之不
===
病其爲贅也子雖齊聖不先父食昔人嘗
有是疑然自後世報功崇德者視之不容
以其私論也是或一道而不足以爲典禮
之疵者故愚不及致詳噫言及之而不言
謂之隱執事柔其所極言者達之
朝廷其所未詳者以俟後之君子幸甚
第三問
楊揫
同考試官訓導談　批〔光明正大之氣委曲忠厚之〕
punctuated:
當時尚欲肆之市朝，萬世之下，顧從而祀之夫子之庭，其可乎？至所謂荀況者，以性爲惡，以禮爲僞，以古先聖王爲不足法，以子思、孟軻爲亂天下。且其所事者奸邪之黄歇，所教者坑焚之李斯，定罪行辟，當不在揚雄之下。然卒未有能建議黜之者，此又不可曉之甚也。草野之見所未安者如此。至於郡學削兩廡，縣學並削十哲，大儒嘗有是議。然自後人景行仰止者言之，不病其爲贅也。「子雖齊聖，不先父食」，昔人嘗有是疑。然自後世報功崇德者視之，不容以其私論也。是或一道而不足以爲典禮之疵者，故愚不及致詳。噫！言及之而不言，謂之隱。執事柔其所極言者，達之朝廷；其所未詳者，以俟後之君子，幸甚。
第三問
楊揫
同考試官訓導談批〔光明正大之氣，委曲忠厚之〕
translation_en:
…at the time even wished to expose his corpse in the marketplace or at court. Yet, countless generations later, we instead offer him sacrifices in the Master's temple courtyard. Can this be acceptable? As for the man called Xun Kuang, he regarded human nature as evil and ritual as artifice; he held that the sage kings of antiquity were unworthy of emulation and that Zisi and Meng Ke brought disorder to the world. Moreover, the man he served was the treacherous Huang Xie, and the man he taught was Li Si, responsible for burying scholars and burning books. If his guilt were determined and punishment imposed, it surely should be no lighter than Yang Xiong's. Yet no one has ultimately been able to propose removing him from the sacrifices. This is even more utterly incomprehensible. Such are the matters that trouble me, viewing them as a man outside official service.
As for abolishing the sacrifices in the two side galleries at prefectural schools, and additionally abolishing those to the Ten Philosophers at county schools, eminent Confucian scholars have indeed proposed this. But from the standpoint of later generations who look up to these exemplary figures, their inclusion need not be considered superfluous. “Even if a son equals a sage, he does not eat before his father”: earlier men have indeed expressed doubts on this account. Yet, viewed in terms of later generations repaying merit and honoring virtue, the matter cannot be judged by their private family relationships. This may be one line of reasoning, but it does not suffice to establish a defect in the prescribed rites; therefore I have not gone into detail. Alas! To remain silent when speech is called for is termed concealment. If you, honored sir, would temper [?] the points I have argued most forcefully and convey them to the court, leaving what I have not fully explained for worthy men of later times, I would be most fortunate.
Third Question
Yang Jiu
Associate Examiner Tan, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔An open and upright spirit, and a considerate and generous…〕

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
風於是乎兩見之他日進用必將為真御史也
考試官教諭羅　批〔如此議論足知其器局矣〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔其氣勃勃可槩以循行數墨〕
士得耶
御史之設厥惟舊矣戰國以前御史掌書
傳命而兼記事之任是其官尚輕也秦漢
而降乎章報奏之外得兼彈擊之任而拳
始重矣自唐以來御史職專察劾而兼訟
獄之事是其拳固重也由宋至今彈劾訟
===
獄之外又加言事之責而任愈難矣請陳
其故曰察劾不過指摘群臣之過失凡嚴
於疾惡者皆可為之曰訟獄不過平反刑
名之過悞凡明於聽訟者皆可為之至兼
言事則上焉以正君心下焉以正百官而
綱紀之在朝廷賴以匡扶風俗之在天下
賴以救正非諸司百執事之比矣況劾人
臣之過易攻人主之失難蘡鈞之壓何物
得全人非喪心孰不惜死君天下者不擇
punctuated:
風於是乎兩見之，他日進用，必將為真御史也。
考試官教諭羅，批〔如此議論，足知其器局矣〕。
考試官教諭孫，批〔其氣勃勃，可槩以循行數墨〕士得耶？
御史之設，厥惟舊矣。戰國以前，御史掌書傳命，而兼記事之任，是其官尚輕也。秦漢而降，乎章報奏之外，得兼彈擊之任，而拳始重矣。自唐以來，御史職專察劾，而兼訟獄之事，是其拳固重也。由宋至今，彈劾訟獄之外，又加言事之責，而任愈難矣。請陳其故，曰：察劾不過指摘群臣之過失，凡嚴於疾惡者，皆可為之；曰：訟獄不過平反刑名之過悞，凡明於聽訟者，皆可為之。至兼言事，則上焉以正君心，下焉以正百官，而綱紀之在朝廷，賴以匡扶；風俗之在天下，賴以救正，非諸司百執事之比矣。況劾人臣之過易，攻人主之失難。蘡鈞之壓，何物得全？人非喪心，孰不惜死？君天下者不擇
translation_en:
…a manner of conduct: both are evident here. When he is advanced to office in the future, he will surely become a true censor.
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “Such arguments suffice to reveal his capacity and breadth of vision.”
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “His spirit is vigorous. Can he be classed with scholars who merely follow the lines and count the ink marks [?]?”
The establishment of censors dates far back. Before the Warring States period, censors managed documents and transmitted commands, while also recording events; their office was still of modest consequence. From the Qin and Han onward, besides handling memorials and reports to the throne [?], they also acquired responsibility for impeachment, and their authority [?] began to grow weighty. From the Tang onward, censors were charged principally with investigation and impeachment, while also handling litigation and criminal cases; their authority [?] was thus firmly established as weighty. From the Song down to the present, beyond impeachment and judicial matters, they have also been charged with speaking out on affairs of government, making their duties still more difficult.
Allow me to explain why. Investigation and impeachment amount merely to identifying the faults of the assembled officials: anyone resolute in hating wrongdoing can undertake them. Judicial work amounts merely to reviewing and correcting errors in criminal adjudication: anyone discerning in hearing cases can undertake it. But when speaking out on affairs of government is added, one must rectify the ruler’s mind above and correct the officials below. The court’s governing order depends on this office for support, and the customs of the realm depend on it for correction. It cannot be compared with the various agencies and their functionaries.
Moreover, it is easy to impeach a minister’s faults, but difficult to attack a ruler’s failings. Beneath a crushing weight [?], what could remain intact? Unless a person has lost his senses, who would not shrink from death? If the ruler of all under Heaven does not select…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其人以任之重其拳以假之員雖具也治
奚益乎若其得人則蕭望之之按延壽嚴
延年之劾霍光王義方之抗奏奸人溫造
之威望稱職是名於漢唐著聲於彈擊為
多仲淹道輔之諫廢郭后呂誨大防之諫
尊濮園唐介之論除四使明道之論沮公
議是名於宋著聲於諫諍為顯而其事勢
之難易人品之優劣又自不言可知矣洪
惟我
===
國家稽古為治建都察院分十三道監察御
史內以振舉
朝綱外以總領諸道倣前代之官而名實不
紊兼前代之任而付托加重體勢加嚴焉
夫簪筆於內天下事皆得言之銜
命於外天下事皆得行之士誠有負抱居是官
能無有以自見哉故百餘年來直躬之臣
後先輩出抗疏論列當陛蘇嚴持斧巡方
山嶽搖動雷霆之威屢加而蹇諤之風未
punctuated:
其人以任之，重其拳以假之，員雖具也，治奚益乎？若其得人，則蕭望之之按延壽，嚴延年之劾霍光，王義方之抗奏奸人，溫造之威望稱職，是名於漢唐、著聲於彈擊為多。仲淹、道輔之諫廢郭后，呂誨、大防之諫尊濮園，唐介之論除四使，明道之論沮公議，是名於宋、著聲於諫諍為顯。而其事勢之難易、人品之優劣，又自不言可知矣。
洪惟我國家稽古為治，建都察院，分十三道監察御史，內以振舉朝綱，外以總領諸道。倣前代之官而名實不紊，兼前代之任而付托加重，體勢加嚴焉。夫簪筆於內，天下事皆得言之；銜命於外，天下事皆得行之。士誠有負抱，居是官，能無有以自見哉？故百餘年來，直躬之臣，後先輩出，抗疏論列，當陛蘇嚴，持斧巡方，山嶽搖動。雷霆之威屢加，而蹇諤之風未
translation_en:
…suitable men to appoint to these posts and grant them substantial authority [?], then, although the positions are filled, what benefit is there to government? When suitable men were obtained, there were Xiao Wangzhi’s investigation of Yanshou, Yan Yannian’s impeachment of Huo Guang, Wang Yifang’s outspoken memorial against a treacherous man, and Wen Zao’s prestige and fitness for office. These men became famous under the Han and Tang, chiefly winning renown for their impeachments. Zhongyan and Daofu remonstrated against deposing Empress Guo; Lü Hui and Lü Dafang remonstrated against conferring honors on the Pu ancestral precinct; Tang Jie protested the appointment of the four commissioners [?]; and Mingdao protested the obstruction of public deliberation. These men became famous under the Song, winning particular distinction for remonstrance. The relative difficulty of their circumstances and the relative excellence of their character are, moreover, evident without further explanation.
We reverently reflect that our dynasty has looked to antiquity in governing, establishing the Censorate and organizing investigating censors into thirteen circuits, internally to uphold the discipline of the court and externally to oversee the various circuits. It has modeled its offices on those of former dynasties, keeping titles and actual functions in proper order; it has combined the responsibilities of former dynasties, making the trust placed in these officials still weightier and their institutional authority still more imposing. Serving at court with writing brushes tucked into their headgear, they may speak on every affair of the realm; bearing imperial commands abroad, they may take action on every affair of the realm. If a scholar truly possesses aspirations and abilities, can he hold this office without finding some means to demonstrate them? Thus, for more than a hundred years, ministers of upright conduct have emerged in succession. They submit forthright memorials setting out their criticisms, standing at the throne steps in solemn dignity [?]; bearing the axe of authority as they inspect the regions, they make mountains tremble. Though thunderous imperial wrath has repeatedly fallen upon them, their spirit of outspoken remonstrance has not yet…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
褒貶斥之行相繼而清勁之烈愈奮得人
之盛度越前代遠矣執事猶以舉職之難
為憂而求所謂兩全盡善之術愚也不在
其位惡足與議此雖然亦嘗得之聞見而
思所以處之矣大抵振舉
朝綱則諫諍乃其職也顧今之言者務竭其
能危言激論以為忠發隱摘細以為直則
非事君之體矣默者務全其身事關社稷
而不卹患切生民而不念則失守官之義
===
矣夫然則默固非矣而言者亦豈皆是乎
先正有言事君者必誠意交孚而後可以
有為又曰凡進言於君者須從容委曲庶
幾其言易入故職諫諍者積誠以先之竭
忠以發之審事幾之利害揆治體之重輕
鑒太易納約自牖之義服孔子勿欺而犯
之戒當言而言務從容以開導當默而默
不矯訐以干名則諫行言聽
國體以全物議以息
punctuated:
褒，貶斥之行相繼，而清勁之烈愈奮。得人之盛，度越前代遠矣。執事猶以舉職之難為憂，而求所謂兩全盡善之術。愚也不在其位，惡足與議此？雖然，亦嘗得之聞見，而思所以處之矣。
大抵振舉朝綱，則諫諍乃其職也。顧今之言者，務竭其能，危言激論以為忠，發隱摘細以為直，則非事君之體矣。默者務全其身，事關社稷而不卹，患切生民而不念，則失守官之義矣。夫然，則默固非矣，而言者亦豈皆是乎？先正有言：「事君者必誠意交孚，而後可以有為。」又曰：「凡進言於君者，須從容委曲，庶幾其言易入。」故職諫諍者，積誠以先之，竭忠以發之，審事幾之利害，揆治體之重輕，鑒《太易》納約自牖之義，服孔子勿欺而犯之戒。當言而言，務從容以開導；當默而默，不矯訐以干名。則諫行言聽，國體以全，物議以息。
translation_en:
…[?]. Dismissals and expulsions followed one another, yet the ardor of these upright and resolute men grew ever stronger. The abundance of worthy men obtained far surpassed that of earlier dynasties. You nevertheless remain concerned about the difficulty of fulfilling your duties and seek what is called a method of satisfying both demands and attaining complete excellence. I, in my ignorance, do not occupy such an office: how could I presume to discuss this? Even so, I have learned something through hearing and observation and have considered how to handle it.
Broadly speaking, when it comes to upholding the governing order of the court, remonstrance is the duty of this office. Yet those who speak out today strive to display their abilities to the utmost. They take bold words and impassioned arguments for loyalty, and exposing hidden matters and picking out minor faults for uprightness. This is not the proper manner of serving a ruler. Those who remain silent strive to protect themselves: they show no concern for affairs affecting the altars of soil and grain, and give no thought to troubles pressing upon the people. They thus forsake the obligation to discharge their office. If this is so, silence is certainly wrong; but can those who speak out all be right?
A worthy predecessor said: “Those who serve a ruler must first establish mutual trust through sincerity of purpose; only then can they accomplish anything.” He also said: “Whenever one offers advice to the ruler, one must proceed calmly and tactfully, so that one’s words may more readily be accepted.” Thus those charged with remonstrance should first cultivate sincerity and then speak with the utmost loyalty. They should examine the benefits and dangers at the first signs of developments and weigh the relative importance of matters within the overall order of government. They should take as their guide the meaning of “presenting simple offerings through the window” in the Great Changes [?], and observe Confucius’s admonition: “Do not deceive him, but confront him.” When speech is called for, they should speak, striving calmly to enlighten and guide; when silence is called for, they should remain silent, without ostentatious denunciations intended to win a reputation. Then their remonstrances will be acted upon and their words heeded, the dignity of the state will be preserved, and public criticism will subside…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷尊嚴儼然太阿之出匣矣在內之職寧
有不舉者乎統領諸道則糾察乃其職也
顧今之嚴者或過于苛急其弊使人無所
容無以全渾厚之治體寬者或流于縱弛
其弊使人無所忌難以立精明之治功夫
然則縱固失矣而苛者亦豈為得乎先正
有言責人者必求吾之所能行又曰治道
去太甚察察非善政故任糾察者公以處
之恕以行之觀民情之向背廉吏治之臧
===
否明大體而畧細故扶君子而抑小人善
有當勸不見遺於疏遠過有當懲不見沮
於貴近則已正物正嚴而不峻寬而不弛
縉紳畏憚凜然嚴霜之在望矣在外之職
寧有不盡者乎夫御史所以舉其職者如
此若事有所必爭人有所必去勢不能以
兩全精不能以曲盡則與其為不言之仗
馬孰若為朝陽之鳴鳳與其沽鸞凰之美
名孰若取鷹鸇之勁力瞬至于是則死生
punctuated: 朝廷尊嚴，儼然太阿之出匣矣。在內之職，寧有不舉者乎？統領諸道，則糾察乃其職也。顧今之嚴者，或過于苛急，其弊使人無所容，無以全渾厚之治體；寬者，或流于縱弛，其弊使人無所忌，難以立精明之治功。夫然則縱固失矣，而苛者亦豈為得乎？先正有言：「責人者必求吾之所能行。」又曰：「治道去太甚，察察非善政。」故任糾察者，公以處之，恕以行之，觀民情之向背，廉吏治之臧否，明大體而畧細故，扶君子而抑小人。善有當勸，不見遺於疏遠；過有當懲，不見沮於貴近。則已正物正，嚴而不峻，寬而不弛，縉紳畏憚，凜然嚴霜之在望矣。在外之職，寧有不盡者乎？夫御史所以舉其職者如此。若事有所必爭，人有所必去，勢不能以兩全，精不能以曲盡，則與其為不言之仗馬，孰若為朝陽之鳴鳳？與其沽鸞凰之美名，孰若取鷹鸇之勁力？瞬至于是，則死生
translation_en:
…The court’s dignity and authority will be as awe-inspiring as the sword Tai’a drawn from its scabbard. How could any duty within the capital then go unfulfilled? In overseeing the various circuits, investigation and impeachment are their responsibilities. Yet those who exercise severity today sometimes go too far in harshness and urgency. The resulting harm leaves people no room to maneuver and prevents the preservation of a generous and tolerant framework of government. Those who exercise leniency sometimes lapse into lax indulgence. The resulting harm leaves people without anything to fear and makes it difficult to achieve the results of discerning and effective government. Thus, indulgence is certainly a fault, but how could harshness be right either?
An earlier worthy said: “In holding others to account, one must demand what one can oneself carry out.” He also said: “The way of governing rejects excess; prying scrutiny is not good government.” Thus, those charged with investigation and impeachment should approach their duties impartially and carry them out with forbearance. They should observe what wins or loses the people’s allegiance, investigate the merits and faults of officials’ administration, understand the larger principles while passing over minor matters, support gentlemen, and restrain petty men. When good conduct deserves encouragement, those distant from power must not be overlooked; when wrongdoing deserves punishment, those of high rank and close connections must not be allowed to obstruct it. Then, being upright themselves, they will set others right, showing severity without harshness and leniency without laxity. The officials will stand in awe, as though a bitter frost were before their eyes. How could any duty outside the capital then fail to be fully discharged?
Such is the way in which censors fulfill their duties. If there are matters over which they must contend, or people whom they must remove, and circumstances make it impossible to preserve both sides, while their energies cannot encompass every detail [?], then rather than be a silent horse in the ceremonial guard, would it not be better to be a phoenix calling toward the morning sun? Rather than seek the fine reputation of the luan and phoenix, would it not be better to possess the force of hawks and falcons? At such a juncture [?], life and death…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
禍福懸置之度外矣又安用別求所以處
之之術哉愚也蹈出位之咎以復明問然
則達之所施即窮之所養究古人已然之
迹備今日將然之用亦學者分內事耳如
有用我者執此以往
第四問
張子渭
同考試官訓導黃　批〔五策皆豐贍而用人一策尤有斷制所謂識時務者竟非徒錄其文他日效用吾〕
===
有望於子矣
考試官教諭羅　批〔援古人之言斷今日之事是非博洽多聞者不能可嘉可嘉〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔議論正大而處置詳密他日〕
從政端不負所學矣
對進賢有道公薦舉是已退不肖有道嚴
考課是已蓋進賢退不肖天下之治忽所
繇係也天下之賢吾不能盡知而賢者人
難於自售則必公薦舉以來之天下之□
punctuated:
禍福懸置之度外矣，又安用別求所以處之之術哉？愚也蹈出位之咎，以復明問。然則達之所施，即窮之所養，究古人已然之迹，備今日將然之用，亦學者分內事耳。如有用我者，執此以往。
第四問
張子渭
同考試官訓導黃，批〔五策皆豐贍，而用人一策尤有斷制，所謂識時務者，竟非徒錄其文。他日效用，吾〕有望於子矣。
考試官教諭羅，批〔援古人之言，斷今日之事，是非博洽多聞者不能。可嘉！可嘉！〕
考試官教諭孫，批〔議論正大，而處置詳密。他日〕從政，端不負所學矣。
對：進賢有道，公薦舉是已；退不肖有道，嚴考課是已。蓋進賢退不肖，天下之治忽所繇係也。天下之賢，吾不能盡知，而賢者人難於自售，則必公薦舉以來之。天下之□
translation_en:
…calamity and good fortune are put entirely out of consideration. Why, then, seek some further technique for dealing with them? In my ignorance, I have incurred the fault of speaking beyond my station in answering your discerning question. Yet what one puts into practice when successful is precisely what one cultivates while obscure. To investigate what the ancients accomplished and prepare for what may be required today is also a scholar’s proper duty. Should anyone employ me, I would proceed on these principles.
Fourth Policy Question
Zhang Ziwei
Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “All five policy essays are ample in substance, but the essay on employing men is especially decisive in its judgments. Here is someone who understands the needs of the times; indeed, we are not selecting him merely for his writing. I have hopes for your future service.”
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “He draws upon the words of the ancients to judge the affairs of today. Only someone of extensive learning and broad knowledge could do this. Admirable! Admirable!”
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “His arguments are upright and broad in scope, and his proposed measures detailed and thorough. When he enters government service, he will surely live up to his learning.”
Answer: There is a way to advance the worthy: impartial recommendation. There is a way to dismiss the unworthy: rigorous evaluation of performance. For the empire’s good government or disorder depends upon advancing the worthy and dismissing the unworthy. I cannot know all the worthy men in the empire, and worthy men find it difficult to promote themselves; thus impartial recommendation is essential to bring them into service. As for the empire’s □ [illegible] …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
肖吾不能盡識而所謂不肖者又巧爲誕
譎以投吾間隙也又必嚴考課以察之聖
人復起不易斯言矣執事以天下大計下
詢承學將謂韋縫之士亦有以天下爲已
任如范希文者乎而愚也非其人也請因
明問所及而畧陳之四門之闢見於虞則
衆賢爲之和朝無方之立著於商則後人
賴之啓迪自漢以來其途益廣如賈誼王
褒之文學則郡守所薦也辛湯段會宗之
===
政事則公府所薦也雋不疑之經義直指
薦之龔勝之高潔執金吾薦之至於房玄
齡爲相而久無所舉則太宗加之詰責王
曾執政而獨少明揚則希文攻其所短是
庶府皆得薦賢而宰相尤其所急也然知
人聖哲所難君子求其在已盡吾心焉雖
不中不遠矣彼呂正獻誤除秩之薦明道
則教其寧受百欺不可怠好賢之心韓持
國怒下吏之謁伊川則譏其不能求人而
punctuated:
肖，吾不能盡識，而所謂不肖者又巧爲誕譎以投吾間隙也，又必嚴考課以察之。聖人復起，不易斯言矣。執事以天下大計下詢承學，將謂韋縫之士亦有以天下爲已任如范希文者乎？而愚也非其人也。請因明問所及而畧陳之。
四門之闢見於虞，則衆賢爲之和朝；無方之立著於商，則後人賴之啓迪。自漢以來，其途益廣。如賈誼、王褒之文學，則郡守所薦也；辛湯、段會宗之政事，則公府所薦也；雋不疑之經義，直指薦之；龔勝之高潔，執金吾薦之。至於房玄齡爲相而久無所舉，則太宗加之詰責；王曾執政而獨少明揚，則希文攻其所短。是庶府皆得薦賢，而宰相尤其所急也。然知人，聖哲所難；君子求其在已，盡吾心焉，雖不中，不遠矣。彼呂正獻誤除秩之薦，明道則教其寧受百欺，不可怠好賢之心；韓持國怒下吏之謁，伊川則譏其不能求人而
translation_en:
…the unworthy, I cannot recognize them all; moreover, those deemed unworthy cleverly employ falsehood and deception to exploit gaps in my vigilance. It is therefore also necessary to make performance evaluations rigorous in order to scrutinize them. Were a sage to arise again, he would not alter these words. You, sir, have condescended to consult us students about the great affairs of the realm. Do you suppose that among scholars in humble dress [?] there are also men who take responsibility for the realm upon themselves, as Fan Xiwen did? In my foolishness, I am no such man. Allow me nevertheless to offer a brief account of the matters addressed in your illuminating question.
The opening of the four gates is recorded of Yu, and through it the assembled worthies brought harmony to the court. Appointment without restriction is recorded of Shang, and later generations drew guidance from it. From the Han onward, the avenues of recommendation grew ever broader. Jia Yi and Wang Bao were recommended by commandery governors for their literary learning; Xin Tang [?] and Duan Huizong were recommended by the offices of the Three Dukes for their administrative abilities. Jun Buyi was recommended by an Investigating Censor for his understanding of the Classics; Gong Sheng was recommended by the Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia for his lofty integrity. When Fang Xuanling served as chief minister but went a long time without recommending anyone, Taizong questioned and reproached him. When Wang Zeng directed the government yet did little to bring worthy men to prominence, Xiwen attacked this shortcoming. Thus all government offices may recommend worthy men, but for chief ministers this is an especially urgent duty. Yet discerning men’s character is difficult even for sages and wise men. The gentleman looks to what lies within his own power: if I devote my whole heart to the task, then even if I miss the mark, I shall not be far from it. When Lü Zhengxian mistakenly recommended someone for appointment [?], Mingdao instructed him that he should sooner be deceived a hundred times than let his desire to welcome worthy men slacken. When Han Chiguo became angry at a subordinate official’s request for an audience, Yichuan reproached him for failing to seek out men and instead …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
使人求己豈不以大臣之當務莫急於此
且其機固有不係於人者乎周官小宰以
六計弊群吏則廉善廉能廉敬廉正廉法
廉辨是也以八柄御群臣則爵祿廢置生
殺予奪是也自漢而下其法益嚴刺史以
六條按郡國所以督責二千石者甚至宇
文周以六條勅守令所以稽察民事者甚
詳至於唐陸贄之教黜陟使以五術察風
俗而八計則聽吏治焉曰戶口豐耗曰墾
===
田盈縮曰賦役薄厚曰案積繁簡曰囚數
盈虛曰奸濫有無曰選舉衆寡曰學校興
廢法無復加矣然法之用也存乎其人任
法任人有不可偏廢者若陽道州爲刺史
郡民知化而以催科政拙書下考何易于
爲縣令三年無囚而以官無異稱書殿績
是奉法者之非其人也而豈法之過乎我
國家之用人也專委吏部大者擬陞小者注
授妙簡端揆之任垂拱責成固無容議矣
punctuated: 使人求己，豈不以大臣之當務莫急於此，且其機固有不係於人者乎？周官小宰以六計弊群吏，則廉善、廉能、廉敬、廉正、廉法、廉辨是也；以八柄御群臣，則爵、祿、廢、置、生、殺、予、奪是也。自漢而下，其法益嚴。刺史以六條按郡國，所以督責二千石者甚至；宇文周以六條勅守令，所以稽察民事者甚詳。至於唐陸贄之教黜陟使，以五術察風俗，而八計則聽吏治焉：曰戶口豐耗，曰墾田盈縮，曰賦役薄厚，曰案積繁簡，曰囚數盈虛，曰奸濫有無，曰選舉衆寡，曰學校興廢。法無復加矣！然法之用也，存乎其人，任法任人，有不可偏廢者。若陽道州爲刺史，郡民知化，而以催科政拙書下考；何易于爲縣令，三年無囚，而以官無異稱書殿績。是奉法者之非其人也，而豈法之過乎？我國家之用人也，專委吏部，大者擬陞，小者注授，妙簡端揆之任，垂拱責成，固無容議矣。
translation_en:
…make others seek him out. Was this not because, among a great minister’s duties, none is more urgent than this—and because some of the means available do not depend upon particular individuals?

In the Offices of Zhou, the Junior Steward judged the officials by six assessments: integrity with goodness, competence, diligence, uprightness, adherence to law, and discernment. The eight means of controlling ministers were rank, emoluments, dismissal, appointment, preservation of life, execution, granting, and deprivation. From the Han onward, these regulations became increasingly strict. Regional Inspectors investigated commanderies and kingdoms under six articles, subjecting officials of the two-thousand-shi rank to exceptionally exacting oversight. The Yuwen Zhou issued six articles of instruction to prefects and county magistrates, providing exceptionally detailed scrutiny of matters affecting the people. In the Tang, Lu Zhi instructed commissioners responsible for demotions and promotions to investigate local customs through five methods and to assess official administration through eight measures: increases or decreases in registered households and population; expansion or contraction of cultivated acreage; lightness or heaviness of taxes and labor services; the extent of accumulated cases; the number of prisoners; the presence or absence of misconduct and abuses; the number of men selected and recommended for office; and the flourishing or decline of schools. Nothing further could be added to these regulations!

Yet the application of regulations depends upon the people administering them. Reliance upon regulations and reliance upon people are both indispensable; neither may be neglected. When Yang Daozhou served as prefect, the commandery’s people responded to his transforming influence, yet he received a low evaluation because he was judged inept at collecting taxes. When He Yiyu served as county magistrate, there were no prisoners for three years, yet his performance was ranked at the bottom because his official service was said to lack distinction. These were cases in which those administering the regulations were unsuitable. How could the fault lie with the regulations?

Our dynasty entrusts the employment of officials exclusively to the Ministry of Personnel: for higher offices it proposes promotions, and for lesser offices it makes appointments. The sovereign carefully selects the person entrusted with the chief minister’s responsibilities, then governs with folded hands, holding him accountable for results. There is surely no room for criticism of this.

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
然天下之大負才抱藝之多豈一人二人
所能周知故行之既久任年勞則有賢愚
同滯之譏循資格則有涇渭混淆之弊
朝廷知其然曩歲納輔臣之議
詔三品以上各舉所知毋循資格蓋以矯積習
之弊也而論者復恐植桃李於多門失人
之弊將有甚焉嗚呼有是哉誠使司銓衡
者公心以端其本明目以達其用廣詢博
訪以求之平心易氣以待之以資格遇常
===
流而不易其法以不次拔異等而必嚴其
選雖仍舊貫可也其或耳目所不逮則各
舉所知之故事參而行之亦可也何必遂
探其弊耶且今之所謂三品以上者皆鄉
相重任豈復有所謂憸人曲士參廁其間
顧因薦舉以為苞苴請托之媒乎是不得
為法之累矣哉
國家之課吏也要諸三載考績有殿最
朝覲有黜陟稽合庶僚之論綜核名實固無
punctuated:
然天下之大，負才抱藝之多，豈一人二人所能周知？故行之既久，任年勞則有賢愚同滯之譏，循資格則有涇渭混淆之弊。朝廷知其然，曩歲納輔臣之議，詔三品以上各舉所知，毋循資格，蓋以矯積習之弊也。而論者復恐植桃李於多門，失人之弊將有甚焉。嗚呼！有是哉？誠使司銓衡者公心以端其本，明目以達其用，廣詢博訪以求之，平心易氣以待之，以資格遇常流而不易其法，以不次拔異等而必嚴其選，雖仍舊貫可也。其或耳目所不逮，則各舉所知之故事參而行之亦可也。何必遂探其弊耶？且今之所謂三品以上者，皆鄉相重任，豈復有所謂憸人曲士參廁其間，顧因薦舉以為苞苴請托之媒乎？是不得為法之累矣哉！
國家之課吏也，要諸三載考績，有殿最；朝覲，有黜陟。稽合庶僚之論，綜核名實，固無
translation_en:
Yet with the empire so vast, and those possessing talent and accomplishments so numerous, how could one or two men know them all thoroughly? Thus, after this system had long been in operation, reliance on years of service drew criticism that the worthy and the foolish alike languished without advancement, while adherence to formal qualifications produced the fault of mingling the clear waters of the Jing with the muddy waters of the Wei. Recognizing this, some years ago the court accepted the proposal of its assisting ministers and decreed that officials of rank three and above should each recommend men they knew, without adhering to formal qualifications. This was intended to correct the defects of entrenched practice. Yet critics again feared that this would plant peach and plum trees at many gates—that is, create clients of numerous patrons—and that the fault of choosing unsuitable men would become still worse. Alas! Can this really be so? If those responsible for personnel selection would establish a sound foundation through impartiality and exercise their functions with clear discernment, seeking men through wide consultation and extensive inquiry, and receiving them with an even mind and a composed disposition; if they would treat ordinary candidates according to formal qualifications without changing the rules, while promoting exceptional men out of the regular sequence but rigorously scrutinizing their selection—then even retaining the old practices would be acceptable. Where their own knowledge did not reach, it would also be acceptable to supplement these practices with the precedent of having each official recommend men he knew. Why must one then seek out its defects? Moreover, those now described as officials of rank three and above all bear the weighty responsibilities of high ministers and chief councillors [?]. Could there really be treacherous men and crooked scholars mingled among them, who would use recommendations as a means of soliciting bribes and favors? Surely this cannot be counted as a fault of the system!
In evaluating officials, the state takes the triennial assessment of merit as its basis, distinguishing the lowest and highest performers; at court audiences, there are dismissals and promotions. By examining and collating the judgments of the assembled officials and comprehensively checking actual performance against professed standing, it certainly leaves no…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遺法矣然四海之廣伏讒慝之巧豈一
言一事所能盡見故法久弊生是非或得
之傳聞愛憎或生於毀譽
朝廷知其然比歲當述職之期
詔自今考績當黜者皆須備陳實跡果有枉抑
聽其自訴蓋深懲偏聽之失也而識者又
恐招反訐之尤姑息之風將自茲始焉嗚
呼豈其然哉誠使典黜陟者存愛惜人才
之志嚴課功覈實之令一人之言未必信
===
也而參諸衆人焉今日之考未足據也而
驗之前日焉又量其所書之人酌其所書
之事出於賢者為可憑出於庸者為未信
雖仍舊規足矣若衆論之未合則人才難
得姑亦存之耳何至一一必求其實邪且
今貪吏罪狀暴露著理官按之猶為摭拾
況考課之舉苟聽其自理孰肯甘伏其辜
乎是反為不肖者之地耳嗟乎天下之人
才天實生之天不能自為進退而付之大
punctuated: 遺法矣。然四海之廣，伏讒慝之巧，豈一言一事所能盡見？故法久弊生，是非或得之傳聞，愛憎或生於毀譽。朝廷知其然，比歲當述職之期，詔自今考績當黜者，皆須備陳實跡，果有枉抑，聽其自訴。蓋深懲偏聽之失也。而識者又恐招反訐之尤，姑息之風將自茲始焉。嗚呼！豈其然哉？誠使典黜陟者存愛惜人才之志，嚴課功覈實之令，一人之言未必信也，而參諸衆人焉；今日之考未足據也，而驗之前日焉。又量其所書之人，酌其所書之事，出於賢者為可憑，出於庸者為未信。雖仍舊規足矣。若衆論之未合，則人才難得，姑亦存之耳，何至一一必求其實邪？且今貪吏罪狀暴露，著理官按之，猶為摭拾；況考課之舉，苟聽其自理，孰肯甘伏其辜乎？是反為不肖者之地耳。嗟乎！天下之人才，天實生之。天不能自為進退，而付之大
translation_en: … no procedures have been omitted. Yet, given the vastness of the realm and the cunning of concealed slander and wickedness, how could a single statement or deed reveal everything? Thus, as regulations remain in force over time, abuses arise: judgments of right and wrong may rest on hearsay, and affection or aversion may arise from disparagement or praise. Recognizing this, in recent years, when officials were due to report on their duties, the court decreed that henceforth, whenever a performance evaluation warranted dismissal, the actual grounds must be fully stated; if an official had indeed been unjustly treated, he was to be allowed to plead his own case. This was intended to guard firmly against the error of hearing only one side. Yet discerning observers also feared that it would invite the further abuse of retaliatory accusations, and that a tendency toward undue indulgence would begin here. Alas! Could this really be so? If those responsible for dismissals and promotions truly cherished men of talent and strictly enforced the requirements to assess achievements and verify the facts, they would not necessarily believe one person’s statement, but would compare it with those of others; they would not regard today’s evaluation as sufficient evidence, but would test it against earlier ones. They would also weigh the persons mentioned in the written reports and consider the matters recorded: reports originating with worthy men could be relied upon, while those originating with mediocre men would remain unproven. Simply retaining the old regulations would suffice. Where opinions did not agree, since talented men are hard to find, one might provisionally retain the official. Why insist on establishing the truth of every single matter? Moreover, even now, when corrupt officials’ crimes are exposed and judicial officials are ordered to investigate them, this is still regarded as picking over faults [?]. How much more so with performance evaluations: if officials were allowed to argue their own cases, who would willingly admit his guilt? This would instead give unworthy men room to maneuver. Alas! It is Heaven that produces the talented men of the realm. Heaven cannot itself promote or dismiss them, and entrusts this to the great …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
君君不能自爲進退而責之大臣使大臣
當薦舉之任秉黜陟之柄者誠得其人則
將擇人以任庶府以任藩憲固是所進皆
賢何有親讐退避之嫌所退皆不肖何有
流言疑似之惑然則君道之急務亦慎擇
其人以居大臣之位焉耳不然則其法屢
變其弊屢生所禁在此所失在彼欲進退
之必協公論不可得也執事以爲何如
第五問　　　　　　　　李盛
===
同考試官訓導黃　批〔與學勸農先王固有定法此　策能發明之而參以時宜真有識之士也〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔策有考據有議論有斷制非　博古通今者不能爲此言也〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔議論出問目外真是策手〕
成周教養之法大備而後世未能舉
當代教養之法益備而得人爲易行夫教養
之法固莫備於成周尤莫備於
punctuated:
君，君不能自爲進退，而責之大臣。使大臣當薦舉之任、秉黜陟之柄者，誠得其人，則將擇人以任庶府，以任藩憲。固是所進皆賢，何有親讐退避之嫌？所退皆不肖，何有流言疑似之惑？然則君道之急務，亦慎擇其人以居大臣之位焉耳。不然，則其法屢變，其弊屢生；所禁在此，所失在彼。欲進退之必協公論，不可得也。執事以爲何如？
第五問，李盛。
同考試官訓導黃，批〔與學勸農，先王固有定法。此策能發明之，而參以時宜，真有識之士也。〕
考試官教諭羅，批〔策有考據，有議論，有斷制，非博古通今者不能爲此言也。〕
考試官教諭孫，批〔議論出問目外，真是策手。〕
成周教養之法大備，而後世未能舉；當代教養之法益備，而得人爲易行。夫教養之法，固莫備於成周，尤莫備於
translation_en:
…the ruler. The ruler cannot himself manage their advancement and dismissal, and so charges the great ministers with this responsibility. If the great ministers entrusted with recommending men and wielding the authority to dismiss and promote are truly the right men, they will select men to serve in the various offices and in provincial administration and surveillance. If all those advanced are worthy, what grounds are there for suspicion concerning relatives or enemies, or withdrawal to avoid such suspicion? If all those dismissed are unworthy, what confusion can arise from rumors and dubious allegations? Thus an urgent task of rulership is simply to choose carefully the men who will occupy the positions of great ministers. Otherwise, however often the regulations change, abuses will repeatedly arise: what is prohibited in one quarter will go wrong in another. It will be impossible to ensure that advancement and dismissal accord with public judgment. What is your view, honored examiner?
Fifth Question. Li Sheng.
Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔For promoting learning [?] and encouraging agriculture, the former kings certainly had established methods. This policy essay elucidates them while taking account of present circumstances. Its author is truly a man of discernment.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔This policy essay offers evidence from the sources, reasoned discussion, and decisive judgments. Only someone versed in antiquity and conversant with the present could make these statements.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion goes beyond the points raised in the question. Truly an accomplished writer of policy essays.〕
The methods of educating and nurturing the people were fully developed under the Zhou, yet later ages were unable to put them into practice. In the present age, these methods are still more complete, and with the right men they are easy to implement. Indeed, no methods of educating and nurturing the people were more complete than those of the Zhou, and still less could any be more complete than those of…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
當代也苟得其人則教養之政以行而隆古
之治可復不得其人則徒法不能以自行
矣尚何望其治之古若哉書曰立政惟人
禮曰為政在人良有以也請因明問以對
夫今之天下即古之天下而其致治之法
亦不外於古之興學勸農也粤稽諸古上
下有庠東西有序農殖嘉穀蒸民乃粒二
者並用虞夏已然之迹卓乎不可尚已逮
至成周教人則有六德以立其本有六行
===
以觀其行有樂語以導其性情有樂舞以
養其血脉考校則自三年以至七年視其
所為謂之小成自七年以至九年因其所
立謂之大成先王之興學至精至備無遺
法也嗣是若漢武帝嘗建學郡國矣然創
置之初諸生或困厄而不自激厲選士或
貲作而無以資貧唐太宗嘗大召名儒矣
然未幾再傳而論堂之庭或壟為園圃助
教之職或躬任犂鋤以至宋太宗之徧立
punctuated:
當代也。苟得其人，則教養之政以行，而隆古之治可復；不得其人，則徒法不能以自行矣，尚何望其治之古若哉？書曰：「立政惟人。」禮曰：「為政在人。」良有以也。請因明問以對。
夫今之天下，即古之天下，而其致治之法，亦不外於古之興學勸農也。粤稽諸古，上下有庠，東西有序，農殖嘉穀，蒸民乃粒。二者並用，虞夏已然之迹，卓乎不可尚已。逮至成周，教人則有六德以立其本，有六行以觀其行，有樂語以導其性情，有樂舞以養其血脉。考校則自三年以至七年，視其所為，謂之小成；自七年以至九年，因其所立，謂之大成。先王之興學，至精至備，無遺法也。嗣是，若漢武帝嘗建學郡國矣，然創置之初，諸生或困厄而不自激厲，選士或貲作而無以資貧。唐太宗嘗大召名儒矣，然未幾再傳，而論堂之庭或壟為園圃，助教之職或躬任犂鋤。以至宋太宗之徧立
translation_en:
…the present age. If the right men are found, policies for educating and nourishing the people will be carried out, and the good government of high antiquity can be restored. Without the right men, laws alone cannot put themselves into effect. How, then, could one hope for government equal to that of antiquity? The Book of Documents says, “Establishing government depends on men.” The Book of Rites says, “The conduct of government rests with men.” These statements indeed have good reason behind them. Allow me to reply to your illuminating question.
The world today is the same world as in antiquity, and the methods for bringing it good government likewise extend no further than the ancient practices of promoting schools and encouraging agriculture. Looking back to antiquity, there were upper and lower xiang schools and eastern and western xu schools; agriculture produced fine grains, and the multitude thereby had grain to eat. Both measures were employed together: the established achievements of the Yu and Xia eras were outstanding and unsurpassed. By the time of the Zhou, instruction employed the six virtues to establish people's foundations and the six forms of conduct to observe their behavior; musical and verbal instruction guided their dispositions and feelings, while music and dance nurtured their blood and vital channels. In examinations, from the third through the seventh year, students were assessed on what they did: this was called “minor attainment.” From the seventh through the ninth year, they were assessed on what they had established: this was called “major attainment.” The former kings' promotion of learning was supremely refined and complete, leaving no method unprovided for.
Thereafter, Emperor Wu of Han did establish schools in the commanderies and kingdoms. Yet when these were first founded, some students were beset by hardship and failed to spur themselves onward; the selection of scholars sometimes depended on wealth [?], with no means of supporting the poor. Emperor Taizong of Tang did summon eminent Confucian scholars in great numbers. Yet before long, after two successions to the throne, the courtyards of lecture halls [?] were sometimes ridged into garden plots, and holders of the post of Instructor sometimes personally wielded plows and hoes. Then, in the Song, Emperor Taizong established throughout the realm…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
學舍真宗之月書歲試其制固有在矣始
則舍法行而郡縣之學有實政終則舍法
廢而郡縣之學爲具文所謂近乎古者少
而不能近者多也成周勸農旣以親稼穡
勸疆理爲家法之相傳復以教土宜勸時
器爲田畯之職任天子所命者農百辟所
重者農朝廷之所嘉惠者農官府之所分
作者農下至州閭里巷婦人女子賤隸小
夫歌詠賛頌無一而不在於農先王之重
===
民至周至密無遺術也自是若漢之多方
勸率可謂勤矣惜夫限民名田之說不行
於時唐之蠲徭給符可謂詳矣惜夫進退
登耗之數不驗於民以至宋以法駕親視
以人畊繪圖其心固有在矣而經界之制
未推於浙右誘耕之說未行於荆襄所謂
復乎古者少而不能復者多也夫興學固
莫備於成周矣循至于今胄監庠序之並
立公卿大夫之皆學其興學也視成周爲
punctuated:
學舍、真宗之月書歲試，其制固有在矣。始則舍法行，而郡縣之學有實政；終則舍法廢，而郡縣之學爲具文。所謂近乎古者少，而不能近者多也。

成周勸農，旣以親稼穡、勸疆理爲家法之相傳，復以教土宜、勸時器爲田畯之職任。天子所命者農，百辟所重者農，朝廷之所嘉惠者農，官府之所分作者農，下至州閭里巷、婦人女子、賤隸小夫，歌詠賛頌，無一而不在於農。先王之重民，至周至密，無遺術也。自是若漢之多方勸率，可謂勤矣，惜夫限民名田之說不行於時；唐之蠲徭給符，可謂詳矣，惜夫進退登耗之數不驗於民。以至宋以法駕親視，以人畊繪圖，其心固有在矣，而經界之制未推於浙右，誘耕之說未行於荆襄。所謂復乎古者少，而不能復者多也。

夫興學固莫備於成周矣。循至于今，胄監庠序之並立，公卿大夫之皆學，其興學也，視成周爲
translation_en:
…school buildings, and Zhenzong’s monthly records and annual examinations: these certainly had their established regulations. At first, when the system of school divisions was implemented, prefectural and county schools were administered effectively; in the end, when that system was abolished, these schools became mere formalities. Thus, few came close to antiquity, while many failed to do so.

In promoting agriculture, Chengzhou made personal participation in sowing and reaping and encouragement of the demarcation of fields part of its transmitted dynastic traditions. It also assigned agricultural officers responsibility for teaching what suited the soil and encouraging timely work and the provision of implements. Agriculture was what the Son of Heaven commanded and what the assembled lords esteemed. Agriculture received the court’s beneficence and was the work apportioned among government offices. Down to neighborhoods and village lanes, women and girls, lowly servants and common men, all their songs and praises concerned agriculture. The former kings’ care for the people was utterly comprehensive and meticulous; no means was neglected. Thereafter, the Han’s many ways of encouraging and guiding agriculture may be called diligent. Regrettably, the proposal to limit the land registered in each person’s name was not implemented at the time. The Tang’s remission of labor service and issuance of certificates may be called detailed. Regrettably, the figures for increases and decreases were not verified among the people [?]. Under the Song, emperors went in person with the imperial procession to inspect farming and had pictures made of people plowing. Their concern was certainly present. Yet the system for surveying and demarcating fields was not extended to Zheyou, and proposals to encourage cultivation were not implemented in Jingxiang. Thus, few restored the practices of antiquity, while many failed to do so.

As for promoting learning, surely no arrangements were more complete than those of Chengzhou. Coming down to the present, the Directorate of Education and local schools stand alongside one another, and dukes, ministers, and high officials all pursue learning. In its promotion of learning, compared with Chengzhou, the present age is …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
益備馬法之備也如此宜其人才𨽻興倍
於往昔可也而或者猶有俊民用微之歎
者蓋以教之者或畧養之者或踈擇之者
不精語之者不詳故耳
聖天子尊居九重所託以養賢成德不在於司
俊造者乎誠使司俊造者重體驗身心之
士擇砥礪名節之人經義治事之兼授諸
家百子之旁通警其輕浮躁進之心培其
光明正大之學則即孟子所謂輔之翼之
又從而振德之矣何患賢俊之不興哉勸
===
農固莫重於成周矣循至于今口分世業
之並行夏歛秋征之有節其勸農也視成
周為益備馬法之盛也如此宜其農事大
修倍於古昔可也而或者猶有黎民阻饑
之歎者蓋以務本者少逐末者多生之者
寡食之者衆故耳
聖天子統御萬方所託以仁民皆勸不在牧任
守令者乎誠使任守令者勸相以時而賦
punctuated:
益備馬。法之備也如此，宜其人才𨽻興，倍於往昔可也。而或者猶有俊民用微之歎者，蓋以教之者或畧，養之者或踈，擇之者不精，語之者不詳故耳。聖天子尊居九重，所託以養賢成德，不在於司俊造者乎？誠使司俊造者重體驗身心之士，擇砥礪名節之人，經義治事之兼授，諸家百子之旁通，警其輕浮躁進之心，培其光明正大之學，則即孟子所謂輔之翼之，又從而振德之矣。何患賢俊之不興哉？

勸農固莫重於成周矣。循至于今，口分世業之並行，夏歛秋征之有節，其勸農也視成周為益備馬。法之盛也如此，宜其農事大修，倍於古昔可也。而或者猶有黎民阻饑之歎者，蓋以務本者少，逐末者多，生之者寡，食之者衆故耳。聖天子統御萬方，所託以仁民皆勸，不在牧任守令者乎？誠使任守令者勸相以時，而賦
translation_en:
…still more comprehensive [?]. With institutions so fully developed, talented men ought surely to arise in succession [?], twice as numerous as in former times. Yet some still lament that outstanding men are little employed. This is simply because their instruction may be cursory, their nurture negligent, their selection insufficiently discriminating, and the guidance given them insufficiently thorough. The sagely Son of Heaven dwells exalted within the ninefold palace. Are not those charged with overseeing promising scholars the very men entrusted with nurturing the worthy and perfecting their virtue? If those overseeing promising scholars truly valued men who put learning into practice in mind and body, selected men who tempered their integrity and reputation, taught both the meaning of the Classics and the conduct of affairs, and encouraged broad familiarity with the various schools and the Hundred Masters; if they warned scholars against frivolity, rashness, and eagerness for advancement, and cultivated in them learning that was upright and honorable—then this would be precisely what Mencius meant by assisting and supporting them, and further rousing them to virtue. What need would there be to fear that worthy and outstanding men would not arise?

Surely no age placed greater weight on encouraging agriculture than the Zhou. Coming down to the present, with both individual land allotments and hereditary holdings in operation, and summer and autumn tax collections duly regulated, the encouragement of agriculture is still more comprehensive than under the Zhou [?]. With institutions so flourishing, agricultural affairs ought surely to be thoroughly attended to, twice as well as in antiquity. Yet some still lament that the common people suffer hunger. This is simply because few pursue the fundamental occupation of agriculture, while many pursue secondary occupations; those who produce are few, while those who consume are many. The sagely Son of Heaven governs the myriad regions. Are not the prefects and magistrates charged with tending the people the very men entrusted with treating them humanely and encouraging them all [?]? If those serving as prefects and magistrates truly encouraged and assisted them at the proper seasons, and the taxes …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
稅以平優恤其財而愛養其力游市井者
繩以互知丁業之法適四方者科以荒蕪
田土之條則即孟子所謂老者衣帛食肉
黎民不饑不寒矣何患農事之不舉哉是
則興學也勸農也二者咸在於得人焉愚
也固非蹏通知遠之才亦不敢為泥古近
俗之論第以濟時之術舍得人無可言者
故曰待其人而後行敢誦以為治天下者
之龜鑑
punctuated: 稅以平，優恤其財而愛養其力。游市井者，繩以互知丁業之法；適四方者，科以荒蕪田土之條。則即孟子所謂「老者衣帛食肉，黎民不饑不寒」矣，何患農事之不舉哉？是則興學也，勸農也，二者咸在於得人焉。愚也固非蹏通知遠之才，亦不敢為泥古近俗之論。第以濟時之術，舍得人無可言者，故曰：「待其人而後行。」敢誦以為治天下者之龜鑑。
translation_en: …levy taxes equitably, generously safeguard the people's resources, and cherish and nurture their strength. Those who idle in the marketplaces should be restrained by the law requiring mutual knowledge of adult males’ occupations [?]; those who travel about the country should be dealt with under the provisions concerning uncultivated farmland. Then what Mengzi described would indeed come to pass: “The elderly wear silk and eat meat, and the common people suffer neither hunger nor cold.” Why then worry that agriculture will not flourish? Thus, both promoting learning and encouraging agriculture depend upon finding the right people. I, in my ignorance, certainly lack the talent for comprehensive understanding [?] and far-reaching insight, nor do I dare offer arguments that cling to antiquity or accommodate prevailing customs. Yet as for methods of meeting the needs of the age, there is nothing to discuss apart from finding the right people. Hence the saying: “Only when the right person is found can it be put into practice.” I venture to recite this as a guide and mirror for those who govern all under Heaven.

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄後序
陝自曩歲八郡告饑凋敝之
餘百凡所須爲塲屋經費者
率多苟簡乃弘治乙卯秋八
月再當試士之期先是巡按
監察御史李　翰博詢于衆知
其事因仍且久當改觀易聽
遂謀于巡撫右副都御史張
敷華相與協志修舉幣聘之
儀校文之室餼廩之供與夫
鹿鳴之宴饗勸駕之條格視
昔有加焉試錄成當併所取
士之姓名與文之合程式者
獻于
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄後序

陝自曩歲八郡告饑凋敝之餘，百凡所須爲塲屋經費者，率多苟簡。乃弘治乙卯秋八月，再當試士之期。先是，巡按監察御史李　翰博詢于衆，知其事因仍且久，當改觀易聽，遂謀于巡撫右副都御史張敷華，相與協志修舉。幣聘之儀、校文之室、餼廩之供，與夫鹿鳴之宴饗、勸駕之條格，視昔有加焉。試錄成，當併所取士之姓名與文之合程式者，獻于
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In Shaanxi, following the devastation left by famine reported in its eight prefectures in earlier years, provision for all the expenses of the examination establishment had generally been makeshift and scanty. In the eighth month of autumn in the yimao year of the Hongzhi reign [1495], the time to examine candidates came round again. Before this, Li Han, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector, had consulted widely and learned that these arrangements had persisted unchanged for a long time and ought to be renewed so as to make a different impression. He therefore consulted Zhang Fuhua, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and together they resolved to put matters in order. The ceremonial gifts for inviting examiners, the rooms for evaluating essays, the provisions of food and grain, the Deer-Cry Banquet, and the regulations for encouraging successful candidates to proceed to the capital were all improved over former practice. Once the examination record was completed, it was to be submitted, together with the names of the successful candidates and their essays conforming to the prescribed standards, to …

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
朝夫惟古賓興賢能之書作選
舉之道無容議矣洎乎文氣
漸薄士風不振乃有爽時態
之流宕考材能於端實斯二
者歸之何哉亦存乎操是柄
者之正與否爾且士嘗學於
家絺章繪句聲動郡邑自以
===
為足擅一方蓋一世也至有
體性輕薄文詞浮豔如唐之
張昌齡輩或不免於誘毀後
生故當時王師旦謂其將變
朝廷風雅而黜之呂渭欲結
附裴延齡知其手操文詞非
工固擢之登第士君子咸鄙
punctuated: 朝。夫惟古賓興賢能之書作，選舉之道無容議矣。洎乎文氣漸薄，士風不振，乃有爽時態之流宕，考材能於端實。斯二者歸之何哉？亦存乎操是柄者之正與否爾。且士嘗學於家，絺章繪句，聲動郡邑，自以為足擅一方，蓋一世也。至有體性輕薄，文詞浮豔，如唐之張昌齡輩，或不免於誘毀後生，故當時王師旦謂其將變朝廷風雅而黜之。呂渭欲結附裴延齡，知其手操文詞非工，固擢之登第，士君子咸鄙
translation_en: …to the court. When the ancient writings concerning the ceremonial reception and recommendation of the worthy and capable were composed, the principles of selecting men for office admitted of no dispute. Later, as literary vigor gradually weakened and the ethos of scholars languished, there arose the tasks of correcting the wayward tendencies of the age [?] and assessing talent by uprightness and substance. On what do these two depend? Simply on whether those who wield this authority are upright. Scholars study at home, embroidering their compositions and embellishing their phrases, until their reputations resound through prefectures and counties. They consider themselves capable of dominating a region and eclipsing an entire age. Yet some are frivolous in disposition and florid and superficial in expression, like Zhang Changling of the Tang. Such men may inevitably mislead and corrupt younger students. Thus Wang Shidan at that time said that Zhang would alter the court’s cultivated literary standards and rejected him. Lü Wei wished to attach himself to Pei Yanling; although he knew that Pei’s own literary compositions lacked skill, he nevertheless promoted him to a passing place in the examination [?]. Scholars and gentlemen all scorned…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其謬濫夫均之知舉選也一
以執持顯一以詭隨敗正邪
失得之判彰彰如此與爲事
者其亦慎所擇而知夫適從
耶史稱得賢者有賞得不肖
者有罰況今日之事有監臨
有提調有監試相與裁抑浮
===
華藉數倖進不遺餘力暨諸
執事又無匪人廁乎其間〔聰〕
輩以徵聘而來濫司文柄其
所責與所負亦云厚且重矣
顧敢自爲汚賤以得罪於名
教得罪於清議哉嗚呼精鑒
徇公正之發也不敢不勉矯
punctuated: 其謬濫。夫均之知舉選也，一以執持顯，一以詭隨敗，正邪失得之判，彰彰如此。與爲事者，其亦慎所擇而知夫適從耶？史稱得賢者有賞，得不肖者有罰。況今日之事，有監臨，有提調，有監試，相與裁抑浮華、藉數倖進，不遺餘力。暨諸執事，又無匪人廁乎其間。〔聰〕輩以徵聘而來，濫司文柄，其所責與所負，亦云厚且重矣。顧敢自爲汚賤，以得罪於名教，得罪於清議哉？嗚呼！精鑒徇公，正之發也，不敢不勉。矯
translation_en: …their erroneous and indiscriminate selections. Both alike were responsible for selecting examination candidates, yet one gained distinction through steadfast adherence to principle, while the other came to disgrace through unscrupulous compliance. So manifest is the distinction between uprightness and perversity, failure and success. Should not those participating in this undertaking likewise choose their course carefully and know what to follow? The histories state that those who obtain worthy men are rewarded, while those who obtain unworthy men are punished. Moreover, in the present undertaking there are a Supervising Official, Proctors, and examination monitors, who together spare no effort to curb superficial ornamentation and advancement through reliance on luck [?]. Nor is there any unworthy person mingled among the various functionaries. We, 〔Cong〕 and his colleagues, have come by invitation and undeservedly hold authority over literary selection. What is demanded of us and the responsibilities we bear are indeed substantial and weighty. Would we dare debase ourselves and thereby offend against moral teaching and the judgment of honorable opinion? Alas! Discerning appraisal and devotion to the public interest are expressions of uprightness; we dare not fail to strive for them. To correct…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
枉過當正之病也〔聰〕豈忍為
是哉其或為文者詞類理通
而亦在所必取焉斯又崇本
抑末之論非正之病也諸士
子能以正自處而復自慶焉
則知評品之高下與收錄之
先後一皆出於正而非所謂
===
棄實務華雜良以苦者矣即
是而往亦惟畢趨以正上為
所事下為所學使人皆望之
為端士為正人斯則曰科目
之出也有光無忝其毋苟焉
頽墮以重取邪媚之誚哉〔聰〕
不佞用是自勵而復以勵諸
punctuated: 枉過當，正之病也。〔聰〕豈忍為是哉？其或為文者詞類理通，而亦在所必取焉。斯又崇本抑末之論，非正之病也。諸士子能以正自處，而復自慶焉，則知評品之高下與收錄之先後，一皆出於正，而非所謂棄實務華、雜良以苦者矣。即是而往，亦惟畢趨以正，上為所事，下為所學，使人皆望之為端士、為正人，斯則曰科目之出也，有光無忝。其毋苟焉頽墮，以重取邪媚之誚哉！〔聰〕不佞，用是自勵，而復以勵諸
translation_en: …to go too far in correcting what is crooked is a failing in the pursuit of rectitude. Could I, Cong, bear to do this? If a candidate’s composition has fitting diction [?] and coherent reasoning, it too must be selected. This is a judgment that honors essentials and restrains embellishment, not a failing of rectitude. If you candidates can conduct yourselves with rectitude and take satisfaction in doing so, you will understand that the higher and lower rankings of your work, and the order in which you are selected, all proceed from rectitude. They are not instances of what is called abandoning substance to pursue ornament, or mixing the good with the bitter [?]. From this point onward, you should all advance with rectitude: toward those above, in your service; and in your own pursuits, in your learning. Let everyone regard you as upright scholars and righteous men. Then it may be said that your emergence through the examinations brings honor and no disgrace. Do not carelessly lapse into degeneration and thereby incur further reproaches for perversity and flattery! Unworthy though I, Cong, am, I use this to encourage myself, and also to encourage all…

title: 弘治八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
人
直隷鳳陽府鳳陽縣儒學教
諭羅聰謹序
punctuated:
人。

直隷鳳陽府鳳陽縣儒學教諭羅聰謹序。
translation_en:
…the others.

Preface respectfully written by Luo Cong, Instructor in the Confucian School of Fengyang County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region.
